chapters.title: Chapter 1 | The Three Wives
paragraphs: "Life is never made unbearable by circumstances, but only by lack of meaning and purpose."—Victor Frankl
[10,000x Investment Multiplier System]
[Requirement for System Integration: Minimum of 0.1 Affection (1/3)]
The evening sky glowed orange as the sun set. Its rays reflecting off the roof of a small bungalow building in an urban neighborhood.
In front of this building was a limousine and five people.
"Here is the house key deed, the key, and ten thousand dollars. The Ashford family will no longer have anything to do with you as of this moment. Do we understand each other?"
Dexter opened his mouth.
The butler didn’t wait for Dexter to speak, nor did he offer a parting glance. He simply stepped back into the black limousine, leaving nothing behind but the faint smell of premium exhaust.
Dexter stood there, staring blankly.
He looked down at the key in his palm. It was faded and worn, as though a hundred people had used it.
Dexter was born into the wealthy Ashford Family by a slave mother who died during childbirth.
To make matters worse he was born with an F-rank mana affinity which he would never become a hero and was destined to be a nobody.
He was hidden away and abandoned, treated like a slave in the Ashford family where he was supposed to be royalty until today when he signed the condition for his freedom from the family.
He didn’t know what it was but he was desperate to escape the family’s influence, so he signed the contract.
But how could he have known that the condition was getting married to the three famous cripples in the entire city.
He turned around and behind him were three women dressed in white wedding gowns.
When he married them thirty minutes ago, it still felt like he was living in a nightmare.
Escaping one family only to be involved with three other families?
’Did I jump from frying pan straight into fire?’
He hated this situation. He had been helpless all his life. Finally escaping only to be tied down once more... it was hell.
He turned around to finally take a look at his three ’wives’.
The lady who was in a wheelchair, in the middle of the others is called: Mira Calloway.
From the wealthy Calloway family, she’s permanently paralyzed from the neck down.
She has flaming red hair, crimson eyes and a tiny mole beneath her nose.
She looked like the picture perfect painting of a sun goddess as she sat there with a blank expression on her face.
Three Years ago, she was called the Crimson-Valkyrie.
Born with an S rank mana affinity and an A rank Crimson Flame-heart talent. She battled monsters through countless dungeons, becoming one of the youngest B-rank heroes in the city.
However, tragedy struck when three families joined forces to explore a wild S-Rank dungeon under the Ashford Family’s jurisdiction.
Due to a grave miscalculation by the Ashford family, the dungeon was classified as S-Rank when it was, in fact, an SSS-Rank dungeon.
The expedition ended in catastrophe, leaving her crippled and her meridians completely shattered.
To Mira’s left, stood a tall, slender woman with dark hair cascading past her shoulders.
The second wife, Lyra Vance of the influential Vance family, was once a prodigy in her own right.
Born with B-rank mana affinity, she had awakened an A-rank ability known asShadow Worldand rose rapidly to become one of the fastest individuals to attain C-rank hero status.
Since it was a joint family expendition, it included her family. She had been present in the dungeon alongside Mira when the incident occurred.
Since then, her vocal cords had been ruptured and her eardrums destroyed, leaving her unable to speak or hear.
In her prime, she was known asAurelyx: The Shadow Saintess.
It was rumored that she has two faces. She could be smiling at you and then next second wish to kill you just like that.
At this moment, she currently stared at Dexter with an unreadable expression, just as one would stare at a strange painting.
To Mira’s right stood the third lady, Selene Frost from the prestigious Frost noble family.
Born with an A rank mana affinity and S rank Eternal Ice Winter ability. She became an A-rank hero and also was in the same SSS rank dungeon when she became blind and chronically ill.
Selene’s skin was pale, almost translucent and she wore a thin cardigan over her wedding dress that did nothing to hide how much she was shaking.
’They must be freezing.’
That was his first thought.
He walked to the rusty iron gate, fumbled with the key and finally got it open. He went to the women.
He moved behind Mira’s wheelchair first. Then he reached out and gently caught the hem of Selene’s sleeve.
"It’s cold out here. Let’s head inside."
His voice came out rougher than he intended. He cleared his throat.
The moment his fingers touched her sleeve, Selene flinched as she yanked her arm away.
Dexter’s jaw tightened and he frowned.
’What the hell?’
He could feel the evening cold through his suit which meant she had to be freezing.

Out of the corner of his eye, he saw a curtain twitch in the house across the street which meant that the neighbors were already watching. If someone took a photo of them and posted it on the internet, this place would turn into something else.
’Since I can’t touch her, maybe Lyra would.’ He said in thought and then brought out his phone, opened the notes app, and typed in a big font.
[Take her hand. Let’s head inside. It’s too cold.]
He held the screen in front of Lyra’s face. Her dark eyes focused on the text, then looked up at Dexter.
She stared at him for what seemed to be a minute and then slowly nodded.
Then she stepped toward Selene. Her hand hovered near Selene’s arm for a moment. Selene seemed to have noticed it. She brought her arm forward and Lyra’s fingers settled around Selene’s wrist.
Dexter sighed and then gripped the handles of Mira’s wheelchair.
He wheeled her up the path, while Lyra guided Selene behind them in silence. The front door got stuck, making Dexter put his shoulder into it to open.
The smell of dust and old wood escaped the house. He tapped at the wall with his fingers and found the switch, lighting up the entire house.
The bungalow was small but structurally sound. A previous owner had left behind three sagging sofas, an old television, a wooden dining table with five chairs, and a shelf of dusty paperbacks.
The wallpaper was also peeling at the corners.
He left the three women in the living room and went to check the bedrooms.
It was two rooms. One was slightly larger than the other. Each contained a bed frame with a bed, a nightstand, and a window with iron bars and dirty curtains.
’Two rooms and four people.’ Dexter thought.
It would be logical for two people to sleep in one room but nothing about this night was logical.
’I can only use the small room, merge the two beds together for the three of them to sleep.’
The beds were large enough for two people to sleep on so two combined beds should be more than enough to house the three women.
He found some extra blankets in a closet that smelled like mothballs and spread them out to cover the gap between the mattresses.
His own room was now empty. Luckily, he found a hand-crank air mattress in a storage closet, pumped it up, and threw a blanket over it.
’This should be alright for tonight. Tomorrow, I will make other arrangements.’Dexter muttered to himself.
When he returned to the living room, the girls were exactly where he’d left them. No one had moved an inch just like barbie dolls.
"I set up the beds," he said, leaning against the doorframe. "You guys can head in and get some sleep."
Dexter was about to leave when he saw no one answered him
He frowned in frustration ’Why aren’t they—’
And then it hit him.
One couldn’t hear him, the other couldn’t see and the third couldn’t move.
Dexter gritted his teeth and without a word, he turned and walked back to his bedroom.

He needed five minutes. Just five minutes to sit in silence and not think about the fact that he had been disowned, married to three strangers, and left in a crumbling house with ten thousand dollars and no plan.
About an hour later, he came back.
He had washed his face with cold water from the kitchen tap and had calmed down a bit.
He typed a new note on his phone:
[Let’s go to bed. Bring Selene with you. I’ll handle Mira.]
He held it in front of Lyra. Her eyes focused once more. Then she looked at him, making Dexter a bit uncomfortable, but she eventually nodded her head.
She went to Selene and guided her toward the bedroom, one hand on Selene’s elbow, the other on the small of her back.
Dexter walked over to Mira.
She was still in her wheelchair. She hadn’t looked at him once since the wedding.
He crouched in front of her. "I’m going to pick you up now."
Her eyes trembled but she said nothing as Dexter lifted her up.
She was really light as though she hadn’t been eating.
He carried her through the doorway and into the bedroom. Lyra had already settled Selene on the far side of the bed. He lowered Mira on the empty side of the bed.
Mira’s head suddenly turned as she looked directly at him for the first ever. Her ember eyes were extremely dull.
"You know," she suddenly spoke. Her voice was like a thousand sirens singing "It’s our wedding night."
Dexter was at first stunned. Not because of her voice but because one of them was finally willing to speak to him.
He glanced at her and said nothing
She continued. "You can do whatever you want to me. I’m completely paralyzed and won’t be able to resist you at all.
Dexter was stunned.
’I still don’t know whether to be happy now that I’ve finally escaped my family or be sad that I’ve gotten entangled with three.’
Right now, he was feeling something but it was definitely not lust.
But now that she mentioned it...
Dexter felt heat crawl up the back of his neck. But he kept his face still.
Mira of course she saw it. Her lips curled into a cold smile.
"Or... did you want all three of us? Don’t worry. One is blind and won’t know if you’re small. And the other can see everything, but she can’t tell a soul." Mira chuckled coldly.
"Convenient, isn’t it?"
On the far side of the bed, Selene reached into her sleeve to pull out a slightly bruised apple and began to munch on it gently.
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"Save the reverse psychology," he said flatly. "I wasn’t planning on anything. Even if I wanted to do it, it certainly won’t be with someone who can’t move."
The room suddenly went silent and a flicker of amusement flashed in Mira’s eyes.
Selene had stopped chewing as she froze there on the bed.
Dexter exhaled through his nose and rubbed the back of his neck.
"I don’t plan to do anything to you guys either. I like my women taking the initiative so just... sleep. We’ll figure the rest out tomorrow."
He didn’t wait for a response. He hit the light switch, plunging the room into darkness and closed the door.
Dexter rested in his room massaging his forehead
’How the hell am I supposed to take care of three people when I can barely take care of myself?’

chapters.title: Chapter 2 | Life With Three Ex-Heroines
paragraphs: "When fate hands you three lemons, make three cups of lemonade." — Dale Carnegie
Dexter tried sleeping but it refused to claim him just like his father...
Eventually, he ended up cultivating through the night. The Starlight Meditation Technique extracts mana from the sun and the stars to increases one’s cultivation level.

Hero levels are graded: Awakened Hero also called Meta Heroes (1 to 12), Super Hero (1 to 12), Ultra Hero (1 to 12), Transcendent (Initial, Mid, Advance, Peak), Supreme (Initial, Mid, Advance, Peak), and Legend.
But Dexter possesses the lowest mana affinity: F rank, even comparable to an ordinary human. Absorbing mana to him is like trying to catch a fish with greasy hands, mana slips away.
But the meditation itself had another benefit, it clears one’s mind. By the time it was morning, he felt relaxed, calm and refreshed.
He stood up and stretched.
"Pop!"
His spine popped, then he went to the bathroom.
The hot water thankfully worked. He turned the tap and let it run until steam curled up from the basin, fogging the mirror.
He brushed, showered quickly, dressed in a grey t-shirt and dark joggers then padded to the kitchen on bare feet.
The kitchen was small and outdated, but functional. He opened the cupboards, found rice, a few eggs, some dried mushrooms, and a bottle of soy sauce.
Then he remembered the wedding gift boxes still out in the entrance. Luckily they had a gate.
He dragged them into the kitchen and started unpacking.
Most of it was useless jewelry, he found practical items though: bags of dried grains, canned soups, instant noodles, tea, and a small container of brown sugar.
He cooked. Rice porridge with dried mushrooms and soft-boiled egg on the side.
While it simmered, he set the small dining table. Four bowls, four spoons, four cups of hot tea.
Then he went to the master bedroom.
The door was open and Mira was already in her wheelchair, parked near the window, staring at nothing.
Her hair was tangled around her face, and her wedding dress was wrinkled.
Selene was still in bed, lying on her back, her eyes open and fixed on the ceiling, looking like she hadn’t moved all night.
Lyra was sitting upright at the edge of the mattress, with her hands folded neatly in her lap.
Dexter typed on his phone and held it out to Lyra:
[Breakfast is ready. Can you help Selene to the table?]
Lyra read the message. But instead of nodding, she hesitated. She raised one hand and pointed a slender finger at her own mouth.
Dexter blinked in confusion. "What?"
She pointed again.
"Oh! Sorry!"
They hadn’t brushed their teeth, washed their faces or bathed yet.
He pressed his lips together and typed:
[Hold on. Two minutes.]

Going back to the gift boxes and dug through them. Toothbrushes—still in packaging. Toothpaste. Two bars of soap. A bottle of lotion. A comb. He gathered everything up, carried it to the bedroom, and set it on the nightstand.
He unpackaged an electric toothbrush, applied toothpaste, and held it out to Lyra. She took it. Their fingers briefly brushed and it was ice cold making Dexter raise an eyebrow.
Gave Selene another and then turned to Mira.
"Open your mouth."
Mira’s eyes narrowed. "Excuse me?"
"Open. Your mouth."
"You can’t just—"
Mid sentence, Dexter slid the toothbrush between her teeth and flicked it on.
Mira’s eyes went wide, then narrowed into a glare so sharp it could have cut diamond. She sat there with indignation as toothpaste foam was gathering at the corner of her lips.
Dexter felt happy for shutting her up and grinned.
He held up a small basin. "Spit."
She spat hard, making a bit of foam splash and land on his wrist.
"I thought you might prefer your women to swallow," Mira said with disdain. "Guess I was wrong."
Dexter was stunned. ’This girl is crazier than I thought!’He shook his head and brought a bottle of water to her mouth.
"Rinse."
She smirked but opened her mouth to drink the water and rinsed then spat it out.
He took the toiletries to the bathroom, washed his hands, and came back. He stood in front of her wheelchair and asked.
"Do you need help with the restroom, or do you want to bathe first?"
Mira didn’t look at him. She stared at the wall beside her. "I’m paralyzed, in case you hadn’t noticed. Or do you see a pair of working legs I don’t know about?"
Dexter chuckled. "Will tell Lyra to assist you."
Dexter was about to leave when he heard a small voice. "D-don’t."
Dexter stopped dead in his tracks and frowned.
’What does she mean by ’don’t?’ Does she actually want me to do it myself? Hell no.’
She had practically called him a pervert last night, if he did this, he would be a true pervert in her eyes.
He was about to reject but as he saw her sitting unmoving, face down and looking all sad.
’Ah! Fuck me!’
He cursed in his mind and inhaled sharply, unlocked Mira’s wheelchair and pushed her through the hallway.
The bathroom was small with a toilet, a sink, and an old cast-iron bathtub with clawed feet. He’d scrubbed it earlier that morning while the water was heating.
"Toilet or bathtub first?"
She replied in a quiet voice. "Toilet,"

She was still wearing the wedding dress. Dexter knelt in front of her, wrapped one arm around her waist, and lifted. Her body pressed against his chest and it was warm. He could feel breasts and even count her ribs through the cloth.
Dexter’s expression didn’t change and with his free hand, he found the zipper at the back of her dress and pulled it down.
Underneath, she wore a plain sports bra and cotton briefs. Her skin was pale, milky and ungodly smooth.
"Do you like what you see?" Her voice cracked slightly.
Dexter scoffed. "I’ve seen thousands of beautiful women on Cornhub. What makes you think yours is special?"
"Y-you!"
Mira’s face flushed red in anger but Dexter suddenly removed her panties and placed her securely on the toilet so she wouldn’t fall.
"I’m going to step out now just call me when you’re done."
He pulled the door halfway shut and left to pick up underwear and a dress for her. He saw a flowery gown and smiled. "Perfect."
About fifteen minutes later, Mira spoke in a quiet voice. "I’m done."
Dexter entered. He wouldn’t let his gaze linger anywhere it shouldn’t and pressed the button on the smart toilet. The water hissed and Mira stared strangely at it but she said nothing.
When she was clean, Dexter lifted her again and suddenly unclasped her sports bra, keeping his gaze fixed firmly on the tile above her head, and gently lowered her into the warm water.

He washed her hands first, her arms, her shoulders and her legs, lathering shampoo into her scalp, rinsing it with a cup. She sat in the tub with her eyes closed, her face turned away, her ears burning red.
He lifted her out, wrapped her in a towel, and patted her dry. Then he picked up the flowery sundress he’d found in her luggage.
"I hate this dress," Mira said. Her voice was tight.
Dexter smirked. "I know. That’s why I picked it."
Mira instantly glared daggers at him. But she couldn’t stop him and could only watch as he put it on her.
He helped her back into the wheelchair and pushed her to the kitchen table.
Meanwhile, Lyra had successfully helped Selene wash up in the other bathroom, and the two of them were already seated.
Dexter ladled the hot porridge into four bowls.
Lyra gently took Selene’s hand, guiding her fingers to the handle of the spoon until Selene was able to eat on her own.
Mira took a small bite, chewed slowly, and looked up. "It doesn’t actually taste half bad."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "Was that... a compliment?"
"Don’t push your luck." She retorted drily and went back to eating.
They ate in silence but it was too late when Dexter realized Lyra had consumed more than four people’s worth of porridge.
’How’s this possible? Her body is so thin. Where did all that food go?’
He was stunned.
Lyra noticed him staring and she glanced with her causal expression. But a flush crept up her neck. She was embarrassed but didn’t want to show.
’That was supposed to be our lunch.’
He shook his head, and grabbed his phone, typing.
[It was supposed to be lunch but it’s alright. I will cook more now.]
He held the screen out to her. She read it and looked up at him then hesitantly nodded.
After breakfast, Dexter cleared the table and started washing dishes.
"The great heir of the Ashford family, washing dishes." Mira’s voice sounded out as she mocked.

Dexter rinsed a bowl and set it on the rack. "I’m sure you and your family were quite shocked when you realized I was the one you married and not the legitimate heir. Can’t believe the three great families got scammed. Haha."
Mira eyes twitched and she was suddenly speechless.

Of course Dexter knew the families had been scammed. According to the contract, the three families were promised marriage to the first born of Ashford family, but ended up getting scammed as the bastard son is the first born.
The three families thought it would be easy to form ties with the Ashford family, not knowing it was a trap all along.
Suddenly, a sharp gasp sounded out.

Dexter turned around, Selene was trembling violently on the sofa. The temperature in the room started dropping fast as frost spread across the floorboards, climbing the walls, creeping across the coffee table.
’I read in the file that she’s chronically ill. I didn’t expect it to be this bad.’
’Fuck! Where did I place the medicine her family dropped?’
He panicked and he ran to the hallway where they’d stacked the medical supplies. Quickly unlocked a box with two syringes in it. He took one.

The air around Selene was so cold his fingers went numb the moment he crossed into the frost radius. Ice crystals formed on his eyelashes but he pushed through it, bent down and quickly stabbed the syringe into her.
Nothing happened at first, then the frost stopped spreading as the ice finally cooled.
Dexter grabbed every blanket he could find and wrapped them around her as the tremor slowly faded.
From the doorway, he saw Mira and Lyra.
However, neither of them spoke.
Selene drifted into an exhausted sleep. Her face was ghost-pale, her lips still faintly blue.
A few hours after the morning crises, Dexter was lost in thought.
And went to the kitchen, the porridge was gone, the eggs were finished and the dried grains nearly gone. With Lyra’s appetite, they’d burn through what little remained by dinner.
He found Mira in the living room and crouched in front of her wheelchair.
"I need to go to the market. I’ll be back within an hour. Don’t open the door for anyone."
Mira raised an eyebrow. "Yes, master. Shall I have dinner ready when you return, master?"
"Very funny. Don’t open the door."
He told Lyra the same thing via text, made sure Selene was still sleeping comfortably, and left.
The corner store was three blocks away. Dexter kept his head down as he moved. He needed rice, vegetables, cooking oil, salt, maybe some meat if it was available.
The shopkeeper stared at him for a while.
"You’re quite popular but I can’t seem to remember where I know you from."
The man’s eyes lit up. "Yeah! From the news. They mention you as the hidden son of the Ashford family."
Then the old man frowned and glanced at Dexter. "Come to think of it, it wasn’t hidden son, it was bastard son. You’re the one that scammed three girls to get married to you hmm?"
The shopkeeper sneered in disgust.
’How did the news get out so fast?’
Dexter frowned and simply greeted the shopkeeper.
"Morning," Dexter said. He started gathering items. "Rice. Two kilos. Cabbage. Carrots. Cooking oil. Salt. And whatever pork you have that’s—"
"We’re low on pork," the shopkeeper interrupted, leaning against the counter. "Prices have gone up."
Dexter paused, his eyes narrowed at the shopkeeper.
"How much?"
"10 dollars per pound."
Dexter’s face turned black.
"That’s twice the market price,"
"Inflation." The shopkeeper shrugged. "Take it or leave it."

Dexter paid. He counted out the bills, placed them on the counter, and left immediately with his things.

Dexter hesitated but eventually entered the store. He purchased Selene’s suppression medicine which cost 500 dollars per syringe, he bought a week’s worth.

sentences.text: "When fate hands you three lemons, make three cups of lemonade." — Dale Carnegie
Dexter tried sleeping but it refused to claim him just like his father...
Eventually, he ended up cultivating through the night.
The Starlight Meditation Technique extracts mana from the sun and the stars to increases one’s cultivation level.

Hero levels are graded: Awakened Hero also called Meta Heroes (1 to 12), Super Hero (1 to 12), Ultra Hero (1 to 12), Transcendent (Initial, Mid, Advance, Peak), Supreme (Initial, Mid, Advance, Peak), and Legend.
But Dexter possesses the lowest mana affinity: F rank, even comparable to an ordinary human.
Absorbing mana to him is like trying to catch a fish with greasy hands, mana slips away.
But the meditation itself had another benefit, it clears one’s mind.
By the time it was morning, he felt relaxed, calm and refreshed.
He stood up and stretched.
"Pop!"
His spine popped, then he went to the bathroom.
The hot water thankfully worked.
He turned the tap and let it run until steam curled up from the basin, fogging the mirror.
He brushed, showered quickly, dressed in a grey t-shirt and dark joggers then padded to the kitchen on bare feet.
The kitchen was small and outdated, but functional.
He opened the cupboards, found rice, a few eggs, some dried mushrooms, and a bottle of soy sauce.
Then he remembered the wedding gift boxes still out in the entrance.
Luckily they had a gate.
He dragged them into the kitchen and started unpacking.
Most of it was useless jewelry, he found practical items though: bags of dried grains, canned soups, instant noodles, tea, and a small container of brown sugar.
He cooked.
Rice porridge with dried mushrooms and soft-boiled egg on the side.
While it simmered, he set the small dining table.
Four bowls, four spoons, four cups of hot tea.
Then he went to the master bedroom.
The door was open and Mira was already in her wheelchair, parked near the window, staring at nothing.
Her hair was tangled around her face, and her wedding dress was wrinkled.
Selene was still in bed, lying on her back, her eyes open and fixed on the ceiling, looking like she hadn’t moved all night.
Lyra was sitting upright at the edge of the mattress, with her hands folded neatly in her lap.
Dexter typed on his phone and held it out to Lyra:

Can you help Selene to the table?]
Lyra read the message.
But instead of nodding, she hesitated.
She raised one hand and pointed a slender finger at her own mouth.
Dexter blinked in confusion.
"What?"
She pointed again.
"Oh!
Sorry!"
They hadn’t brushed their teeth, washed their faces or bathed yet.
He pressed his lips together and typed:
[Hold on.
Two minutes.]

Toothbrushes—still in packaging.
Toothpaste.
Two bars of soap.
A bottle of lotion.
A comb.
He gathered everything up, carried it to the bedroom, and set it on the nightstand.
He unpackaged an electric toothbrush, applied toothpaste, and held it out to Lyra.
She took it.
Their fingers briefly brushed and it was ice cold making Dexter raise an eyebrow.
Gave Selene another and then turned to Mira.
"Open your mouth."
Mira’s eyes narrowed.
"Excuse me?"
"Open.
Your mouth."
"You can’t just—"
Mid sentence, Dexter slid the toothbrush between her teeth and flicked it on.
Mira’s eyes went wide, then narrowed into a glare so sharp it could have cut diamond.
She sat there with indignation as toothpaste foam was gathering at the corner of her lips.
Dexter felt happy for shutting her up and grinned.
He held up a small basin.
"Spit."
She spat hard, making a bit of foam splash and land on his wrist.
"I thought you might prefer your women to swallow," Mira said with disdain.
"Guess I was wrong."
Dexter was stunned. ’This girl is crazier than I thought!’He shook his head and brought a bottle of water to her mouth.
"Rinse."
She smirked but opened her mouth to drink the water and rinsed then spat it out.
He took the toiletries to the bathroom, washed his hands, and came back.
He stood in front of her wheelchair and asked.
"Do you need help with the restroom, or do you want to bathe first?"
Mira didn’t look at him.
She stared at the wall beside her.
"I’m paralyzed, in case you hadn’t noticed.
Or do you see a pair of working legs I don’t know about?"
Dexter chuckled.
"Will tell Lyra to assist you."
Dexter was about to leave when he heard a small voice.
"D-don’t."
Dexter stopped dead in his tracks and frowned.
’What does she mean by ’don’t?’ Does she actually want me to do it myself?
Hell no.’
She had practically called him a pervert last night, if he did this, he would be a true pervert in her eyes.
He was about to reject but as he saw her sitting unmoving, face down and looking all sad.
’Ah!
Fuck me!’
He cursed in his mind and inhaled sharply, unlocked Mira’s wheelchair and pushed her through the hallway.
The bathroom was small with a toilet, a sink, and an old cast-iron bathtub with clawed feet.
He’d scrubbed it earlier that morning while the water was heating.
"Toilet or bathtub first?"
She replied in a quiet voice.
"Toilet,"
She was still wearing the wedding dress.
Dexter knelt in front of her, wrapped one arm around her waist, and lifted.
Her body pressed against his chest and it was warm.
He could feel breasts and even count her ribs through the cloth.
Dexter’s expression didn’t change and with his free hand, he found the zipper at the back of her dress and pulled it down.
Underneath, she wore a plain sports bra and cotton briefs.
Her skin was pale, milky and ungodly smooth.
"Do you like what you see?" Her voice cracked slightly.
Dexter scoffed.
"I’ve seen thousands of beautiful women on Cornhub.
What makes you think yours is special?"
"Y-you!"
Mira’s face flushed red in anger but Dexter suddenly removed her panties and placed her securely on the toilet so she wouldn’t fall.
"I’m going to step out now just call me when you’re done."
He pulled the door halfway shut and left to pick up underwear and a dress for her.
He saw a flowery gown and smiled.
"Perfect."

"I’m done."
Dexter entered.
He wouldn’t let his gaze linger anywhere it shouldn’t and pressed the button on the smart toilet.
The water hissed and Mira stared strangely at it but she said nothing.

Her voice was tight.

That’s why I picked it."

chapters.title: Chapter 3 | System Awakening!
paragraphs: "The afterglow of a battle is always sweeter than the victory itself." — Oscar Wilde
Dexter got home within the hour.
When he opened the door, he saw his wives in the living room, Lyra and Mira were staring into space as usual and Selene was still asleep on the old couch.
Their eyes didn’t even move to him when he entered as they remained in their own world.
’Can’t imagine what they must be feeling.’
Afterall, they were previously at the peak of their lives but now, the had all been tossed to a useless person.
Dexter shook his head and calculated how much he had left and it was about 5000 dollars.
At this rate, they’d be broke in two weeks. Maybe less.
He dropped the pen and rubbed his face.
That evening, Dexter sat alone in the small backyard. The sky was dark and the neighborhood hummed with distant sounds of televisions, arguments, a baby crying.
He crossed his legs, closed his eyes, and cultivated.
The meditation technique drew ambient mana into his body but he couldn’t absorb it. Like a bucket fetching water from a well.
His thought began to wander and landed on money. He needed money if he wanted to make it through this month.

He needed a job. But with F-rank ability, no formal combat training, and the stink of the Ashford disgrace, no legitimate guild or company would touch him. The only work available was low-level Dungeon Porters and Scouts.
Even that required a basic hero license. And a hero license required clearing at least one dungeon.
Dexter opened his eyes and stared at the sky. A single star poked through the haze.
’Tomorrow,’ he thought. ’I’ll figure it out tomorrow.’
The next morning, Dexter prepared a simple breakfast, rice porridge again, with pickled vegetables and tea. He was setting the table when three heavy knocks rattled the front gate.
’Are the neighbors finally getting friendly?’
Dexter set down the teapot. He looked at his three wives and spoke.
"Stay here."
He walked out the door and opened the gate.
The moment he opened the door, a huge man burst through the door and entered the gate.
The one in front was a tall dude built like a door with a white beard. He wore a leather jacket.
Seeing him, Dexter felt his mana wave.
’Awakened Hero level 3.’
The others were level 2 and 1.
Behind him, three smaller men fanned out, hands in pockets, trying to look casual.
"Morning," the big man said. His grin widened, revealing his gold tooth.
"Well, well. The bastard prince of the Ashfords. Look at this, boys, this is the closest you can ever get to royalty."
He shoved past Dexter without waiting for an invitation and directly entered the house. The three thugs followed, their boots tracking mud across the living room floor.

"My name’s Kreg," the big man said, scanning the living room like a generational thief. "This territory belongs to us, the Red Fang Crew. Since you’re new here, I’ll explain how things work. You pay us protection fee, monthly and we will protect you from monsters invasions."
Dexter’s expression didn’t change.
’He’s at the Awakened Hero rank level 3 stage. There’s no way I can be his match. surrender is not a sign of defeat. ’
He inhaled and asked. "How much is the protection fee?"
Kreg smiled. "I like smart people a lot."
Then he came before Dexter, a head taller than him as he looked down at Dexter as he grinned. "How about 5,000 dollars for starters."
Dexter’s face changed slightly. "That’s impossible. I don’t have 5,000 dollars to give."
Kreg laughed out loud, his voice booming through the walls.
"Oh, I think you do." He stopped in the middle of the living room. His eyes moved slowly around the room and then landed on the three women.

Mira sat in her wheelchair near the sofa. She met Kreg’s gaze with indifference, as though he were a stain on the wall she couldn’t be bothered to clean. Lyra sat beside Selene, the same indifference while Selene simply stared elsewhere.

"Word is," Kreg said, stepping closer to Dexter, "the Ashfords gave you a nice little parting gift. Ten grand, right? Cash?" He cracked his knuckles. "Protection fee is five thousand. For the first month. After that, we negotiate."
Dexter’s fists clenched hard. ’What to do? That cash is all we have. If I give them, we won’t survive for long but if I don’t, these men might do something worse.
"Take the money and leave," Dexter said, pulling the remaining cash envelope from his pocket. "It’s all I have."
At that moment, Kreg’s men started drifting moving towards the women. One of them licked their lips.
"Boss, these girls are high-quality. Look at them. We could use them for a while, then sell them to some wealthy clients. Nobles pay top credit for."
"Hahaha. You’re right. Even if they’re broken, we could get a massive price for them from some of the underground collectors..."
One of the thugs grabbed Lyra by the jaw, examining her face like checking a dog.
Kreg’s eyes flashed with a sudden, ugly greed as he looked at the three women.
"They would fetch a pretty penny..." Kreg murmured, ignoring Dexter.
A surge of white-hot anger hit Dexter. Usually, he was thoughtful and calculating but right now, his sanity vanished.
Before Kreg could finish his sentence, Dexter moved.
He punched the first thug square in the jaw. Turned, kicked the second in the balls and tackled the third one directly to the ground punching his face in!
He had no formal combat training, but he caught them completely off guard.
But the physical disparity was too wide. Dexter was only a level 1 bronze warrior, the lowest level here is level 2.
Before Dexter could land the third punch, the men recovered faster than he had thought
Two of them grabbed him from behind, wrenching his arms behind his back. The third one stood up and immediately punched him in the ribs.
"Ugh!"
Kreg stepped forward. His gold tooth gleamed.
"That was stupid," he said, and hit Dexter across the face.
The blow sent blood spilling in the air, staining the floor.
Kreg leaned in. "What did you think would happen?"
Dexter looked up at him. Blood trickled from his split lip down his chin. "Take the money and get out."
Kreg sneered and ignored him as he turned toward the women again. "Why would I leave when there are precious cargo to be secured?"
Dexter chuckled. "Do you really think our families will let common thugs touch their daughters without consequences?"
Kreg’s grin faltered but he recovered it quickly. "You’ve all been abandoned. They don’t care about you."

"They don’t care about us," Dexter nodded in agreement. "You’re right. They don’t care about us. However, they care about their reputation. If word gets out that some low-life street thugs laid hands on the daughters of the Frost, Vance, and Calloway families, what do you think would happen? "
"The only way they could save face would be to make an example. Just wiping your entire crew completely won’t be enough to pacify them. Your families won’t be spared either. Even the bastards."
Kreg’s face immediately went pale. He was just a regular thug, nowhere near enough to compete with those massive families.
Suddenly, Kreg drove a fist directly into Dexter’s stomach.
Dexter doubled over as he coughed up blood.
His knees buckled. The men holding him let go, and he dropped to the floor.
Kreg snatched the envelope from Dexter’s pocket.
"Even if I can’t do anything to the girls, I can still do so many things to you."
Kreg muttered and patted Dexter’s face.
"We’ll be back next month. You better have more money by then." He glanced at the women one more time. "Or we’ll find other ways to collect."
"Let’s go."
The thugs laughed and mocked him as they left the house.
Dexter lay on the floor for a long moment. Stars speckled his vision and his ribs ached as he breathed.
The girls stared at him with strange expressions on their faces. But Dexter ignored it as he heard a sound.
[Ding!]
Dexter flinched. He looked around. But nothing nearby made that sound.
Suddenly, golden text materialized in the air before his eyes.
’Could it be?’
’[Requirements have been met.]
[Conditions: Minimum Affection of 0.1 (4/3)]
[Initializing system integration]
’[Integration Complete. Welcome, Host, to the Ten-Thousandfold Investment Multiplier System.]’
Dexter couldn’t believe it. Ever since the incident when he was 9, the system had been a part of his life.
However, the requirement for activating the system was gaining a miniscule 0.1 affection of at least 3 people. For 10 years, he only managed to gain the affection of a single person.
Now that he’s 19, he had completely given up and had completely forgotten about the system. But now, it the requirement was reached? How?
10,000x INVESTMENT MULTIPLIER SYSTEM
[Investment Target(s)]: Mira Calloway (Wife), Lyra Vance (Wife), Selene Frost (Wife), Jasmine Constance (Ex-Girlfriend)
[Name]: Dexter Ashford
[Race]: Human
[Talent]: Not Awakened
[Mana Affinity]: F-Rank (Low Grade)
[Rank]: Awakened Hero/ Meta Hero
[Level]: 1
[Attributes]
Strength: 25 (Basic human stat is 10)
Agility: 25 (Basic human stat is 10)
Physique: 25 (Basic human stat is 10)
Mana: 20 (Basic human stat is 10)
[Meditation Technique]
★ Starlight Meditation Technique [Mortal Grade]
• Increases Mana Absorption
• Improves Mana Recovery
• Accelerates Cultivation Speed
[System Notice]
’[System Note: Invest in your wives. Protect them. Provide for them. Every act of investment; financial, emotional, physical, strategic will yield returns multiplied by your current tier.
Higher investment significance yields greater rewards.
Requirement to upgrade to 100x Multiplier: Kill 10 beings.]

’[System Note: Rewards given directly by the system cannot be reused to trigger a direct investment return. For example, using the 50,000 credits to directly hand over as cash will not trigger a return. However, if you use those credits to purchase items, food, medicine, or assets for your wives, the investment return will trigger.]’
’[Scanning investment...]’

’[Investment detected: Subject sacrificed 100% of liquid assets (5,000 Credits) to neutralize an immediate physical threat to all three investment targets. Accepted physical violence to create a protective barrier. Prioritized target safety over personal welfare.]
Dexter was still stunned when another set of notifications came in.
’[Analyzing target responses...]’
’[Mira Calloway: Emotional disturbance detected — dormant emotional seed planted.]’
’[Lyra Vance: Physiological response detected — cortisol decrease of 12% — a minuscule sense of madness restored for the first time in 6 months.]’
’[Selene Frost: Core temperature elevation of 0.3°C during protective action — frost generation suppressed voluntarily for 3.2 seconds — longest conscious suppression on record.]’
’[Current Multiplier: 10x — Base Tier]’
’[Calculating Returns...]’
’[Calculation Complete.]’
’[Returns Granted:]’
’1. 50,000 Credits — Direct Financial Return (10x original investment of 5,000 Credits).’
’2. Mana Affinity Upgrade: F-Rank → E-Rank.’
’3. Talent Awakening: Enhanced Hearing (E-Rank) (200-meter radius + sound differentiation).’
’4. Cultivation Boost: 10 Months of compressed mana refinement applied.’
’5. Flame Demon Bloodline (Royal Grade).’
[Do you wish to accept Rewards? Y/N]

"My name’s Kreg," the big man said, scanning the living room like a generational thief.
"This territory belongs to us, the Red Fang Crew.
Since you’re new here, I’ll explain how things work.
You pay us protection fee, monthly and we will protect you from monsters invasions."
Dexter’s expression didn’t change.
’He’s at the Awakened Hero rank level 3 stage.
There’s no way I can be his match. surrender is not a sign of defeat. ’
He inhaled and asked.
"How much is the protection fee?"
Kreg smiled.
"I like smart people a lot."
Then he came before Dexter, a head taller than him as he looked down at Dexter as he grinned.
"How about 5,000 dollars for starters."
Dexter’s face changed slightly.
"That’s impossible.
I don’t have 5,000 dollars to give."
Kreg laughed out loud, his voice booming through the walls.
"Oh, I think you do." He stopped in the middle of the living room.
His eyes moved slowly around the room and then landed on the three women.
Mira sat in her wheelchair near the sofa.
She met Kreg’s gaze with indifference, as though he were a stain on the wall she couldn’t be bothered to clean.
Lyra sat beside Selene, the same indifference while Selene simply stared elsewhere.
"Word is," Kreg said, stepping closer to Dexter, "the Ashfords gave you a nice little parting gift.
Ten grand, right?
Cash?" He cracked his knuckles.
"Protection fee is five thousand.
For the first month.
After that, we negotiate."
Dexter’s fists clenched hard. ’What to do?
That cash is all we have.
If I give them, we won’t survive for long but if I don’t, these men might do something worse.
"Take the money and leave," Dexter said, pulling the remaining cash envelope from his pocket.
"It’s all I have."
At that moment, Kreg’s men started drifting moving towards the women.
One of them licked their lips.
"Boss, these girls are high-quality.
Look at them.
We could use them for a while, then sell them to some wealthy clients.
Nobles pay top credit for."
"Hahaha.
You’re right.
Even if they’re broken, we could get a massive price for them from some of the underground collectors..."
One of the thugs grabbed Lyra by the jaw, examining her face like checking a dog.
Kreg’s eyes flashed with a sudden, ugly greed as he looked at the three women.
"They would fetch a pretty penny..." Kreg murmured, ignoring Dexter.
A surge of white-hot anger hit Dexter.
Usually, he was thoughtful and calculating but right now, his sanity vanished.
Before Kreg could finish his sentence, Dexter moved.
He punched the first thug square in the jaw.
Turned, kicked the second in the balls and tackled the third one directly to the ground punching his face in!
He had no formal combat training, but he caught them completely off guard.
But the physical disparity was too wide.
Dexter was only a level 1 bronze warrior, the lowest level here is level 2.
Before Dexter could land the third punch, the men recovered faster than he had thought
Two of them grabbed him from behind, wrenching his arms behind his back.
The third one stood up and immediately punched him in the ribs.
"Ugh!"
Kreg stepped forward.
His gold tooth gleamed.
"That was stupid," he said, and hit Dexter across the face.
The blow sent blood spilling in the air, staining the floor.
Kreg leaned in.
"What did you think would happen?"
Dexter looked up at him.
Blood trickled from his split lip down his chin.
"Take the money and get out."
Kreg sneered and ignored him as he turned toward the women again.
"Why would I leave when there are precious cargo to be secured?"
Dexter chuckled.
"Do you really think our families will let common thugs touch their daughters without consequences?"
Kreg’s grin faltered but he recovered it quickly.
"You’ve all been abandoned.
They don’t care about you."
"They don’t care about us," Dexter nodded in agreement.
"You’re right.
They don’t care about us.
However, they care about their reputation.
If word gets out that some low-life street thugs laid hands on the daughters of the Frost, Vance, and Calloway families, what do you think would happen?
"The only way they could save face would be to make an example.
Just wiping your entire crew completely won’t be enough to pacify them.
Your families won’t be spared either.
Even the bastards."
Kreg’s face immediately went pale.
He was just a regular thug, nowhere near enough to compete with those massive families.
Suddenly, Kreg drove a fist directly into Dexter’s stomach.
Dexter doubled over as he coughed up blood.
His knees buckled.
The men holding him let go, and he dropped to the floor.
Kreg snatched the envelope from Dexter’s pocket.
"Even if I can’t do anything to the girls, I can still do so many things to you."
Kreg muttered and patted Dexter’s face.
"We’ll be back next month.
You better have more money by then." He glanced at the women one more time.
"Or we’ll find other ways to collect."
"Let’s go."
The thugs laughed and mocked him as they left the house.
Dexter lay on the floor for a long moment.
Stars speckled his vision and his ribs ached as he breathed.
The girls stared at him with strange expressions on their faces.
But Dexter ignored it as he heard a sound.
[Ding!]
Dexter flinched.
He looked around.
But nothing nearby made that sound.
Suddenly, golden text materialized in the air before his eyes.
’Could it be?’
’[Requirements have been met.]
[Conditions: Minimum Affection of 0.1 (4/3)]
[Initializing system integration]
[Progress: 0%...
[Progress: 75%...
’[Integration Complete.
Welcome, Host, to the Ten-Thousandfold Investment Multiplier System.]’
Dexter couldn’t believe it.
Ever since the incident when he was 9, the system had been a part of his life.
However, the requirement for activating the system was gaining a miniscule 0.1 affection of at least 3 people.
For 10 years, he only managed to gain the affection of a single person.
Now that he’s 19, he had completely given up and had completely forgotten about the system.
But now, it the requirement was reached?
How?
10,000x INVESTMENT MULTIPLIER SYSTEM
[Investment Target(s)]: Mira Calloway (Wife), Lyra Vance (Wife), Selene Frost (Wife), Jasmine Constance (Ex-Girlfriend)
[Name]: Dexter Ashford
[Race]: Human
[Talent]: Not Awakened
[Mana Affinity]: F-Rank (Low Grade)
[Rank]: Awakened Hero/ Meta Hero
[Level]: 1
[Attributes]
Strength: 25 (Basic human stat is 10)
Agility: 25 (Basic human stat is 10)
Physique: 25 (Basic human stat is 10)
Mana: 20 (Basic human stat is 10)
[Meditation Technique]
★ Starlight Meditation Technique [Mortal Grade]
• Increases Mana Absorption
• Improves Mana Recovery
• Accelerates Cultivation Speed
[System Notice]
’[System Note: Invest in your wives.
Protect them.
Provide for them.
Every act of investment; financial, emotional, physical, strategic will yield returns multiplied by your current tier.
Higher investment significance yields greater rewards.
Requirement to upgrade to 100x Multiplier: Kill 10 beings.]
’[System Note: Rewards given directly by the system cannot be reused to trigger a direct investment return.
For example, using the 50,000 credits to directly hand over as cash will not trigger a return.
However, if you use those credits to purchase items, food, medicine, or assets for your wives, the investment return will trigger.]’
’[Scanning investment...]’
’[Investment detected: Subject sacrificed 100% of liquid assets (5,000 Credits) to neutralize an immediate physical threat to all three investment targets.
Accepted physical violence to create a protective barrier.
Prioritized target safety over personal welfare.]
Dexter was still stunned when another set of notifications came in.
’[Analyzing target responses...]’
’[Mira Calloway: Emotional disturbance detected — dormant emotional seed planted.]’
’[Lyra Vance: Physiological response detected — cortisol decrease of 12% — a minuscule sense of madness restored for the first time in 6 months.]’
’[Selene Frost: Core temperature elevation of 0.3°C during protective action — frost generation suppressed voluntarily for 3.2 seconds — longest conscious suppression on record.]’
’[Current Multiplier: 10x — Base Tier]’
’[Calculating Returns...]’
’[Calculation Complete.]’
’[Returns Granted:]’
50,000 Credits — Direct Financial Return (10x original investment of 5,000 Credits).’
Mana Affinity Upgrade: F-Rank → E-Rank.’
Talent Awakening: Enhanced Hearing (E-Rank) (200-meter radius + sound differentiation).’
Cultivation Boost: 10 Months of compressed mana refinement applied.’
Flame Demon Bloodline (Royal Grade).’
[Do you wish to accept Rewards?
Y/N]

chapters.title: Chapter 4 | Returns: 50,000 Dollars, Talent Awakening &Flame Demon Bloodline
paragraphs: "You gave them everything," Mira’s flat voice snapped Dexter out of his shock.
He managed to steady himself, leaning his shoulder against the peeling wallpaper of the entryway.
He wiped his mouth with the back of his hand, leaving a dark red smear across his face as he chuckled bitterly.
"I had no other choice."
Mira’s lips curled into a sharp sneer. "You’re too weak."
Dexter’s eyes flashed with irritation and he retorted. "Pot calling the kettle black."
As though she hadn’t heard him, Mira closed her eyes and sunk into her own world.
As for Lyra, she stared at him for a brief moment as though trying to figure something out but then she eventually gave up, turned to stare at the window.
On the other side of the sofa, Selene hadn’t moved a single bit even when the thugs came, it was as though she hadn’t heard anything and remained closed off in her world.
Dexter sighed but didn’t say anything else. While he felt they were disappointed in him, his system told him something else.
Dragging his feet, Dexter made it to his small bedroom and sat cross legged on his airbed.
He closed his eyes and breathed out. The glowing golden text of the system still hovered in his vision, bright and steady in the darkness of his closed eyelids.
[Returns Granted:]
1. 50,000 Credits — Direct Financial Return (10x original investment of 5,000 Credits).
2. Mana Affinity Upgrade: F-Rank → E-Rank.
3. Talent Awakening: Enhanced Hearing (E-Rank) (200-meter radius + sound differentiation).
4. Cultivation Boost: 10 Months of compressed mana refinement applied.
5. Flame Demon Bloodline (Royal Grade).
[Do you wish to accept Rewards? Y/N]
Dexter stared at the prompt with shivering hands.
He had spent his entire life believing he would always be a useless, unawakened nobody. But these girls he thought were burdens turned out to be the ones to unlock his system.
"Accept."
In that instant, a notification rang out on his phone. Dexter took out his Samsung Galaxy 9 out and saw 50,000 dollars had been deposited into his bank account.
"It’s actually real!?"
Just as this shock rippled through his mind, an invisible shockwave exploded outward from his chest.
"BOOM!"
A violent shockwaves exploded from his body as something within him snapped like massive chains clacking and unlocking all at once.
Dexter’s eyes flew wide open as his body trembled uncontrollably as his heart began to beat with a force of a piston in an engine.
"Thump! Thump! Thump!"
The force of the heartbeat was so strong that it sent vibrations down the bed and to the ground.
Every single pore on his skin suddenly opened wide and in that instant, started to suck in the mana in the surroundings like a vacuum.
Gradually, an invisible vortex of mana formed around him as his body rapidly absorbed it like sponge.
The raw energy rushed toward him like a vacuum as mana forced its way into his skin, filling his empty, dry meridians with mana. Just like a dress well finally producing water.
"Kra-ka-ka!"

His bones popped, from his toes to his skull. It sounded like a string of firecrackers going off inside his skeleton. Dexter gasped as his muscles began to tighten, and hardening under the sudden influx of raw power.
He felt so light and incredible free. All his life he hadn’t notice just how sluggish and heavy he was.
`[System Notification: Cultivation boost applied. 10 months of compressed mana refinement integrated.]`
`[Host has leveled up: Awakened Hero Level 1 → Level 2!]`
The pain in his ribs began to fade, replaced by a warm, solid pressure.
But before the happiness could fully settle, a sudden, terrifying heat bloomed erupted from within him.
The heat grew rapidly and it felt like someone had poured liquid fire directly down his throat.
His eyes widened as steam began to rise from his skin. The blood inside his veins felt as though it had turned into molten lava, bubbling and boiling as it rushed through his newly widened pathways.
’Damn it! What is this!?’ Dexter thought, his teeth slamming shut.
He bit his tongue hard, as he fought not to scream in pain.

Sweat poured from his forehead, sizzling as it dripped onto the dusty wood. The pain was intense, consuming every single nerve ending in his body. It felt as though his very cells were being torn apart and rebuilt.
Deep within his chest, his cellular structure was changing. A dark, powerful demonic essence was weaved itself into his human DNA, fusing with his flesh and bone.
Then, just as the heat came, it vanished back and faded into nothing.
A soft wave of hot air burst outward from his body, carrying a faint scent of sulfur and ash, before dissipating into the corners of the room.
"Huff!" "Huff!" "Huff!"
Dexter slumped on his bed and panted heavily. But his eyes shine brilliantly.
[System Notification: Flame Demon Bloodline (Royal Grade) successfully integrated.]
[All basic attributes have received a permanent +2 bonus.]
[Bloodline Profile: Flame Demon Bloodline]
Grade: Royal
Passive Skills:
1) Fire Resistance (20%): Host can resist 20% of all damage caused by fire-based attacks.
2) Flame Will: Host can conjure and control basic flames using personal mana.
Active Skills:
1) Scorching Fury: Increase overall physical strength by 50% for 3 minutes.
- Cost: 20 Mana per minute
- Cooldown: 24 hours
2) Flame Demon Transformation: Awaken the innate bloodline to temporarily gain 1% of a true Flame Demon’s power. (Locked: Requires higher cultivation level).
3) Flame Slash: Release a destructive blade strike composed of concentrated fire. 200% attack power and speed.
- Cost: 20 Mana per strike
- Cooldown: 24 hours
4) Flame Burst Step: Gain a sudden burst of speed, increasing movement velocity by 300% for 1 second.
- Cost: 30 Mana per burst
- Cooldown: 10 seconds

chapters.title: Chapter 5 | Flame Demon Bloodline
paragraphs: Dexter slowly raised his hands, staring at them in the dim light of the bedroom. They still looked the same but he felt raw power coursing through his muscles.
He hadn’t expected the bloodline to be so powerful.
With his current strength and skills, he felt like he could handle the three thugs and even Kreg easily now.
He was currently a Tier 2 Awakened Hero and while it wasn’t impressive, to a man who had spent his life at the bottom, this was like learning to breathe after years of drowning.
The moment his mana affinity shifted from F-rank to E-rank, he felt his meridians changing slowly widening by a few millimeters at most.
At this rate, mana easily flowed through his system with less resistance.
[Talent: Enhanced Hearing]
Type: Auxiliary
Rank: E
Ability: Hear sounds within a 200-meter radius under normal conditions, and up to 1 kilometer in a straight line when focusing. Permits sound differentiation and heart-rate tracking.
Nor just increasing his affinity, gaining bloodline and strength, he also awakened talent too!
Dexter closed his eyes, focusing his mind on his ears.

Instantly, the world exploded with sound. He could hear the slow, rhythmic dripping of the leaky faucet in the kitchen three walls away. He could hear the rustle of dry leaves scraping against the backyard fence.
More than that, he could hear the distinct, separate heartbeats of the three women in the living room.
Mira’s heartbeat was slow, steady, and heavy, carrying a deep, sluggish rhythm. Lyra’s heart beat with a rapid, light pattern, like a bird trapped in a cage. And Selene’s heart was weak and erratic.
Satisfied, Dexter stood up. The movement was incredibly smooth, his joints no longer making sounds. He walked to the bathroom, stripped off his sweat-soaked clothes, and stepped into the shower.

As the hot water washed over him, he looked at his reflection in the small, fogged-up mirror. The purple bruise on his jaw was gone. The sharp, deep pain in his ribs had completely vanished, leaving only a faint red scratch on his side. His body looked more fit, the muscles more defined and tight.
He dried himself off, dressed in a clean black t-shirt and grey joggers, and walked out into the hallway.
Dexter decided to check on the girls if they needed anything.
The moment he entered, Mira, Lyra, and Selene all turned their heads toward the hallway at the exact same instant.
Their eyes locked onto him, their expressions filled with a strange, sudden intensity.
Dexter paused, feeling a bit self-conscious under their combined stare. ’Why are they looking at me like they’ve seen a ghost?’ he thought, blinking.

Lyra’s dark eyes narrowed slightly, her gaze moving from his face down to his shoulders, then to his hands. Even though she could not hear, she was still connected to mana and could feel the sudden, dramatic shift in his presence.
Selene’s head remained tilted toward him, her sightless eyes wide.
The two of them stared for only a 2 seconds before turning their heads away, returning to their quiet states.
But Mira continued to look at him with her crimson eyes.
"Is... something wrong?" Dexter frowned as he asked, clearing his throat.
"You’ve awakened," Mira said. Her voice was quiet, but there was an unusual weight behind it.
As a former Super Hero, even with her meridians blocked, her she could still perceive mana due to her high affinity.
Dexter hesitated for a moment, then gave a slow, honest nod. "Something happened while I was resting. After the fight with Kreg’s men... it felt like a barrier inside me broke."
Mira gazed at him for half a second and gave a simply, quiet hum then closed her eyes and returned to darkness.
Dexter was about to leave but he suddenly thought if something.
He expanded his system interface then focused on Mira’s name under the investment targets, and the screen expanded into a detailed panel of golden text.
[Name]: Mira Calloway
[Relationship]: Wife
[Cultivation]
Former Rank: A-Rank Hero
Former Level: Super Hero (7th Tier)
Current Level: Awakened (4th Tier)
Current Mana: 12% (Sealed)
[Body Condition]
Meridian Damage: 89%
Neck-Down Paralysis
• Paralysis from the neck down
• Chronic nerve pain
• Muscle atrophy
• Core instability
[Mental State]
• Depressed
• Suicidal
• Angry
• Hateful
• In Pain
• Slightly Amused

Dexter felt a sudden, deep ache in his chest as he read the description. A level six out of ten chronic nerve pain, constantly firing through her body while she sat there, unable to move a single finger to soothe it. No wonder her voice was always so bitter and cold.
"I can feel your eyes on me," Mira said suddenly. "See something you like, husband?"
Before Dexter could find a response, a sharp, choked gasp shattered the silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 | Another Episode
paragraphs: Selene Frost, who had been sitting quietly on the far edge of the old sofa, suddenly stiffened.
Her breath hitched in her throat, a soft, wheezing sound escaping her lips. Dexter’s head snapped toward her. He recognized the signs instantly—another icy seizure was beginning.
"Selene!" he called out.

The temperature in the small living room plummeted instantly. The air grew so cold that Dexter’s breath turned into thick, white plumes. Frost began to bloom rapidly across Selene’s pale skin, turning the ends of her dark hair a stark, icy white. Thin, delicate sheets of ice began to crawl across the fabric of the sofa, spreading down the wooden legs and onto the floorboards.
She was sitting right at the very edge of the cushions. As her body began to convulse, her balance wavered. She began to tilt forward, her sightless eyes wide with silent panic.

If she fell, her head would slam directly into the sharp edge of the low wooden coffee table. With her frail, weakened body, such an impact could easily result in a fatal head injury or a fractured skull.
Dexter did not hesitate.
"Flame Burst Step!"

His body moved before his mind could even register the command. 5 points of mana vanished from his core, and a soft, low thud of heat exploded beneath his feet. In an instant, his speed tripled. He blurred across the short distance, his hand reaching out to catch her just as her shoulders cleared the edge of the seat.
He wrapped his arms around her shivering frame, pulling her back against his chest.

The moment his skin made contact with her shoulders, a biting, intense cold surged through his arms. The frost on her cardigan transferred to his sleeves, turning the fabric stiff and white. It felt as though a hundred tiny needles of ice were driving deep into his flesh, trying to freeze the blood in his hands.
But Dexter held on. He gritted his teeth and immediately activated Flame Will.
A burst of heat surged from his hands as he tried to contain the frost but it was like a candle in a hurricane

With his right hand, he reached into his pocket and pulled out one of the emergency syringes he had purchased from the pharmacy earlier. He removed the cap with his teeth, lined up the needle against her shoulder, and pressed the plunger, injecting the warm, thick serum directly into her system.
The seizure lasted for thirty seconds.
To Dexter, it felt like hours.
Gradually, the violent tremors in her limbs began to slow, and the rapid spread of frost on the floorboards halted, the thin layers of ice slowly melting into small pools of water.
When the episode finally passed, Selene slumped forward against his shoulder, completely unconscious. Her skin was still damp and pale, but her breathing had returned to a slow, even rhythm.
Throughout the entire ordeal, neither Lyra nor Mira glanced at their direction. They seemed to have gotten used to Selene’s condition.

Dexter’s gently lifted her, carrying her small, fragile body into the bedroom, and laid her down on the large, combined mattress. He pulled three thick blankets over her, tucking her in tightly to ensure she would stay warm then turned on the radiator.
’The sickness seem to be acting up faster than usual.’
Dexter wiped the remaining frost from his hands, thinking about the time intervals when a clear, familiar sound echoed in his mind.
’Ding!’
[System Notification: Investment detected — Physical protection and medical intervention during an episode.]
[10x Multiplier activated.]
[Target: Selene Frost (Wife)]
[Calculating Returns...]
[Calculation Complete. Returns Granted:]
1. Frost Resistance (Minor): Host can now tolerate low temperatures and ice-based energy attacks 15% more effectively.
2. Frost Sense: Host’s body is now sensitive to the unique mana fluctuations of frost. You can now sense and predict Selene’s seizures 10 to 15 seconds before they physically begin.
Dexter was pleasantly surprised. With this system, maybe he would eventually find a cure for her.
He closed his eyes and accepted the rewards.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 | Food Smith: Novice Peak
paragraphs: The sun slowly came as night fell over the quiet neighborhood.
Inside, the atmosphere was completely different from the cold despair of the previous day.
For the first time in years, Dexter felt a deep, genuine happiness.

He hummed a soft tune as he moved around the kitchen. Earlier, he had searched the internet on his phone, looking for healthy, nourishing recipes that could help restore physical strength and gently soothe damaged meridians.

He had settled on a recipe for a slow-simmered chicken and wild herb broth. He carefully chopped fresh ginger, dry ginseng roots he had found in the family gift boxes, and fresh green onions. He washed a cup of pearl rice he bought earlier, letting it boil slowly in a clay pot until the grains softened and broke down, releasing a thick, comforting aroma then he added sliced mushrooms and soft, shredded meat.
It was a simple meal, but to a body that had been starved of nourishment, it was medicine.
’I wonder what rewards I will get this time.’
Dexter thought happily as he set four bowls and spoons on the wooden dining table. He walked to the living room, where the three girls sat in their usual silence.
" Dinner’s ready," he called out.
No one moved.
’Right. I keet forgetting.’
He pulled out his phone and typed: [Food is ready. Come to the kitchen.]
He held the screen in front of Lyra who read it, nodded. She stood up, her movements were graceful despite her thin frame as she walked to Selene’s side and touched her elbow.
Selene tilted her head, recognizing the touch, and allowed Lyra guide her toward the kitchen.
They’d only been here two days, but they were already learning each other’s rhythms.
Dexter then turned to Mira.
Shes still had her eyes closed. The evening light caught her red hair and made it glow like embers.
He walked behind her wheelchair and gripped the handles.
"I’m taking you to the kitchen."
Mira didn’t respond nor did she open her eyes.
Dexter didn’t mind, he wasn’t looking for response the first place. He unlocked the wheelchair and pushed her through the doorway, and into the kitchen.

The four sat together in the small kitchen. Only the hum of the refrigerator and the clinking of spoons could be heard. Lyra guided Selene’s hand to her spoon, helping her find the bowl and she began to eat on her own.
Dexter sat beside Mira. He picked up her spoon, scooped a small portion of the warm food and blew on it then held the spoon to her lips.

Mira stared at him, her crimson eyes flickering with a mixture of annoyance and reluctance. But the rich, savory smell of the food was too enticing to ignore making her stomach let out a quiet, embarrassing growl.
She opened her mouth, letting him feed her.

The moment the warm porridge touched her tongue, her crimson eyes widened slightly. The savory flavor of the chicken broth, balanced by the earthy sweetness of the ginseng and ginger, seemed to burst across her taste buds.
Moreover, she felt a faint warmth ease the sharp, persistent nerve pain in her neck and shoulders slightly.
Even Lyra and Selene paused when they tasted the food.
Mira swallowed and looked at Dexter. "Did you actually cook this?"
"I did," Dexter said, smiling as he gathered another spoonful. "Is it to your liking?"
"It is acceptable," she replied indifferently, though she quickly opened her mouth for the next bite.
Dexter smiled at her reaction and fed her until her bowl was completely empty. He then finished his own portion and was satisfied as the other two finished their meal.
After dinner, Dexter cleaned the dishes while the women sat in their various spot. Lyra by the window, Selene by the couch and Mira, anywhere Dexter placed her.
He was drying the last bowl when the notification appeared.
[Ding!]

[Investment detected: Subject prepared and provided meal with beneficial mana properties to all three investment targets. Physical nourishment provided. Emotional labor performed (feeding assistance).]
[Current Multiplier: 10x — Base Tier]
[Calculating Returns...]
[Calculation Complete.]
[Returns Granted:]
1.Five Body Nourishing Meals Recipe (Complete Set) (Grade 2)
— A collection of five recipes specifically designed for heroes with damaged meridians. Each meal targets different aspects of physical and energetic recovery.
2.Cultivation Boost: 2 Days of Compressed Mana Refinement Applied.
3.Peak Novice Food-smith
[Do you wish to accept Rewards? Y/N]
Dexter was stunned by the rewards. Just cooking for them casually gave this much rewards. What if he unlocked the 10,000 multiplier system, wouldn’t he become godlike?
’I actually got a graded technique?’
’And it’s actually a cooking type technique!’
’Woah! It actually also made me a Foodsmith

In this world, there are Geneticists who concoct serums that provide special attributes like increasing strength, speed and even advancing cultivation levels. And also, there are those who apply the same techniques to food.

These people are called Food-Smiths! They use special techniques to nourish their food, making it have effects that is beneficial to the body and now, he was at the peak of novice rank without having a single knowledge about being a Foodsmith.
He accepted immediately.
In that moment, mana rushed into his body in a ways and his bones cracked and popped as his strength increased by a bit.
At the same time memories flooded his brain rapidly. Various cooking techniques flooded his mind in a flash and just like that he was a Peak Novice, Food-Smith!
That’s not all, the information about the recipe and also various ingredients needed flooded into his mind like they had been part of his memories.
Five Nourishment Meal:

Meal 1: Meridian-Soothing Broth — A golden liquid made with various ingredients but two main ingredients with two main ingredients Sun-moon fruit, Juiper root Sun-moon fruit and Juniper bark root. Soothes inflamed meridians and promotes gradual repair of minor damage.
Meal 2: Marrow-Fortifying Stew — Thick, hearty stew containing Ground Dragon Bone and Blood Rice. Strengthens the skeletal structure and improves mana circulation through the bones.
Meal 3: Nerve-Calming Congee — A rice porridge infused with Serenity Willow Bark and Moonlight Dew. Reduces chronic nerve pain and calms the nervous system.
Meal 4: Qi-Replenishing Soup — A clear soup made with Starlight Mushroom and Essence Spring Water. Directly replenishes depleted mana reserves and accelerates natural mana regeneration.
Meal 5: Body-Harmonizing Rice Bowl — A balanced meal combining elements of the previous four recipes with additional herbs. Brings the body’s systems into alignment and promotes overall healing.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 | Spoiling The Girls
paragraphs: Dexter’s hands were trembling slightly as he finished drying the bowl.
Half of the ingredients listed in his memories, he hadn’t seen them. And half he recognized but they were to expensive.
He pulled out his phone and began searching for the price of the ingredients.
It took Dexter half an hour to find what he needed.
There was a commercial district nearby called the Merchant Quarter. Most of the shops there are equipment stores, potion suppliers and other stuffs.
Tucked between a weapon smith and a potion brewery was a small shop called "Heaven’s Taste: Cultivation Cuisine Supplies."
Dexter scanned their online catalog and found everything he needed.
Spirit Ginseng: 400 credits per root
Phoenix Feather Root: 300 credits per bundle
Ground Dragon Bone: 500 credits per packet
Serenity Willow Bark: 200 credits per portion
Starlight Mushroom: 350 credits per batch
Moonlight Dew: 250 credits per vial
Essence Spring Water: 150 credits per bottle
Blood Rice: 100 credits per bag
For Meal 1 — the Meridian-Soothing Broth — the daily cost was approximately 1,100 credits for three servings.
For all five meals rotated throughout the week, the daily cost averaged around 2,000 credits.
It was astonishingly expensive. A regular family could eat for a month on what Dexter would spend in a day.
Dexter’s eyes flickered and he wondered if it was going to be worth it spending so much money on food. But he quickly shook the thought of. With the system, he didn’t need to be worried.
Dexter did the math in his head.
If he spent 2,000 credits per day on ingredients, that was 14,000 credits per week. Over a month, that was roughly 56,000 credits.
If he maximized the "significance" of each investment, the returns could far outweigh the costs.
The next morning, Dexter woke up early, showered and dressed in a simple black hoodie and sweatpants, pulling the hood low over his face.
The walk to the Merchant Quarter took forty minutes.
He reached the Merchant Quarter and it was quite less crowdy as people were still preparing for work.
Delivery trucks were unloading crates and the shop owners were setting up displays.
Heaven’s Taste was a narrow storefront with a green awning and a hand-painted sign. The windows displayed jars of dried herbs, bundles of roots, and packets of powder.
Dexter pushed open the door.
"Morning," Dexter said, keeping his voice low. "I need a week’s supply of specialized ingredients. Sun-moon fruit, Juniper bark root, Dry Dragon-Leaf, and premium spiritual pearl rice."
An elderly man with thick glasses was behind the counter. The man gave a warm smile and replied. "How much quantity do you want to purchase?"
Dexter calculated for a bit and replied.
The merchant nodded his head."Two thousand dollars for a single day’s supply of genuine Sun-moon fruit and Juniper bark root. For a week, that will be fourteen thousand dollars."
Dexter did not hesitate. He tapped his phone against the payment terminal, confirming the transfer. "I’ll take them. Please pack them securely."
The old man smile widened.
’What a nice customer. He didn’t even haggle’
Then he replied. "Please wait while I prepare them do you."
He then left the counter and headed deeper into the shop.

After the transaction was done, Dexter bought more things, two large bags of premium organic rice, fresh vegetables, lean chicken breast, and high-quality beef from the organic section, spending another five hundred dollars.
While walking on the street , he used his phone to browse a reputable local security agency online.

The bungalow’s wooden doors and thin window frames were far too easy to breach, as Kreg had proven. He selected a high-grade home defense package that included reinforced steel deadbolts, heavy iron security bars for all ground-floor windows, and a basic motion-sensor alarm system.
He paid five thousand dollars upfront for an express, same-day installation. The agency promised to send a team of technicians that same morning.
While walking through the district, he stopped in front of an Relic shop. Relic are tools with special effects to increase one’s damage power, speed and even mana.
The higher the type of Relic the stronger they are.
The Relic shop was called "Essence Emporium".
The interior was larger than Heaven’s Taste, with glass display cases arranged in a grid pattern.
Each case held jewellery, weapons, accessories and all of them faintly glowing with stored mana.
Type 1 Relics were the lowest tier of enchanted items, but even they were expensive.
A young man in a neat uniform stood behind the counter. "Welcome to Essence Emporium. How can I help you today?"
"I need equipments with Pain reduction and Calming effects. Do you have anything like that?"
The clerk’s expression became professionally interested. "We have several options. For pain reduction, I’d recommend the Serenity Bangle. "
The youth to a display case of silver bracelets — "Type 1, reduces pain signals by up to 10% and takes the edge off chronic conditions."
"How much?"
"Eight thousand credits.
Dexter’s eyes twitched. That was more than he’d expected. He sighed and replied.
"I’ll take one."
The clerk retrieved the bracelet and placed it on the counter. It was plain thin silver band with a small blue gem set in the center. But there was actual beauty in its simplicity.

"For calming effects," the clerk continued, "we have the Tranquility Band. Type 1, reduces anxiety and stabilizes emotional fluctuations. It’s often prescribed for heroes with PTSD or anxiety disorders."
"Does it help with seizures?"
The clerk hesitated. "It’s not designed for that specifically. But if the seizures are triggered by emotional instability or stress, it might reduce their frequency. I can’t make any guarantees."
Dexter thought of Selene and replied.
"I’ll take two," he said.
"Two Tranquility Bands?"
"Yes."
"That’s five thousand each, so ten thousand total."
Dexter’s remaining balance was shrinking rapidly.
But the system would reward him. He had to trust that.
He paid and took the three bracelets — one Serenity Bangle for Mira, two Tranquility Bands for Selene and Lyra.
After confirming the payment, Dexter took the three small jade boxes and slipped them into his backpack.

His also stopped at a licensed medical supply pharmacy. He purchased a few bandages, painkillers and other things. While standing at the counter, he hesitated, his face turning slightly red as his eyes fell on the hygiene section. He realized that three young women living in an old house would eventually need basic personal supplies.
Embarrassed but resolute, he grabbed several packs of premium tampons and personal hygiene wipes, placing them on the counter.
"Is that everything, sir?" the pharmacist asked, hiding a small smile.
"Yes," Dexter said, clearing his throat. "That’s everything."
On his way back to the bungalow, as he passed a high-tech electronics store, a display in the window caught his eye.

It was a pair of sleek AI smart glasses. The advertisement claimed the glasses could translate spoken words into real-time text projected onto the lenses, or translate it to other languages so one can speak across several languages.
Dexter paused as an idea formulated in his mind.
He entered the store and purchased two pairs of the smart glasses for twenty thousand dollars.
By the time he finished his shopping spree, his bank account had been reduced from 150,000 thousand credits to exactly 6000.
He had spent forty-four thousand dollars in a single morning. But he did not feel a single shred of regret.
