Type 1 Relics were the lowest tier of enchanted items, but even they were expensive.
A young man in a neat uniform stood behind the counter.
"Welcome to Essence Emporium.
How can I help you today?"
"I need equipments with Pain reduction and Calming effects.
Do you have anything like that?"
The clerk’s expression became professionally interested.
"We have several options.
For pain reduction, I’d recommend the Serenity Bangle.
The youth to a display case of silver bracelets — "Type 1, reduces pain signals by up to 10% and takes the edge off chronic conditions."
"How much?"
"Eight thousand credits.
Dexter’s eyes twitched.
That was more than he’d expected.
He sighed and replied.
"I’ll take one."
The clerk retrieved the bracelet and placed it on the counter.
It was plain thin silver band with a small blue gem set in the center.
But there was actual beauty in its simplicity.
"For calming effects," the clerk continued, "we have the Tranquility Band.
Type 1, reduces anxiety and stabilizes emotional fluctuations.
It’s often prescribed for heroes with PTSD or anxiety disorders."
"Does it help with seizures?"
The clerk hesitated.
"It’s not designed for that specifically.
But if the seizures are triggered by emotional instability or stress, it might reduce their frequency.
I can’t make any guarantees."
Dexter thought of Selene and replied.
"I’ll take two," he said.
"Two Tranquility Bands?"
"Yes."
"That’s five thousand each, so ten thousand total."
Dexter’s remaining balance was shrinking rapidly.
But the system would reward him.
He had to trust that.
He paid and took the three bracelets — one Serenity Bangle for Mira, two Tranquility Bands for Selene and Lyra.
After confirming the payment, Dexter took the three small jade boxes and slipped them into his backpack.
His also stopped at a licensed medical supply pharmacy.
He purchased a few bandages, painkillers and other things.
While standing at the counter, he hesitated, his face turning slightly red as his eyes fell on the hygiene section.
He realized that three young women living in an old house would eventually need basic personal supplies.
Embarrassed but resolute, he grabbed several packs of premium tampons and personal hygiene wipes, placing them on the counter.
"Is that everything, sir?" the pharmacist asked, hiding a small smile.
"Yes," Dexter said, clearing his throat.
"That’s everything."
On his way back to the bungalow, as he passed a high-tech electronics store, a display in the window caught his eye.
It was a pair of sleek AI smart glasses.
The advertisement claimed the glasses could translate spoken words into real-time text projected onto the lenses, or translate it to other languages so one can speak across several languages.
Dexter paused as an idea formulated in his mind.
He entered the store and purchased two pairs of the smart glasses for twenty thousand dollars.
By the time he finished his shopping spree, his bank account had been reduced from 150,000 thousand credits to exactly 6000.
He had spent forty-four thousand dollars in a single morning.
But he did not feel a single shred of regret.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 | Smart Glass For Selene
paragraphs: Dexter arrived back at the bungalow at eight-thirty.

At exactly nine o’clock, a white van pulled up outside the gate. Three professional security technicians stepped out, carrying heavy toolboxes and metal bars. Dexter greeted them quietly, guiding them through the house. For the next two hours, the sound of drilling and metal clanging echoed through the bungalow.

By ten o’clock, the work was finished. Every window on the ground floor was now reinforced with thick, black iron security bars, and the front and back doors had been fitted with heavy, grade-1 steel deadbolts and a digital keypad lock.
A small, subtle alarm panel was installed beside the entrance. It wasn’t enough but at least it could inform the police if there was another break in attempt.
With the house secure, Dexter walked into the lady’s room. Mira was already awake, strangely sitting in her wheelchair. Dexter guessed Lyra might have helped her there.
While Lyra sat quietly on the sofa and Selene laying in the bed with her eyes opened.
Dexter reached into his backpack and pulled out the first pair of AI smart glasses. He walked over to Lyra, crouching down so he was at eye level with her.

As he reached out, Lyra flinched slightly, her shoulders tensing as she pulled back. Dexter stopped his movement, keeping his hands open and visible. He pulled out his notepad and wrote in large, clear letters:
`[These are smart glasses. They will translate my voice into text on the screen so you can see what I am saying. Please try them.]`
He held the note in front of her. Lyra read the words, her dark eyes moving from the paper to the sleek, white glasses in his hand.
But her expression didn’t change in the slightest.
He held them out to her.
Lyra didn’t reach for them.
Dexter waited. Then he typed another message.
[Please try them. I think they’ll help.]
She stared at the text for a long moment. Then, slowly, she raised her hand and took the glasses.
Her fingers were cold, she turned the glasses over in her hands, examining them.
Then she put them on.
The lenses flickered as the AI activated. The clerk had alredy calibrated it in advance so he didn’t need to touch anything.
Dexter nervously cleared his throat and spoke. "Can you see the text?"
The glasses translated his voice into words that appeared on Lyra’s lenses in real time.
[Can you see the text?]
Lyra’s eyes moved slightly, reading. Then she looked at Dexter.
Her expression changed.
It was so subtle that anyone without enhanced perception might have missed it. But Dexter caught it.
’That means it’s working.’
Dexter grinned and spoken again.

"If you want to speak back to me," Dexter said, pointing to the small button on the frame of the glasses, "you can type a message on your phone, and the glasses will read the text out loud using a text-to-speech feature. We can communicate now."
Lyra remained silent, completely rooted in place, staring at him through the glasses.
"Hey," Dexter said softly, leaning closer. "Are you alright?"

She did not respond. She looked down at her lap, her hands clenching into tight fists. Dexter sighed quietly, thinking he might have pushed her too fast or made her uncomfortable. He stood up, turning his attention to Selene.
Dexter walked over to Selene, holding the second pair of smart glasses. He carefully sat beside her, keeping his voice low so as not to startle her.
"Selene, I bought something for you too. These glasses have an active AI assistant. I’ve installed the house schematic to the glasses."

"Also, it constantly scans the surroundings and through the bone conducting sound, it will speak to you and inform you where you want to go or how many steps to the kitchen, and where the doors are. It will help you move around the house safely."
Selene did not respond. She laid there as still as a statue, her pale skin looking almost translucent in the morning light.
Dexter waited for a moment, then gently set the white glasses on the sofa cushion right beside her hand. "I’ll leave them here for you. You can try them whenever you feel ready."
Dexter walked back into the kitchen, and started making the "Five Body Nourishing Meals" he knew by heart this time.

According to the text, this broth was a rare, low-grade Enchanted Meal designed specifically to slowly coat damaged meridians, easing the constant nerve pain caused by severed pathways and restoring a tiny fraction of active mana circulation.

Dexter carefully pulled the expensive ingredients from the insulated bags. He sliced the thick, pale root of the Sun-moon fruit into thin, even discs. The root released a sharp, medicinal scent that cleared his sinuses. He then took the Juniper bark root and ground it into a fine powder using a small mortar and pestle.

As the hours passed, the kitchen filled with an incredible, rich aroma. The scent was entirely different from the simple porridge he had made the night before; it was sweet, heavy, and complex, smelling of fresh mountain air, wild honey, and warm herbs.
By one o’clock, the broth had boiled down into a thick, shimmering liquid that looked like liquid gold.
[Ding! You have succeeded in making a Grade 1 making Enchanted Meal]
[Name: Enchanted Meal]
[Type: Food]
[Grade: 1]
[Effect: Nourish the body, moisturize meridians, heal injuries and calm the mind]
Dexter ladled the hot, golden broth into three small bowls then carried them to the dining table, where his three wives were already seated.

Interestingly, none of them were wearing the smart glasses he had purchased. Lyra had left hers on the living room table, and Selene’s still sat untouched on the sofa cushion. Dexter’s brow furrowed slightly in disappointment, but he did not comment. He set the bowls down in front of them.
He sat beside her wheelchair with the bowl in one hand and the spoon in the other.
"Open," he said.
Mira turned her head to look at him. Her crimson eyes moved from his face to the bowl to the spoon. Her eyes squinted as though she recognized what it was but couldn’t believe it.
"What is this?" she asked.
"Meridian-Soothing Broth," Dexter said. "First of the Five Body Nourishing Meals."
Mira’s eyes widened slightly as she knew it was actually a Grade 1 Enchanted Meal the moment she saw it.
But if it was really a Grade 1 Enchanted Meal and Dexter made it, that would mean that Dexter was at least a Novice Food-Smith!

chapters.title: Chapter 10 | REWARDS!!!
paragraphs: ’Truly full of surprises.’ She thought in her mind as she glanced at him.
Dexter fed her and she opened her mouth slightly, letting the warm spoon enter.
The moment the broth touched her throat, a , soothing warmth exploded within her chest.
A wave of pure, refined mana rushed along her severed meridians. The constant, burning nerve pain in her neck and shoulders, suddenly dulled, dropping significantly for the first time in three years.
She stared at Dexter and spoke.
"Didn’t you give all your money to the filth yesterday?"
"Don’t worry about the money," Dexter replied with a small, relaxed chuckle, holding up another spoonful.
Mira stared at him, her eyes searching his face but she eventually gave up and muttered. "Stubborn."
As he fed her, Mira glanced at the empty space on the table beside her, then looked at Dexter. "Where is mine?"
Dexter paused, his spoon hovering in the air. "Your what?"
She narrowed her crimson eyes at him. "My smart glasses. Or do you think I don’t need them just because I’m paralyzed?"
Dexter snorted softly, a trace of amusement in his eyes. "Don’t you usually like closing your eyes and ignoring me? What do you need them for?"
Mira glared at him. "If I don’t wear them, good luck getting those two to wear theirs."

Dexter’s face twitched. He looked from Mira to Lyra and Selene, who were sitting silently at the table. He realized Mira might be right; the other two were watching her, taking cues from her behavior.
"Alright," Dexter said, sighing as he smiled. "I give up. If you can get them to wear the glasses, I will buy the latest, most expensive model for you tomorrow."
Mira let out a short, quiet huff of satisfaction, swallowing the last of her broth.
"Did you sell your kidney?"
Dexter smiled gently as he reached into his backpack, pulling out three small, velvet-lined jade boxes. "Would it have mattered if I did?"
Mira rolled her eyes, but said. Nothing more.
"Oh, before I forget."

Dexter set the three jade boxes on the table. He opened the first box, revealing the bronze-tinted metallic Pain-Reducing Bracelet. He leaned closer to Mira, carefully lifting her limp right hand and sliding the band over her wrist.
"It’s really ugly," Mira muttered, looking at the simple bronze band.

But the moment the metal made contact with her skin, a soft, high-frequency hum vibrated through her wrist. A mild, soothing electric pulse traveled up her arm, gently blocking the chronic pain signals in her spine. The constant pain in her neck and shoulders dropped by another ten percent.

Mira froze. Her crimson eyes widened as she felt the sudden, blessed relief wash over her body. She looked from her wrist to Dexter’s face, her voice dropping to a whisper. "You... you bought me a Type 1 artifact?"
"Yes," Dexter said, nodding his head. "It’s a pain-reduction artifact. It should help make sitting in that chair a bit more comfortable."
He stood up, picked up the other two jade boxes, and handed them to Lyra. He pulled out his phone, typed a quick note, and showed it to her:
`[These are Calming Bracelets. They are low-grade artifacts that will help calm your mind and reduce Selene’s seizure frequency. Please keep them.]`

Lyra read the text, her dark eyes looking at the beautiful, blue jade bracelets inside the boxes. She looked up at Dexter, her expression soft and silent, and slowly nodded. She took one of the bracelets and slid it onto her own wrist, then reached out to slide the second one onto Selene’s arm.
Selene sat quietly, drinking her golden broth in silence. But when she finished her bowl, she slowly tilted her head toward Dexter.
Her lips parted, and she spoke in a voice so soft and quiet that Dexter almost missed it:
"...Warm."
It was the very first word she had spoken to him since they met.
At that exact moment, a flood of bright, golden notifications materialized in Dexter’s vision, accompanied by a rapid succession of soft tones in his mind.
[Ding!]
[Investment Detected: Physical, Mental, Emotional, Security]
[Current Multiplier: 10x]
[Calculating Returns...]
[Calculation Complete.]
[Returns Granted]
[Skill Upgrade]
[Cooking: Novice (Peak) → (Early) Rank 1 Master Food Smith]
• Improved Enchanted Meal Success Rate
• Reduced Ingredient Waste
• Enhanced Flavor Extraction
• Additional Meal Effects
[Recipe Acquired]
[Grade 2 Recipe: Body Accelerating Healing Broth]
• Accelerates recovery and healing
• Double the effect of the Five Body Nourishing Meals when taken together.
[Cultivation Reward]
[2 Months of Compressed Mana Refinement]
[Item Upgrades]
[Serenity Bangle] x2
Type 1 Relic → Type 2 Relic
• Pain Reduction: 10% → 20%
[Tranquility Band]
Type 1 Relic → Type 2 Relic
• Calms the Mind
• Stimulates Brain Activity
[AI Smart Glasses] (Type 1) x3
→ Uses body heat to charge
→ Doesn’t need internet to translate
→ 100x speed in transcribing and translating (Type 2)
• Real-Time Speech Translation
• Multi-Language Translation
• Detects Mana Signatures
• Detects Aura Fluctuations
[Medical Supplies]
→ Grade 1 Painkiller
• Eliminates Pain for 2 Hours
[Security Upgrade]

• Right reinforced Steel Deadbolts
• Iron Window Bars

• Mana-Sensitive Perimeter Ward
• Silent Alert Linked to Security Guild

chapters.title: Chapter 11 | Step-Mother’s Visit
paragraphs: Dexter almost burst out in happiness right there and then. All his investments actually came back to him! Well, not the cash but even then, these returns were terrifying.
Just cooking for a few hours and he gained 2 months worth of cultivation. If he did this everyday, wouldn’t he break through to Super hero stage in less than a month?
It was too terrifying to even think about!
Dexter accepted without hesitation.

The knowledge flooded into his mind — new techniques, new recipes, new understanding of how food and cultivation intersected. His hands tingled as the cooking skill upgraded, muscle memory forming for movements he’d never made.
Two more months of cultivation. Added to the ten months he’d already received, that was a full year of compressed mana refinement in less than forty-eight hours.
He was still weak. Still at the bottom of the power hierarchy. But he was climbing.
Dexter’s smile vanished instantly. His E-rank Enhanced Hearing activated and he picked up the sound of a heavy, idling engine outside the gate.
He walked cautiously to the front door, unlocked the heavy new deadbolt, and stepped onto the porch.
Standing outside the gate was a massive, clean-cut bodyguard wearing a tailored black suit and dark sunglasses. He stood with his hands folded in front of him.

Behind him, a long black Rolls-Royce sat parked against the curb. The rear door of the luxury car opened, and another bodyguard, holding a large black umbrella, helped a woman step out onto the cracked asphalt.
The woman walked elegantly up the concrete path toward the gate.

She looked to be in her late thirties, but her smooth, pale skin and flawless features made her look no older than nineteen. She had long, raven-black hair streaked with elegant silver at the temples, sharp, aristocratic cheekbones, and eyes the color of winter ice. She wore a dark designer dress that likely cost more than Dexter’s entire house, and her every movement oozed a cold, effortless authority.
"Stepmother," Dexter said, his voice going completely flat.
Valentina Ashford.
She was the primary wife of Aldric Ashford, the current leader of the family. She was the woman who had orchestrated Dexter’s suffering and isolation since he was a child.
Valentina had never laid a hand on him herself—she was far too intelligent for physical violence.

Instead, she had simply reduced him to a life of slavery, suffering and pain. She had spent ten years trying to make him invisible, to erase his very existence. And even killed a few of the servants for pitying him. Those who show him affection either ends up dead or maimed.
"Dexter, darling," Valentina said, her perfect smile not reaching her cold, winter-blue eyes. "May I come in?"
Without waiting for his invitation, the lead bodyguard opened the gate, and Valentina walked past Dexter, stepping into the small bungalow.
She surveyed the small living room with barely concealed disdain, her ice-blue eyes lingering on the worn sofas and old tv.
"How... cozy," Valentina murmured, her gaze moving slowly around the room. "I see you’ve made yourselves at home."
"What do you want, Valentina?" Dexter growled.
Valentina’s smile sharpened. "Can’t a mother check on her dear son?"
"My mother died when I was born."
"True, a truly mysterious death." Valentina glanced at him and chuckled then smoothly, walked slowly around the room.
She paused near the dining table, her cold gaze falling on the three women.

"The Crimson Valkyrie, Shadow Saintess and the illustrious Eternal Ice Princess Tempest." She let out a soft, mocking tutting sound. "Such a waste. Three brilliant heroes, reduced to... this. And married to a useless, bastard.

She turned to Dexter, her head tilting like a curious bird. "Your father was quite generous, don’t you think? He could have ignired the plea of the three families. Instead, he let you marry the three useless and famous cripple. ."
Dexter’s eyes narrowed. "I am asking again. What do you want, Valentina? Since I no longer have ties to the Ashford family, I can have you arrested for trespassing."
Valentina’s smile slowly vanished, and for a brief second, her mask of high-class elegance slipped, revealing a cold, ruthless expression.
"Very well," she said quietly.

paragraphs: "It turns out the gate was not misclassified by accident. Someone intentionally altered the records to trap those three girls inside that dungeon permanently."
She let out a soft, mocking chuckle. "If they wanted them dead back then, you might want to ask yourself... will they want to finish the job now?"
Without waiting for his response, she stepped out of the house, her bodyguards closing the heavy door behind her.
Dexter stood frozen in the middle of the living room.
From the table, Mira let out a cold, sharp snort. "If you hadn’t realized that already, ’husband’, then you are even dumber than I thought."
From the start to the finish, she hadn’t once glanced at lady Ashford. Her eyes closed as though she was sleeping in the wheelchair.
Dexter stood in the kitchen for a long time, staring at the closed front door.

Valentina’s words had confirmed his worst fears. The SSS-rank gate disaster was not as simple what they said. It was a targeted, assassination attempt to wipe out the talents of the three families all at once. And now that the three girls were living together in a defenseless, run-down bungalow, it would be even simpler to kill then.
He needed to grow stronger, fast.

With his newly awakened E-rank mana affinity and the Flame Demon bloodline, he had a solid foundation. But he had no formal combat techniques, and he could not afford to purchase expensive monster nexus cores to accelerate his cultivation without a hero license.
To get a license, he would have to register with the local Hero Guild, undergo a physical test, and successfully clear a trial dungeon.
But the fastest way to build his power was still through the system. He needed to take care of his wives, provide for them, and earn more investments.
The next three days passed in a quiet, steady rhythm.

Dexter woke at 4:30 AM every day. He showered, dressed, and began cooking breakfast. The meals were simple — rice porridge, eggs, vegetables — but he added a thread of mana to each one, just like he had with the first nourishing meal.
At 6:00 AM, he woke the women.

Mira was the easiest. She was always awake before he came for her, sitting in her wheelchair by the window, staring at nothing. He’d push her to the bathroom, help her with her morning routine, and then wheel her to the kitchen.
Lyra required text messages. He’d type [Wake up] on his phone and hold it in front of her face until she opened her eyes. Then he’d give hwr the glasses. Afterwhich everything else name easy.
Selene was the hardest. She didn’t wish to wear the glasses and thought it might be humiliating but he convinced her tht the other two girls are wearing she reluctantly wore it on the third day.
Breakfast was eaten in silence. Dexter fed Mira. Lyra fed herself, though she ate enough for three people and he was constantly having to cook more. Selene required guidance Lyra assisted with that.
Mid-Morning.
After breakfast, Dexter prepared the Five Body Nourishing Meal for the day. Each meal took between two and four hours to cook, depending on the recipe.
Dexter rotated through the meals, one per day, following the recipe manual’s recommended schedule.
He fed each meal to the women and watched for changes.

Mira’s pain levels decreased gradually. The Serenity Bangle helped, but the meals were making a difference too. After three days, he saw in the system that her chronic nerve pain had dropped from 6/10 to about 5.2/10 — not a huge change, but noticeable.
Lyra’s appetite remained enormous, but her mood seemed slightly more stable.
Selene’s seizures didn’t stop, but the Frost Sense Dexter had acquired let him anticipate them and adjusted the serum in advance reducing the seizure by a lot.
Afternoon.
After the nourishing meal, Dexter worked with Mira on physical therapy.

Her muscles were atrophying and if he didn’t act, she’d lose what little function she had left. He didn’t know if the meals would eventually repair her meridians enough for her to move again, but he wasn’t going to wait and find out.
Mira hated it.
"This is useless and humiliating," she said through gritted teeth as he bent her left arm at the elbow. "Unhand me you pervert."
"Yes. I’m a pervert."
Dexter replied.
"What’s the use when we’re going to die in a few days?"
"This is for when you will be able to walk again. "
She glared at him, even the nunber one geneticist in the city couldn’t do anything, what’s makes you think you can?
’The system.’ Of course Levi wasn’t stupid enough to blurt it out.
While he worked with Mira, Lyra sat nearby and watched.
Late Afternoon.
Dexter trained in the backyard.
The space was small but it was enough for basic practice. He’d cleared away the debris and set up a makeshift training area with a punching bag he’d bought from a secondhand store.
He practiced basic punches. Jabs. Crosses. Hooks. Uppercuts. The movements were crude as he had no formal combat training, but he was learning.
He practiced kicks too. His legs were stronger than his arms as the Flame Demon bloodline seemed to favor lower body power.
Then he tried to use his abilities.

Flame Burst Step was the easiest. He activated it, and the world blurred and he appeared at another location in a split second. The speed was disorienting, but he was getting better at controlling it. He could now choose a specific destination instead of just launching himself forward blindly.
Flame Slash was harder.
Evening.
Dinner, more simple food, more silence.
Then bedtime.
Dexter helped each woman to the bedroom — Mira in her wheelchair, Lyra guiding Selene. He helped Mira into bed, arranged the blankets around Selene, and made sure Lyra was comfortable.
Then he retreated to his own room and cultivated until sleep claimed him.
This happened for three days and the rewards he got were astronomical. He broke through to Tier 3 Awakened Hero stage the next morning.
Dexter headed to the backyard, practicing his punches, when he heard something.
His enhanced hearing picked it up immediately.
He turned just as a girl climbed over the low fence that separated his backyard from the neighbor’s.
She was about sixteen, with messy brown hair and a face full of freckles.
"You’re the guy from the news," she said. "The one who married the three cripple."

chapters.title: Chapter 13 | Mysterious Tessa
paragraphs: The afternoon sun beat down on the neighborhood, making the air shimmer with heat.
A dog barked from across the street as a car passed.
"Bang!" "Bang!" "Bang!"
Rhythmic punching noises sounded out from the backyard of a small bungalow.
The punching swayed as a young man relentlessly punched at the bag with two jabs, a cross and a hook.
He was wearing a grey wife-beater that was soaked through with sweat.
He raised his fists again. Jab. Cross. Hook.
That young man is Dexter.
After two hours of grilling, he felt he was setting a hang of the whole punching thing.
He wiped the sweat off his forehead and drank an enormous water.
"You’re doing it wrong."
Dexter almost chocked in surprise. He lowered the water and glanced up at the fence line.

A girl was sitting on top of the wooden fence that separated his backyard from the neighbor’s property. She looked completely comfortable, as if sitting on a narrow wooden fence was the most natural thing in the world.

She looked sixteen, maybe seventeen. Red messy hair, tied back with a strip of cloth. Freckles scattered across her nose and cheeks like someone had flicked paint at her face. Green eyes that shone like a cat’s eye.
She wore a simple blue dress with a white apron. Which meant she’s either baking at home right now or works at one.
"Excuse me?" Dexter said.
"The punch." She pointed at the punching bag. "You’re leading with your shoulder. That’s why you keep losing your balance slightly after the hook."
Dexter stared at her. "How long have you been watching?"
"For 10 minutes give or take." She casually said. "You were very loud. I can hear you grunting from my kitchen."
Dexter felt heat crawl up his neck. He hadn’t realized anyone could hear him.
The girl swung her legs and dropped from the fence, and landed on the ground with a soft thud.
She was shorter than him by a few inches, but she carried herself with a confidence that made her seem bigger.
"I’m Tessa. Tessa Wren. I live next door." She jerked her thumb over her shoulder. "My dad owns the bakery on the corner."
"Oh." Dexter wiped sweat from his forehead with the back of his hand. "I’m Dexter."
"I know." She said it blandly, without excitement or judgment. "Everyone knows.
Her mouth was quite sharp and faster than her brain.
"The bastard prince with crippled wives." She tilted her head, studying him. "That’s what everyone in the neighborhood is calling you."
Dexter’s face hardened slightly. "Is that so."

"It is." Tessa walked past him to the punching bag and gave it a light tap with her knuckles. It barely moved. "The old ladies at the market think you’re a scandal. The men think you’re either crazy or brilliant.
"And what do kids like you think?" Dexter asked.
"The kids think you’re interesting." She looked back at him. "And I think you’re bad at punching."
Dexter suddenly chuckled.
"I guess I owe you a thanks then."
"You’re welcome." Tessa turned around and touched the fence.
All of a sudden, she leapt up and landed on the narrow top wood like a cat.
The fence wasnt even two inches wide but she stood on it as if it were solid ground.
"Here is how you punch," Her voice suddenly turned serious as she clenched her fists then started shadow boxing.
"Power comes from the ground and the waist," she said. "Not the arm. The arm is just the delivery system. The real punch starts in your feet."
She gestured at the bag. "Try it."
Dexter looked at her for a moment. Then he turned to the punching bag, set his feet, and threw a hook.
This time, he led with his hip. He rotated his waist, transferred his weight, and let his fist follow the momentum.
"Bang!"
It sounded like a sharp crack as his fist struck the punching bag.
Dexter raised an eyebrow in surprise.
"You’re a fast learner," Tessa smiled.
Dexter clenched and then three another hook, then another. Each one landed with that same sharp crack, sending bag swinging harder and harder.
The difference was quite incredible.
He turned to Tessa. "Where did you learn that?"
She shrugged. "You learn a thing or two in this neighborhood. People here aren’t as simple as they seem."

Dexter squinted. He focused on her, trying to read her energy waves. Everyone who absorb mana emit an energy wave that others can feel to determine their power level. Just like how you look at someone to determine if he’s insane or not.
Well, unless they’re hiding it that is.
But Tessa was like a calm lake with no ripple.
Dexter frowned. He couldn’t get a reading on her at all. Which either meant she’s a normal human or she’s a whole realm higher then him.
But he was certain of one thing: she was a hero.
"You’re a hero," he said.
Tessa’s expression didn’t change. "Am I?"
"Awakened Or Super?"
"I’m just an ordinary girl with no energy to read." She shrugged.
"Ordinary girls can’t stand on a two-inch fence rail without falling."
Tessa smiled an astonishing smile. "Maybe I just have good balance."
Dexter stared at her for a long moment. Then he shook his head. She wasn’t going to tell him. Fine. He had bigger problems.
"You’re training to become a hero, aren’t you?" Tessa suddenly asked.
"Something like that." Dexter turned back to the punching bag and resumed his fisting but this time, he reduced his striking force.
She tilted her head again. "You’ll probably die in your first dungeon."
"Probably."
"But you’re still going anyway."
"I have to." Dexter glanced at the house. Through the kitchen window, he could see the faint outline of someone sitting at the table — Lyra, probably.
Tessa was quiet for a moment. The sound of traffic, dog barking and Dexter’s punch filled the silence.
"My mother was a hero," Her voice lowered softly.

"But you’re still going anyway."
"I have to." Dexter glanced at the house.
Through the kitchen window, he could see the faint outline of someone sitting at the table — Lyra, probably.
Tessa was quiet for a moment.
The sound of traffic, dog barking and Dexter’s punch filled the silence.
"My mother was a hero," Her voice lowered softly.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 | Not Enough
paragraphs: "My mother was a hero," Tessa’s voice lowered softly.
"She died in a D-rank Cyclops dungeon when I was ten."
Dexter paused and he looked at her.

"She was a B-rank hero." Tessa’s green eyes were fixed on the ground. "Strong enough to clear D-rank dungeons in her sleep, everyone said. But dungeons don’t care about ranks. One wrong step, and she never came home."
"I’m sorry."

"Don’t be." Tessa looked up, and her eyes were dry. "Heroing isn’t as glorious as the Hero Association makes it out to be. It’s ugly and dangerous and most people who try it end up dead or worse. The ones who survive are either lucky, talented, or both." She studied him. "You’re neither."
"Thanks."
Tessa guffawed at his reply.
"Come by the bakery tomorrow morning. We’re preparing our special — honey buns with secret glaze. They’re good for recovery." She paused, looking back at him.
Before Dexter could respond, she dropped down on the other side of the fence and disappeared into the neighbor’s yard.
Dexter stood in his backyard, staring at the empty fence.
The girl was definitely not simple.
But she’d helped him. And she hadn’t asked for anything in return.
He shook his head and turned back to the punching bag. He spent the next hour throwing hooks using the method she’d shown him.
By the time he went back inside, the sun was setting and Dexter was sweaty and exhausted but not felt really good.
Mira was sitting at the kitchen table with her eyes closed.
"Not even married for a month and you’re already talking to pretty young girls."
Dexter paused in the doorway, a drop of sweat falling from his chin to the floor. And he grinned.
Mira’s expression was flat. Her voice was even flatter. But there seem to be somythythat resembled amusement.
"Should I be jealous, husband?"
Dexter chuckled and walked to the sink, turning on the tap to wash his hands. "She’s sixteen, Mira."
"And I’m crippled, not blind." Lyra’s eyes followed him as he moved. "She was looking at you like you’re a lost puppy she wants to adopt."
Dexter dried his hands on a towel and leaned against the counter. "She’s just a neighbor."
"Just a neighbor who happens to know how to throw a perfect punch and stand on a fence rail without falling."
Mira remained silent but then spoke. "Be careful who you trust, Dexter. Everyone has an angle, even you."
Dexter froze where he stood.
The last three words ringing in his hears.
She was telling him she knew that he had an ulterior motive but she might have misunderstood.

chapters.title: Chapter 15 | Upgrading The Girls
paragraphs: Dexter closed the interface and sat quietly, his thoughts drifting back to Valentina’s warning.
Those Assassins. Someone had tried to kill the three women in that dungeon. They’d failed and the women had survived. But the people behind it wouldn’t just give up. They’d try again.
And Dexter was the only thing standing between them
He was only a Tier 3 Awakened Hero. Any assassin worth their money would be at Tier 9, maybe even early Super Hero rank. In a direct fight, Dexter wouldn’t last ten seconds.
He needed to advance further and even more, he needed a weapon.
Not the decorative broad sword that had come as a wedding gift but a real relic weapon that can channel his mana and amplify his combat ability.
But real relic weapons cost real money. And more importantly, to buy a weapon from any legitimate shop, you needed a Hero License.
The Hero Association regulated all relic weapons to prevent them from falling into the wrong hands.

To get a Hero License, you had to register with the Association, enter one of their virtual dungeons, and clear it. Your performance inside determined the rank of license you received, which in turn determined what grade of equipment you could buy.
Originally, Dexter had planned to wait until he reached at least Level 5 before taking the exam since a higher level would mean a better evaluation, a better license, and access to better weapons.
But he didn’t have time anymore.
"I actually almost forgot."
The thought came suddenly. He’d been so focused on the assassination threat and leveling up that he’d nearly overlooked something important.
When the system had rewarded him for the massive investment of buying all those items for his wives, it had returned the upgraded versions to him.
He reached into the drawer beside his bed and pulled out three beautiful bracelets.
The moment he touched it, a refreshing sensation flowed through his body, like stepping into a cool stream on a hot day. His mind cleared. The ache in his muscles from training faded to nothing.
’These are the real deal,’ Dexter thought.
A genuine Type 2 Serenity Bracelet was worth at least twenty thousand dollars on the open market.
He could sell them. Use the money to hire guards, buy black-market weapons, set up defenses.
But after only a brief moment of consideration, he shook his head and stood up, holding the three bracelets as he walked toward the living room.

Mira was seated in her wheelchair in front of the television. The TV was off but she sat there anyway, staring at the blank screen. She was wearing the AI smart glasses, but her eyes were closed behind the lenses, and her brows were furrowed in pain.
Even with the Type 1 bracelet, the pain was still there.
She seemed to notice him approaching as her neck tilted slightly but she didn’t open her eyes.
Dexter stopped beside her and held out one of the new bracelets.
"Mira," he said softly. "I brought you another bracelet. It does the same thing as the one you’re wearing, only it’s much more effective. Give me your wrist."
Mira slowly opened her eyes.
Her gaze first landed on his face. Then it shifted to the bracelet in his hand.
Her eyebrows knitted together.
"...That’s a Type 2 bracelet."

She stared at him with suspicion. Dexter had learned over the past few days that Mira knew more about artefacts and cultivation resources than he did — she’d been an A-rank hero, after all. She could identify equipment grades by sight.
"She spoke in a Flat tone. "First, you bought a Type 1 bracelet, and now you’ve brought home a Type 2 relic. don’t tell me you actually sold your kidney to buy this."
Dexter glared at her. "Do you want it or not?"
Mira snorted softly. "As though I can stop you? Do what you want."
Dexter nodded. He reached for her wrist and unclasped the old Type 1 bracelet then quickly fastened the new Type 2 bracelet in its place.
The instant the clasp clicked shut, Mira’s body trembled as a cool, soothing energy spread from the bracelet up her arm. From her shoulder, down her spine, and out into her limbs.
It was really nice, making Mira release a soft sigh.
The relentless pain that had tormented her every waking moment for three years diminished by twenty percent.
Twenty percent didn’t sound like much but for someone who had lived with constant, unbearable pain, it was a massive difference.
Compared to the Type 1 bracelet, which had only reduced her pain by about 10 percent, this was on an entirely different level.
For the first time in a long while, Mira’s tightly knitted brows slowly relaxed.
She sat there for a moment, clearly feeling the difference, her expression something Dexter had never seen on her face before.
It was relief.
Mira’s eyes narrowed slightly as she watched him lower her hand back onto the armrest. Then, without asking, he reached up and removed the bulky AI glasses from her face.
"Hey—"

"Relax." He replaced them with a thinner, lighter pair. "Advanced AI glasses. They have an eye-tracking system. You can use your eyes to browse the internet, navigate apps, read messages — everything. It’s connected to the network."
Mira blinked as the new lenses adjusted around her vision. The display was sharper, the text clearer, the interface more intuitive than the clunky Type 1 glasses.
She tested it — moving her eyes left, right, up, down — and the cursor on the display followed. A small smile tugged at the corner of her mouth before she suppressed it.
"The internet," she said, her voice dry. "Nothing but feeble people with opinions that change every split second."
Dexter said nothing. But he knew what she meant.
Not long ago, she had been the Flame-Heart Princess. An S-rank hero. One of the youngest B-rank heroes in the city. The internet had loved her, praised her, celebrated her, then the dungeon happened.
And the same internet that had worshiped her turned on her overnight. She went from hero to zero in the eyes of the world.
Mira closed her eyes behind the new glasses and said nothing more.
Lyra was standing at the window of the living room.
She always seemed to be standing or sitting near a window. Dexter wondered if it was because she couldn’t hear the world so she watched it instead.
Or maybe it was just the only place where she could feel like she was connected to something beyond these four walls.
He crossed the room and stopped beside her.
"I bought advanced versions," he said, holding up the items. "New AI smart glasses, thinner than the ones you’re wearing. And a Type 2 Serenity Bracelet to replace the Type 1."
The text appeared in her glasses, translating his spoken words in real time.

Lyra’s slender neck turned. Her dark eyes dropped to the bracelet in his left hand, then to the new glasses in his right. She studied them for a moment, her expression unreadable as always, then reached up and removed her old glasses.

She exchanged them for the new ones. The thinner frames settled on her face, and her eyes moved as the display calibrated. Then she unclasped her old bracelet and handed it to him. She fastened the new Type 2 bracelet around her wrist.
For a moment, she was her eyelid trembled.
The Serenity Band’s calming effect was subtle, not as dramatic as the pain relief Mira experienced, but he thought he saw her shoulders drop slightly.
"Is it working?" he asked.
This new glasses traslated the words quickly and even had two automated reply below the words.
[Yes. It’s working.] [No. It’s not working]
She glanced at the [Yes. It’s working] Option and a robotic voice rang out from the frame of the glasses.
"Yes. It’s working."
Dexter smiled.
He handed her a second set of glasses and a second Type 2 bracelet. "These are for Selene. She flinches when I touch her, so can you help me give them to her?"
Lyra looked at the items in his hands. Then she looked at him and nodded.
Took both items, then she turned and walked to the bedroom.
Two minutes later, she returned, carrying the old AI glasses and the old Type 1 bracelet. She handed them to Dexter without a word.

He took them and placed everything into a small storage case. He could sell them to a secondhand relic dealer and use the money to hire a guard at the Hero Association for a day, giving him ample time to enter a controlled dungeon and earn his license.
It wasn’t much of a plan. But it was what he had.
He was halfway to the door when the loud sound cut through the entire neighborhood.

chapters.title: Chapter 16 | Monster Outbreak!
paragraphs: The sound was very faint, but Dexter’s Enhanced Hearing caught it from five blocks away.
A long, wailing tone like that of a siren.
Dexter’s confused face immediately changed as he realized what it was.
A monster outbreak siren.
Every city in the country had them — warning sirens designed to alert the population when a dungeon breach occurred.

Dungeons were supposed to be contained, sealed behind gates that the Hero Association monitored. But sometimes, a gate destabilized, a new dungeon pops up or monsters broke through their cages. It was always unexpected and always cause death or injury.
Andrew groaned softly, he had been expecting assassins, didn’t think there would be an actual monster outbreak.
He closed his eyes, as he activated his ability.
Suddenly, every sound within a 200 meter radius flowed through his ears.
"BOOM!" "HOOOWL!" "Bang!" "Bang!" "Bang!" "H-help me! It’s—" "Squelch!"
Andrew’s face paled slightly and the last sound he heard was of a skull cracking and exploding like watermelon squeezed too tight.
The siren was coming from the east — from the direction of the Merchant Quarter and it was getting louder, which meant the breach was spreading.
’I hope it doesn’t reach here.’ Andrew thought nervously. From what he heard, the monsters were likely wolves but he wasn’t too sure.
Most breaches were contained quickly by the Hero Association had response teams that could be deployed within minutes. So the sirens were more of a precaution instead.
But "most" wasn’t "all."
Dexter had live long enough to know not to depend on his luck.

He immediately started to move as he locked the back door, then ran to the the front door and locked it. Then started with the windows locking every single windows in the house. Just in case. He moved the fridge to the front door and barricaded the back door with the dining chair.
Then he checked the locked doors once more to ensure no mistakes.
Mira’s quiet time was ruined by him running around the house. She opened her eyes and glared at him as he passed her wheelchair for the seventh time.
Her brows furrowed in irritation as she asked. "What are you doing?"
Dexter didn’t stop moving. "It’s hopefully nothing, but I’m hearing the outbreak siren in the distance. It’s better to be safe than sorry."
He went to Lyra, who was watching him from the kitchen doorway with a calm expression.
"There might be a monster outbreak nearby," he said, speaking clearly so the glasses could translate. "I need you to go to the bedroom. Just in case.
Lyra suddenly reached for something. It was her phone. Her fingers moved as a robotic voice spoke from the frame of her glasses.
"We are already dead. The monsters would be doing us a favour."
Dexter stared at her, stunned.
The idea that death would be a mercy made him sympathetic.
She’d been trapped in silence and darkness for three years, unable to hear, unable to speak, unable to do anything but exist. Of course she’d had thoughts like that.
Dexter didn’t know what to say. So he said nothing.
Lyra looked at him for a moment longer. Then she turned and walked to the bedroom without another word.
Dexter exhaled and went to Mira.
"Come on," he said, gripping the handles of her wheelchair.
"Did I tell you I wanted to move?" Mira’s voice was irritated.
"Did I ask your permission?"
Mira’s lips curled. "You know, you’re becoming quite abusive."
"I heard you like abusive men." Dexter replied without thinking.
The words left his mouth before his brain could stop them.
The moment they were out, Dexter wished he could take them back.
Mira’s face changed. The mocking irritation on her face changed as her expression turned blank and then chilling cold.
A raging fire replaced them as the crismon eyes locked in Dexter.
Mira’s father was rumored to be abusive. Dexter didn’t know the full story and was simply said to have been a senseless rumor that came out after the news of her being a cripple came out.
He thought it was just a rumor but from Mira’s reaction, it was most likely true.
He opened his mouth to apologize—
But then he heard something.
From two blocks away, the siren’s wail was suddenly drowned out by other sounds. Gunshots, screams and explosions then a very loud and sharp howl.
It was the sound of a monster.
And it was very close.
Dexter’s face changed. He grabbed Mira’s wheelchair and pushed her fast towards the bedroom.
"Lyra!" he called out as he reached the door. "Lock the door from behind!"
He wheeled Mira inside, positioned her chair against the far wall, and stepped back into the hallway. Then closed the door shut and locked it from the outside.
He waited but there was no sound of a lock clicking from inside.
Dexter’s eye twitched.
’Are these girls courting death!?’
He wanted to roar in anger. He’d just told them there was a monster outbreak. He’d just told them to lock the door. And they couldn’t even manage that one simple task?
He forced himself to calm down. Getting angry wouldn’t help. He needed to focus.
’Fine, it doesn’t really matter.’
He turned and ran to the kitchen.
Part of their wedding gift — the pile of boxes that had come from the three families — had contained a decorative broadsword.
It was a ceremonial blade with intricate design made to look beautiful however it wasn’t meant for battle.
Dexter had never bothered to move it and it had been leaning against the wall in the kitchen since the first night.
He grabbed it and frowned.
The metal was cheap, the balance was terrible, and the edge couldn’t even cut through bread.
But it was solid steel, and right now, solid steel was better than bare hands.
He also grabbed two kitchen knives from the drawer and tucked one into his waistband at his back and held the other in his left hand, the broadsword in his right.
Then he stood at the hall way and listened carefully, suddenly his face changed as the kitchen window shattered...

chapters.title: Chapter 17| Dark Hounds Attack
paragraphs: With his Enhanced Hearing, the world seem to become a map of sound.
He could hear the outbreak in detail now. People fighting, the sounds of gunfire, the roar of hero abilities activating, the crash of bodies hitting walls and vehicles.
But mixed in with the human sounds were the monster sounds.
’Dark Hounds.’
Dexter’s body stiffened as he recognized where he recognized the monster howls.

These are ordinary mutated beast with strength ranging from 3-stars to 7-Stars. But that wasn’t the most terrifying thing about them, the most frightening thing about them was that they came in packs, dozens of them. Sometimes hundreds.
The fast and aggressive pack hunters could tear through civilian neighborhoods like paper and they were getting closer.
"Awooooooo!"
Dexter’s grip tightened on the broadsword and cold sweat dripped down his forehead and ran along his jaw as his heart pounded rapidly.
He inhaled slowly, using the breathing method from the Starlight Meditation Technique to clear his mind and regulate his heart beat.
Then his ears trembled.
Dexter suddenly ran to the kitchen window and positioned himself beside it.
As though in cue,
"Bang!"
A claw tore through the reinforced iron bars on the kitchen window.
The metal screeched as three thick, black claws easily ripped through the bars like they were made of tin and a massive head popped inside.
It was a Dark Hound.
The beast looked like a mutated simple version of a dog. It was about 1.5 meters tall and larger than a lion with thick black fur and yellow eyes.
There was 4 star like patterns on its forehead signifying it was a 4-star Mutated Beast.
Droll escape its massive jaws and its teeth were long and curved like hunting knives.
Dexter eyes turned cold holding his breathe, he stabbed forward with his entire strength.
"Chi!"
Hot, foul smelling blood spilled out in all directions, spattering out there on the kitchen floor and wall.
"Squelch!"
The Hound thrashed, its claws scraping against the window frame. Dexter twisted the blade and pulled it free, and the creature’s body immediately went limp, half-in and half-out of the window.
[Requirement for System Activation Completed]
[Requirement: Kill 3 Humans or 3 Mutated Beast (3/3)]
[System Initialization Completed.
[Congratulations on activating the Slaughter Extraction System]
[Slaughter Extraction System: Extracted +3 strength, +2 Mana, ]
He didn’t have time to read the notification or ponder why his strength had suddenly increased as another sound entered his ears.
Dexter dropped the bloody broadsword and picked up the second kitchen knife from his waistband. One knife in each hand.
He hurried to the front door and his face changed as he rolled to the side.
In a split second, the door exploded inward as a massive Dark Hound burst through the ruined doorframe, letting the wood splinter.
"Hooooooowl—"
The howl shook the walls and rattled the window.
Dexter stomped his feet on the wall, using its momentum, he pivoted, as he stabbed the knife into its throat from underneath. The blade punched through the soft tissue of the neck and into the brain.
The Hound instantly collapsed and immediately died.
[SES: Extracted +3 strength, +2 Mana ]
Dexter yanked the knife free and rolled to the side as two more Hounds came through the destroyed door.
They were both level 5 Mutated Beast!
They immediately spread out as they charged at him from two different direction. One going left and one going right, trying to flank him with astonishing speed!
Dexter’s face changed as this two beasts were even faster than he could keep up with.
He activated his Enhanced Hearing to the fullest as a blur flashes to his left.
Dexter heard the wind shift and he instantly dodged left, letting the claw swipe through empty air.

As the claw missed him by a centimeter, he suddenly moved as he sliced the underside of its front leg but the blade wasn’t sharp enough to fully slice through it and only causing a deep wound, deep enough to make it bleed. The Dark Hound yelped and stumbled.
At that moment the Dark Hound on the left came immediately after.
Dexter instantly dropped low, as the claw sliced some of his hair.
His other knife moved as he slashed at the Hound’s belly as it passed. The knife cut through fur and skin, and the Hound snarled in pain, blood dripping from the wound.
But they weren’t dead. And more were coming.
Dexter suddenly heard another sound from behind him.
Another Dark Hound had actually crawled through the kitchen window!
His face changed as he quickly turned to the back.
But it was too late.
"Bang!"
The Dark Hound’s claw slammed into his back.
The impact was like getting hit by a car.
Pain exploded across his shoulder blades, and Dexter was sent flying across the hallway, slamming heavily in the wall as he slid to the floor.
His grip loosened and both knives clattered out of his hands.
For a moment, the world spun and his vision blurred as his back screamed with agony.

He gritted his teeth and forced himself to push thought the pain. He raised his head and then saw the hound that hit him wasn’t attacking again. He saw its forehead and he saw 6 star like pattern on its head.
6-Star Mutated Beast.
Dexter’s face paled and he knew today he might not survive.
’Should I escape?’
With [Flame Burst] bloodline skill and his Enhance Hearing ability, he was certain he could escape unscathed.
But the women...
His face kept changing as his brain fired up rapidly. His brain told him that his only chance at survival was to escape. There’s no way a Tier 3 Awakened Hero can kill a 6-Star Mutated beast!
Every level provides at least 25 stats which meant the 6-Star mutated beast has at least 150 stats in strength alone.
Dexter only has a pitiful 75 stats in strength; the gap was almost double!
If he runs now, he could survive but his wives...

chapters.title: Chapter 18 | Second System Awakening, Level Up
paragraphs: Dexter only has a pitiful 75 stats in strength; the gap was almost double!
If he runs now, he could survive but the girls, his wives, would definitely die.
He had only known them for almost a week but he didn’t even know what they liked. Therefore they were basically strangers.
Not to mention Lyra’s appetite. She could eat a family of three daily meal in one sitting.
Despite taking his time to cook extra portions for her, she never thanked him.
Selene basically treats him like he was filth from the dirtiest slum and flinches when he gets close to her.
Mira is the worst of them all.
Despite taking care of her every needs, she insults and undermine his ego every chance she got even when he bathes and wash her every single day.
The three women never once expressed their thanks and treats him like nothing.
Therefore it would be unreasonably, incredibly and ridiculously stupid to risk him life for them when they are basically strangers and log weight.

However, as he saw the beast moving toward the bedroom door. Toward Mira, Lyra and Selene, time seem to slow down and every sound seem to fade in the background as he heard breathing of the three women.
He recognized Mira’s taking in a deep breathe of air as though it was her last and then exhaled.
He recognized Lyra’s footsteps as she walked towards the door, impatiently awaiting what’s to come.
He recognized Selene’s slow beating heart suddenly picking up as she whispered her longest words.
"It’s finally hear."
The three had actually accepted their death and was fully embracing it.
Dexter’s face flushed in sadness but his heart lit up in inexplicable rage!
Rage that the girls had given up after this small amount of set back!
How could they be so selfish!?
Do they know how many people were born deaf and mute?
Do they know how many was born crippled or how many was born blind or how many was born with chronic pain?
And yet, those people managed to live life to the fullest, finding meaning and happiness in this world and even managed to find love.
Yet, these three selfish princesses got to live with their senses intact for so many years.
Not only that, the three were born talented and had everything served to them on silver platter but when they suffered this set back, they actually want to take their own lives?
"How can you be so selfish!?"
Dexter roared in anger and fury!
The rage burned so hot it burned away the pain.
"Scorching Fury!"
"BOOM!"
A surge of energy struck him like a thunderbolt.
His blood literally ignited as his magma like blood flooded through every fiber of his body.
His muscles trembled and swelled as his strength increased by 50%!
His eyes seem to burn with flame, with his irises flickering with actual fire as his hair floated upward.
The Dark Hound struck at the bedroom door and its claw easily pierced a hole in the door. One more strike and it would break through.
Dexter suddenly appeared beside the massive hound and thrust its two blade right through its neck.
"Ding!"
The Hound actually turned around so fast it slashed and parried the blade attack.
Dexter felt his arm trembled and he gritted his teeth.
The beast possess 150 agility stats and despite Dexter activating [Scorching Fury] his strength and agility capped at 112.5. There was still a vast difference between the two of them!
Before he could react, the Dark Hound’s mouth opened so wide it could fit a watermelon blurred as it flashed towards him.
If he doesn’t move, his head will be chopped off! But even with Scorching Fury his speed was still too slow to react to his head being bitten off.
Dexter’s eyes widened into a panic as he watched the maws of the Dark Hound Wrap around his head.
"Flame Burst!"
30 points of mana burned and Dexter’s feet released a blast of heat wave as Dexter’s agility increased by 300% for 1 second.
"Bang!"
Dexter watched as the massive mouth of the Dark hound slow down incredibly.
Dexter didn’t retreat, instead he turned towards the side of the beast. Its mouth was still wide open but its eyes actually reacted to Dexter’s incredibly fast movement.
Dexter raised the knives and stabbed them directly through the eyes of the Dark hound with all his strength.
The beast could track Dexter’s movement but just like the previous Dexter, it couldn’t react and could only watch as the blade stabbed into its left eye and straight to its skull.
[SES: Extracted +6 strength, +5 physique, + 3 Mana]
The beast froze and then collapsed in an instant.
"Ding!"
The notification barely registered but Dexter was already moving.
The two wounded Hounds from before already stood up. One was limping while the other was circling around him, snarling and circling, looking for an opening.
"Awooooo!"
"Awooooo!"
The two beasts actually let loose a loud howl. Dexter’s face couldn’t be more blacker.

He moved with incredible speed, slashing the throat of the first Dark Hound and using his momentum, he stabbed his blade through the skull of the second Dark Hound, pinning it to the wall like a decoration.
Hearing the howl, Dark Hounds began converging rapidly around the house.

Two level 6 burst through the kitchen window but before they could land, two emerald and almost invisible needle pin tore through the air like a bullet, heading for the nose of the first Dark hound and the second needle pin heading for the cheek of the second.
If hit, it will probably be non fatal. It was truly a bad throw.
But strangely, the needles changed trajectory in mid air and stabbed into the eyes of the Dark Hounds.
"Chi!" "Chi!"
[SES: Extracted +10 strength, +15 physique, + 3 Mana, +8 agility]
[Hidden Splinter Needle Hairpin]
[Grade]: Type 2 Relic
[Category]: Hidden Weapon
[Durability]: 100/100
[Attributes]
↳ Agility +10
[Passive Effects]
↳ Silent Flight
• Produces no sound and conceals its aura while in flight.
↳ Aimlock Accuracy.
• Auto correct throw path when targeting close to a fatal point.
[Active Skill]
↳ Ghost Needle
• Cooldown: 30 Seconds
• Throws the hairpin at tremendous speed.
• Ignores 40% of the target’s Physical Defense.
• Deals greatly increased damage when striking a vital point.
• Automatically returns to the user after the attack.
The two 6-Star beast collapsed on the kitchen floor, sliding forward due to the momentum of their lunge.
[Ding! You’ve leveled up to Tier 4]
Dexter didn’t care about the notification as another Dark Hound burst through the kitchen doorway. Then another at the destroyed front door.
He pulled the knife from the dead Hound’s neck and gripped it in his left hand, then picked up the broadsword beneath his feet.
The first Hound lunged.

Dexter didn’t try to dodge this time. He parried the claw strike with the broadsword as the impact sent vibrations up his arm, but Scorching Fury gave him the strength to hold his ground, then activated Flame Burst Step.
"Whoosh."
He vanished like a puff of smoke. One moment he was in front of the Hound, the next he was beside it, appearing so fast that the creature’s eyes couldn’t track him.
He slashed its head off clean.
The body dropped. The head rolled.

The second Hound came from behind. Dexter heard it and spun, bringing the broadsword around in a wide arc. The blade caught the Hound across the chest, cutting deep into its ribs. It yelped and stumbled back.
The third Hound attacked from the kitchen doorway. Dexter Flame Burst Stepped again, appearing to its left, and drove the knife into its eye. The creature shrieked and collapsed.

The fourth Hound hesitated but Dexter didn’t, in his anger, he lunged forward and attacked, his speed was fast and his momentum oppressive that the Mutated beast actually turned tail and ran but Dexter caught up with it, killing it in a two strikes.
The Dark Hound kept converging and Dexter was like a mad babarian, using everything in his asernal to kill. The more he kills the stringer he becomes!
By the time Hero’s from the Hero Association, Dark Hound corpses filled the entire house, both inside and outside of it.

"BOOM!"
A surge of energy struck him like a thunderbolt.
His blood literally ignited as his magma like blood flooded through every fiber of his body.
His muscles trembled and swelled as his strength increased by 50%!
His eyes seem to burn with flame, with his irises flickering with actual fire as his hair floated upward.
The Dark Hound struck at the bedroom door and its claw easily pierced a hole in the door.
One more strike and it would break through.
Dexter suddenly appeared beside the massive hound and thrust its two blade right through its neck.
"Ding!"
The Hound actually turned around so fast it slashed and parried the blade attack.
Dexter felt his arm trembled and he gritted his teeth.
The beast possess 150 agility stats and despite Dexter activating [Scorching Fury] his strength and agility capped at 112.5.
There was still a vast difference between the two of them!
Before he could react, the Dark Hound’s mouth opened so wide it could fit a watermelon blurred as it flashed towards him.
If he doesn’t move, his head will be chopped off!
But even with Scorching Fury his speed was still too slow to react to his head being bitten off.
Dexter’s eyes widened into a panic as he watched the maws of the Dark Hound Wrap around his head.
"Flame Burst!"
30 points of mana burned and Dexter’s feet released a blast of heat wave as Dexter’s agility increased by 300% for 1 second.
"Bang!"
Dexter watched as the massive mouth of the Dark hound slow down incredibly.
Dexter didn’t retreat, instead he turned towards the side of the beast.
Its mouth was still wide open but its eyes actually reacted to Dexter’s incredibly fast movement.
Dexter raised the knives and stabbed them directly through the eyes of the Dark hound with all his strength.
The beast could track Dexter’s movement but just like the previous Dexter, it couldn’t react and could only watch as the blade stabbed into its left eye and straight to its skull.
[SES: Extracted +6 strength, +5 physique, + 3 Mana]
The beast froze and then collapsed in an instant.
"Ding!"
The notification barely registered but Dexter was already moving.
The two wounded Hounds from before already stood up.
One was limping while the other was circling around him, snarling and circling, looking for an opening.
"Awooooo!"
"Awooooo!"
The two beasts actually let loose a loud howl.
Dexter’s face couldn’t be more blacker.

He moved with incredible speed, slashing the throat of the first Dark Hound and using his momentum, he stabbed his blade through the skull of the second Dark Hound, pinning it to the wall like a decoration.
Hearing the howl, Dark Hounds began converging rapidly around the house.

Two level 6 burst through the kitchen window but before they could land, two emerald and almost invisible needle pin tore through the air like a bullet, heading for the nose of the first Dark hound and the second needle pin heading for the cheek of the second.
If hit, it will probably be non fatal.
It was truly a bad throw.
But strangely, the needles changed trajectory in mid air and stabbed into the eyes of the Dark Hounds.
"Chi!" "Chi!"
[SES: Extracted +10 strength, +15 physique, + 3 Mana, +8 agility]
[Hidden Splinter Needle Hairpin]
[Grade]: Type 2 Relic
[Category]: Hidden Weapon
[Durability]: 100/100
[Attributes]
↳ Agility +10
[Passive Effects]
↳ Silent Flight
• Produces no sound and conceals its aura while in flight.
↳ Aimlock Accuracy.
• Auto correct throw path when targeting close to a fatal point.
[Active Skill]
↳ Ghost Needle
• Cooldown: 30 Seconds
• Throws the hairpin at tremendous speed.
• Ignores 40% of the target’s Physical Defense.
• Deals greatly increased damage when striking a vital point.
• Automatically returns to the user after the attack.
The two 6-Star beast collapsed on the kitchen floor, sliding forward due to the momentum of their lunge.
[Ding!
You’ve leveled up to Tier 4]
Dexter didn’t care about the notification as another Dark Hound burst through the kitchen doorway.
Then another at the destroyed front door.
He pulled the knife from the dead Hound’s neck and gripped it in his left hand, then picked up the broadsword beneath his feet.
The first Hound lunged.
Dexter didn’t try to dodge this time.
He parried the claw strike with the broadsword as the impact sent vibrations up his arm, but Scorching Fury gave him the strength to hold his ground, then activated Flame Burst Step.
"Whoosh."
He vanished like a puff of smoke.
One moment he was in front of the Hound, the next he was beside it, appearing so fast that the creature’s eyes couldn’t track him.
He slashed its head off clean.
The body dropped.
The head rolled.
The second Hound came from behind.
Dexter heard it and spun, bringing the broadsword around in a wide arc.
The blade caught the Hound across the chest, cutting deep into its ribs.
It yelped and stumbled back.
The third Hound attacked from the kitchen doorway.
Dexter Flame Burst Stepped again, appearing to its left, and drove the knife into its eye.
The creature shrieked and collapsed.

The fourth Hound hesitated but Dexter didn’t, in his anger, he lunged forward and attacked, his speed was fast and his momentum oppressive that the Mutated beast actually turned tail and ran but Dexter caught up with it, killing it in a two strikes.
The Dark Hound kept converging and Dexter was like a mad babarian, using everything in his asernal to kill.
The more he kills the stringer he becomes!
By the time Hero’s from the Hero Association, Dark Hound corpses filled the entire house, both inside and outside of it.

chapters.title: Chapter 19 | MASSIVE Rewards & 100x Upgrade!
paragraphs: Dexter stood in front of his gate.
Dark Hound corpses covered the ground around his house. A few still twitching in their final moments of death.
As the smell of blood filled the air with a faint smell of sulfur coming from Dexter’s body.
Right now, Dexter’s shirt was torn, revealing deep claw marks the 6-Star Hound had left on his back.
Blood was caked under his fingernails and his arms were streaked red from wrist to elbow.
In his left hand, was a steel rod he used to kill the last beast after the knife snapped inside a 5-Star’s skull.
From far away, the wail of emergency sirens cutting through the night, getting closer.

Heroes in proper combat gear were already engaging beasts in the streets and he could hear the crack of abilities activating, the crash of bodies hitting vehicles, the sharp reports of gunfire from the Association’s armed response units.
Dexter exhaled slowly. He let himself lean against the gate post as he breathed in.
He looked around the neighborhood. The fighting was concentrated on the eastern side of the street.
But here, on his side of the block, something didn’t add up.

Directly to his left, a blue house with a cracked driveway was untouched and also to his right, a cream-colored two-story with a garden fence was also untouched. Across the street, two more houses, the same thing.
Then he looked at Tessa’s house, the same thing too.
Dexter frowned as he stared at the four houses.
The Dark Hounds had swarmed this neighborhood like a flood.
But those four houses? Those surrounding his bungalow were not affected.
’What is this situation?’
It was like the beasts didn’t dare go near them.
They arrived 30 seconds later.
The Silver-rank response team moved through the neighborhood quickly dispatching the monsters around.
The team slowed as they approached Dexter’s yard. The house was almost thoroughly destroyed. With beast corpses in the kitchen, the yard and the living room.
There was blood everywhere, claw marks in the wall and the kitchen window destroyed.
And in the center of it all, was a young man, covered head to toe in blood.
The Silver-rank team leader was a tall woman in polished silver armor. Her eyes went from the corpses to Dexter. He was clearly a Tier 4 awakened. How had he killed a 6 star beast?
One of her team members leaned in and whispered something. The woman’s eyes widened slightly as she recognized who he was.
The bastard who married the cripple.
That guy did ’this’?
"You...did this?" she asked.
Dexter met her eyes. He was tired. His body was failing. But his voice came out flat and clear.
"Yes."
She stared at him for a long moment.
Then she brought her fist to her chest and saluted a hero’s salute that’s not meant for civilians.
Dexter blinked. He hadn’t expected that.
"Name?" she asked. "For the report."
"Dexter Ashford, awakened Hero. Tier 4."
"Get the medic over here," she called over her shoulder. "This man has a dozen open wounds."
The team medic rushed forward, already pulling supplies from his kit and started working on Dexter

The Hero Association secured the neighborhood within 20 minutes. The remaining Dark Hounds were either killed or driven back toward the breach zone, where higher-rank heroes were working to seal the Gate instability.
Dexter was escorted to a medical tent set up at the edge of the evacuation zone.
Finally alone, he opened his system notifications.
They’d been piling up for the last hour. He’d been too focused on survival, but now, in the silence of the tent, he let them flood in.
[Investment Multiplier System Activated]
[Investment Detected: Physical, Mental, Emotional, Security]
[Current Multiplier: 100x]
[Calculating Returns...]
[Return 1: Compressed Cultivation — One Year]
A wave of energy slammed into his chest. Dexter grunted in pain and pleasure as he grabbed the edge of the cot as mana flooded through his body.
His mana core expanded, his meridians widened, and he broke through to Tier 5, Tier 6, Tier 7 before the wave finally subsided.
[Return 2: Mana Affinity Upgraded — C-Rank → A-Rank]
Instantly, mana started to flow through him like water through an open pipe. The difference was staggering. He could feel mana in the air now without the need to concentrate and meditate.
It was everywhere, and for the first time, it was actually his to use.
[Return 3: Talent Upgraded — E-Rank → D-Rank (Enhanced Hearing)]
The range of his Enhanced Hearing doubled, and the clarity improved in ways he couldn’t quantify yet.
[Return 4: Bloodline Upgraded — Royal Grade → ORIGIN GRADE]
[New Bloodline: Berserk Flame Demon Bloodline (Origin Grade)]
Dexter’s eyes widened.
Top 100,000 bloodlines — Mutated Grade. Common people have this grade of bloodlines.
Top 10,000 — Royal Grade. It’s typically rare and Wealthy and powerful families built legacies on these.
Top 1,000 — Origin Grade. Had never been found.
And his had just jumped from Royal to Origin.
[Berserk Flame Demon Bloodline — Origin Grade]
[Passive: Fire Resistance increased to 50%. Flame Will now generates ambient heat that weakens nearby enemies.]
[Active: Scorching Fury — Strength increase upgraded from 50% to 80%. Duration extended to 5 minutes.]
[Active: Flame Burst Step — Speed increase upgraded from 300% to 500%. Duration extended to 2 seconds.]
[Active: NEW — Berserk Form — When health drops below 20%, enter a controlled rage state. All stats increase by 100%. Pain receptors shut down. Duration: 10 minutes. Cooldown: 48 hours.]
[Active: NEW — Flame Demon’s Wrath — Unleash a concentrated blast of demonic fire in a 15-meter radius. Damage scales with missing health. The less health you have, the more devastating the attack.]
[LOCKED: Flame Demon Transformation — Requires higher cultivation level to unlock.]
Dexter’s hands were trembling in pure happiness.
But that wasn’t all.
[Return 5: Culinary Rank Advanced — Rank 1 Master Chef → Rank 2 Grandmaster Chef (Early)]

[Effect: All meals prepared by host now contain strong special effects. Enchanted Meals will be significantly more potent. Meals can now actively accelerate healing, boost cultivation, and purify toxins.]
[Return 6: Martial Art Acquired — "Extreme Slaughtering Demon Body" (Tier 3)]

[Description: Transform mana into slaughter energy to temper the body. Progressively strengthens muscle fiber, bone density, and skin toughness through combat. Upon perfection, body becomes impervious to all weapons. Physique doubles. Power of any weapon used is doubled.]
[Return 7: Grade 3 Restoration Pill ×1]
[Effect: Randomly heals a single injury in the body. Can restore damaged nerves, fractured bones, or severed meridians. One-time use.]
Dexter’s heart stopped. "Restore damaged nerves." His mind immediately went to his three wives. But he only had one pill.
[Return 8: Type 3 Macro-Splicing Saber
Macro-Splicing Saber
Relic Grade: Type 3
Category: Saber
Durability: 300/300
Attributes
+35 Strength
+25 Agility
+20 Vitality
Special Effects
• Macro-Splice
Slices through large targets with unnatural precision. Greatly increases damage against armored enemies, fortifications, and colossal monsters.
• Spatial Cleave
The blade releases a compressed crescent slash that travels up to 25 meters before dissipating.
• Structural Severance
Attacks identify and exploit structural weak points, reducing an enemy’s defense by 30% for 5 seconds.
• Edge of Ruin
Each consecutive strike increases blade sharpness and damage by 8%, stacking up to 5 times.
• Relic Rend
Deals 40% bonus damage against relic armor, magical barriers, and summoned constructs.
Ultimate Skill
◆ Macro Dissection

Consumes a large amount of mana to unleash a single overwhelming slash. Everything within a 50-meter line is cut apart on the molecular and magical level, ignoring 60% of physical defense and destroying weaker barriers instantly.
Passive
• Unbreaking Edge
The saber never dulls and automatically repairs minor damage over time.
A real weapon. A Type 3 weapon. The kind of relic that Silver and Gold-rank heroes spent fortunes to acquire.
[Return 9: Type 3 Protective Amulet]
[Effect: Wearer receives a passive barrier that absorbs damage up to Peak Super Hero Regenerates over 24 hours after breaking.]
[Return 10: Type 3 House Protection Talisman]

[Effect: When placed on a dwelling, creates a barrier that repels all entities below Superhero Rank at will. Monsters and hostile individuals below this threshold cannot invade the protected area. Duration: Permanent until destroyed.]
Dexter stared at that last one. A permanent house barrier. The kind of protection that would have stopped the Dark Hounds from ever reaching his door.
If only he’d had it a week ago.
[Return 11: D-Rank Talent Card — "Echo-Location"]

[Effect: Emits high-frequency sound pulses that create a three-dimensional map of the surrounding environment. The user can perceive terrain, walls, obstacles, moving targets, and hidden objects even in complete darkness or through smoke, fog, and similar visual obstructions.
[Return 12: D-Rank Talent Card — "Mana Arms"]
[Effect: Construct up to 4 additional arms using solidified mana. Each arm has 10% of user’s physical strength. Duration scales with mana reserves.]
[Return 13: D-Rank Talent Card — "Telepathy"]
[Effect: Speak directly into the minds of others. Can also read the surface thoughts of individuals whose cultivation level is below the user’s.]
Four extra arms. Telepathy. Ground-based sonar. These are the things that could assist his wives!
[Return 14: Type 3 Chain Pain Ring]
[Effect: Temporarily transfer any ill effect, status condition, or debuff from the user to a target. Can also be used in reverse]
[10,000x Investment Multiplier System— Upgrade Notification]
[Confirmed Kills: 16/100]
[Threshold reached: 10 kills]
[Multiplier Tier UP: 10x → 100x]
[All future Investment returns will now be calculated at 100x multiplier.]
[Kills remaining until next upgrade (1,000x): 84]
"This is slightly too much."
