chapters.title: Chapter 20 | Silent Treatment
paragraphs: "This is slightly too much."
Not only had he advanced by leaps and bounds, he also got Talent cards that could assist his wives and improve their living situation!
Mira is paralyzed and can’t move but with the Mana Hands, she could use the mana hands to do a few things.
Lyra can’t hear and speak but with the telepathy ability card she could speak directly timings kind and hear their outward thoughts. It was basically the same thing as being cured.
Finally, Selene. With the Echolocation talent card, she could see vibrations and map out the surrounding areas within 10 meters!
These abilities to others might be worthless but to his girls, they were everything.
Not to mention his investment had increased from 10 times to over 100 times!
His strength would be truly terrifying from now on.
Every investment he made from this point forward, would return one hundred times what it would have at base. He exhaled a turbid air and opened his eyes.
"Weng!"
Flames seem to dance around his eyes as he looked around with new found clarity.
Eighty-four more kills was the next upgrade.
A healer came to the tent.
She was a middle-aged woman with blue eyes. She smiled when she saw him.
Her Talent was called Healing Hands, and when she pressed her palms against the claw marks on Dexter’s back, a warm golden light seeped into his skin.
The deep wound slowly began to heal rapidly at a speed visible to the naked eyes and then the pain gradually vanished until there was nothing left.
The exhaustion that had been weighing on his bones since he canceled out Scorching Fury bloodline skill also vanished.
Dexter rotated his shoulder experimentally, there was not a single pain.
"Rest up a few hours and you will be good as new." She packed her things and turned to leave.
Dexter didn’t respond. He was watching through the tent flap as Association workers hauled the Dark Hound carcasses onto transport vehicles.
They were taking everything. Dexter pursed his lips. He hadn’t remember to take the nexus fire if the beast.

Nexus cores are crystallized mana essence inside each beast’s heart and was very valuable — both for cultivation and for the money they’d fetch on the open market. Sixteen beasts meant sixteen cores. At market rate, that was enough to live on for months.
But it was too late. The Association had already claimed jurisdiction over the entire outbreak site.
One of the Association officers approached him — a neat man in a pressed uniform holding a clipboard.

"Mr. Ashford. You and your dependents will be transported to a nearby hotel. Fully paid for by the Hero Association. You’ll stay there for a minimum of three days while we repair the damages done to your home and monitor the neighborhood for residual Gate instability."
Dexter nodded and sighed in relief. He didn’t have the money for repairs right now.

"Someone from the Hero Association will come to meet you at the hotel in a few days regarding the beast carcass and your housing repairs." The officer paused, then added with a small nod of respect. "Thank you for your service."
"You’re welcome."
Dexter replied.
A black limousine pulled up outside the tent twenty minutes later.

Association staff loaded Dexter’s things, not that there was much. A few changes of clothes, the leftover food supplies, Selene’s medication, and the small case containing the old Type 1 bracelets and AI glasses he’d replaced. It all fit in two bags.

Two men assisted his wives into the vehicle. One guided Mira’s wheelchair into the spacious back compartment, securing it against the floor mounts. Another helped Lyra who helped Selene to the vehicle.
Dexter watched from outside the limousine.

He looked at his three wives as they settled into the leather seats. Mira’s eyes were forward, her expression closed. Lyra sat quietly, her hands folded, her new AI glasses dark. Selene was still, her face turned slightly away.
He clenched his fists at his sides.
The anger was still there. It had been burning in his chest since the outbreak. Since the moment Lyra had walked toward the door, waiting for death like the other girls.
They hadn’t struggled, not once. They just sat there and waited to die.
He huffed and got into the limousine. The door closed behind him with a soft thud.
The limousine pulled away from the tent, leaving the ruined neighborhood behind. Through the tinted windows, Dexter watched the street pass, Association vehicles with flashing lights.
The city was already recovering. People were already moving on.
He leaned his head against the window and said nothing. The atmosphere was incredibly awkward and thick with tension.
Mira suddenly opened her eyes as though she could feel his anger pressing against her skin.
Her lips crisped into a knowing smile and she closed her eyes again.
Lyra felt it too and she too turned to look at Dexter through her smart glasses before looking away.
Selene remained still but she shifted uncomfortably on the seat.

The hotel was called the Grand Meridian. It was the kind of place Dexter had only ever seen in movies. Marble floors, crystal chandeliers, and uniformed staff who acted like they’d been trained in a military academy for hospitality.
At the front desk, the clerk asked if Dexter wanted connecting rooms.
"No, separate rooms." he replied.

The clerk checked his system and shook his head. "I’m sorry, sir. We’re at capacity due to the monster outbreak evacuation. The only available unit is a premium suite with a single bedroom. It has a very large bed — more than enough to accommodate four guests." He glanced past Dexter at the three women behind him. There was a flash of jealousy in his eyes but he quickly hid it.
Dexter’s frowned. He didn’t want to stay in the same room with the girls but now, he had no choice.
"I’ll take it."
The clerk handed him the key card. "Twentieth floor. Elevator’s to your left."

sentences.text: "This is slightly too much."
Not only had he advanced by leaps and bounds, he also got Talent cards that could assist his wives and improve their living situation!
Mira is paralyzed and can’t move but with the Mana Hands, she could use the mana hands to do a few things.
Lyra can’t hear and speak but with the telepathy ability card she could speak directly timings kind and hear their outward thoughts.
It was basically the same thing as being cured.
Finally, Selene.
With the Echolocation talent card, she could see vibrations and map out the surrounding areas within 10 meters!
These abilities to others might be worthless but to his girls, they were everything.
Not to mention his investment had increased from 10 times to over 100 times!
His strength would be truly terrifying from now on.
Every investment he made from this point forward, would return one hundred times what it would have at base.
He exhaled a turbid air and opened his eyes.
"Weng!"
Flames seem to dance around his eyes as he looked around with new found clarity.
Eighty-four more kills was the next upgrade.
A healer came to the tent.
She was a middle-aged woman with blue eyes.
She smiled when she saw him.
Her Talent was called Healing Hands, and when she pressed her palms against the claw marks on Dexter’s back, a warm golden light seeped into his skin.
The deep wound slowly began to heal rapidly at a speed visible to the naked eyes and then the pain gradually vanished until there was nothing left.
The exhaustion that had been weighing on his bones since he canceled out Scorching Fury bloodline skill also vanished.
Dexter rotated his shoulder experimentally, there was not a single pain.
"Rest up a few hours and you will be good as new." She packed her things and turned to leave.
Dexter didn’t respond.
He was watching through the tent flap as Association workers hauled the Dark Hound carcasses onto transport vehicles.
They were taking everything.
Dexter pursed his lips.
He hadn’t remember to take the nexus fire if the beast.
Nexus cores are crystallized mana essence inside each beast’s heart and was very valuable — both for cultivation and for the money they’d fetch on the open market.
Sixteen beasts meant sixteen cores.
At market rate, that was enough to live on for months.
But it was too late.
The Association had already claimed jurisdiction over the entire outbreak site.
One of the Association officers approached him — a neat man in a pressed uniform holding a clipboard.
"Mr.
Ashford.
You and your dependents will be transported to a nearby hotel.
Fully paid for by the Hero Association.
You’ll stay there for a minimum of three days while we repair the damages done to your home and monitor the neighborhood for residual Gate instability."
Dexter nodded and sighed in relief.
He didn’t have the money for repairs right now.
"Someone from the Hero Association will come to meet you at the hotel in a few days regarding the beast carcass and your housing repairs." The officer paused, then added with a small nod of respect.
"Thank you for your service."
"You’re welcome."
Dexter replied.
A black limousine pulled up outside the tent twenty minutes later.
Association staff loaded Dexter’s things, not that there was much.
A few changes of clothes, the leftover food supplies, Selene’s medication, and the small case containing the old Type 1 bracelets and AI glasses he’d replaced.
It all fit in two bags.
Two men assisted his wives into the vehicle.
One guided Mira’s wheelchair into the spacious back compartment, securing it against the floor mounts.
Another helped Lyra who helped Selene to the vehicle.
Dexter watched from outside the limousine.
He looked at his three wives as they settled into the leather seats.
Mira’s eyes were forward, her expression closed.
Lyra sat quietly, her hands folded, her new AI glasses dark.
Selene was still, her face turned slightly away.
He clenched his fists at his sides.
The anger was still there.
It had been burning in his chest since the outbreak.
Since the moment Lyra had walked toward the door, waiting for death like the other girls.
They hadn’t struggled, not once.
They just sat there and waited to die.
He huffed and got into the limousine.
The door closed behind him with a soft thud.
The limousine pulled away from the tent, leaving the ruined neighborhood behind.
Through the tinted windows, Dexter watched the street pass, Association vehicles with flashing lights.
The city was already recovering.
People were already moving on.
He leaned his head against the window and said nothing.
The atmosphere was incredibly awkward and thick with tension.
Mira suddenly opened her eyes as though she could feel his anger pressing against her skin.
Her lips crisped into a knowing smile and she closed her eyes again.
Lyra felt it too and she too turned to look at Dexter through her smart glasses before looking away.
Selene remained still but she shifted uncomfortably on the seat.
The hotel was called the Grand Meridian.
It was the kind of place Dexter had only ever seen in movies.
Marble floors, crystal chandeliers, and uniformed staff who acted like they’d been trained in a military academy for hospitality.
At the front desk, the clerk asked if Dexter wanted connecting rooms.
"No, separate rooms." he replied.

"I’m sorry, sir.
We’re at capacity due to the monster outbreak evacuation.
The only available unit is a premium suite with a single bedroom.
It has a very large bed — more than enough to accommodate four guests." He glanced past Dexter at the three women behind him.
There was a flash of jealousy in his eyes but he quickly hid it.

He didn’t want to stay in the same room with the girls but now, he had no choice.

Elevator’s to your left."

chapters.title: Chapter 21 | Unexpected Kiss
paragraphs: The elevator doors slid open onto the twentieth floor.

Without a word, Dexter wheeled Mira out into the quiet hallway. The carpet was thick and soft beneath the wheels, swallowing all sound. B ehind them, Lyra gently held Selene’s hand, guiding her slowly as they stepped out of the elevator together.
The four of them walked in complete and heavy silence.
So he stayed silent.
Mira seemed to sense his mood. Every now and then she stole a glance at him from her wheelchair, her lips parting slightly as though she wanted to say something. But the words never came.
Lyra noticed it too. She occasionally looked at him through her smart glasses before quietly lowering her dark eyes again.
No one spoke.
They reached the suite. Dexter unlocked the door and pushed it open.

The room was luxurious — far beyond anything any of them had lived in recently. A spacious living room with elegant sofas, a polished dining table, and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the city lights below.
A marble bathroom with a bathtub big enough for two. And beyond the living room, a single large bedroom with a bed that was, as promised, enormous.
Without saying anything, Dexter wheeled Mira inside and positioned her near the window. He walked into the bedroom, examined the layout, checked the locks on the windows and other stuffs.
Satisfied, he walked back into the living room and picked up the room service phone.

He ordered dinner for everyone, selecting dishes he thought each of them would enjoy based on what he’d observed over the past week. Mira liked rich, flavorful broths. Lyra ate enormous portions but preferred simple, hearty food. Selene hadn’t shown strong preferences, but she seemed to respond well to warm, soft meals.
Less than twenty minutes later, a staff member arrived with a cart covered in silver plates.
"Here."
Dexter tipped him a 10, then heeled the cart to the dining table, and uncovered each dish carefully, arranging them neatly.
"You should eat while it’s still warm," he said flatly.
Without waiting for a response, Dexter turned and walked toward the door.
There was a perfectly comfortable sofa in the living room. He’d intended to sleep there tonight.
But not yet.
The elevator carried him back down to the lobby.
Earlier, when they’d checked in, he’d noticed a small bar tucked into one corner of the ground floor. Warm amber lighting with wood and the faint sound of jazz drifting through the entrance.
The bar wasn’t crowded, but it wasn’t empty either.
Businessmen in loosened ties, a couple sharing a quiet drink, a few weary travelers staring at their phones.
Dexter ignored everyone, took an empty stool at the far end of the counter, and let out a long, slow breath.
The bartender approached with a friendly smile. "What can I get you?
Dexter stared at the rows of bottles for a moment.
He hadn’t had a drink in weeks. Before the marriage, alcohol had been his way of surviving the Ashford estate.

He’d been an alcoholic, though he rarely admitted it to himself. He’d quit mostly because he couldn’t afford it anymore. Then the system appeared, his wives, and somewhere along the way, he’d simply forgotten that alcohol existed.
"Whiskey," he said quietly. "Neat."
"Coming right up."
A few moments later, the bartender placed a crystal tumbler before him.
Dexter wrapped his fingers around the glass then took a slow sip.
The whiskey burned its way down his throat, warming his chest almost instantly.
He closed his eyes.
"Sigh...I really missed this."
It has been a while truly.
Suddenly, something shifted beside him.
"How long has it been?"
Voice like a thousand mystical Sirens. The feminine voice sounded out from beside him.

Dexter opened his eyes and glanced to his left. A beautiful woman sat two stools away, dark hair cascading over one shoulder, vivid green eyes watching him with quiet amusement. She looked really elegant.
Dexter blinked and then glanced over his shoulder. But there was no one there.
When he looked back, she covered her mouth and chuckled lightly.
Realization dawned, and he gave a slightly embarrassed smile. "You were talking to me?"
She chuckled. "I’d be a weirdo talking to ghosts if I wasn’t."
Dexter rubbed the back of his neck. "Sorry. Just been stressed out a lot. What were you asking?"
The lady nodded her head and pointed at his glass.
Dexter understood what she meant and replied. "Oh. It’s been three weeks i took a drink last."
She raised her own glass, something pink and fruity. "Mine is 16 hours ."
Dexter bursted out laughing, making the girl laugh too.
She extended a hand. "Rachel."
He shook it. "Dexter.
"Nice to meet you."
"You too."
They both took another sip.
"So," she said, turning slightly on her stool to face him. "What happened today to make you break?"
Dexter stared into his whiskey before giving a dry chuckle. "Family."
She laughed softly. "That bad?"
"It’s... complicated." He looked at her. "What about you?"
She sighed dramatically and raised her glass. "Business."
Dexter blinked. "Business?"
"Yeah. Business has been hectic and dangerous lately."
He shook his head and toasted with her. "To life."
"To tough life."
They smiled and drank up.
Before either of them realized it, the conversation began to flow naturally.
They talked about work stress, about how adulthood somehow became exhausting overnight and how money became the most important things.
Minutes slipped by, the drinks came and went. Dexter switched from whiskey to something lighter. Rachel ordered something sweeter. The jazz played on. The bar slowly emptied around them.
For the first time that day, maybe for the first time in weeks, Dexter smiled without forcing it.
The conversation gradually slowed, Rachel found herself looking at him differently now, a bit warmer.
More specifically, she found herself looking at his lips.
Dexter noticed her gaze linger for a fraction of a second. But was a little tipsy, so he dismissed it.
"I really need to turn in," Rachel said, gathering her purse. "I’ve got a meeting early tomorrow."
Dexter smiled. "It’s been fun."
And he meant it. In the span of an hour, this stranger had made him feel more like a normal human being than anything had in the past three weeks.
She locked her eyes with his and it seemed magnetic. "It’s been fun," she replied.
Then she suddenly leaned forward and kissed him!

chapters.title: Chapter 22 | Extreme Slaughter Demon Body
paragraphs: Dexter woke up before dawn and let out a long yawn. He was halfway out of bed, his brain already running a checklist for the kitchen, before he caught himself. He wasn’t at the bungalow. There was no rice to wash, and no breakfast to scramble together for the girls.
Instead, he was staring at a fancy ceiling, in a hotel room that cost more per night than he used to make in a month.
Right. The Grand Meridian.
They were still stuck here. The monster outbreak had turned their neighborhood into a graveyard, and the Hero Association had put them here.
"Sigh. I could get used to this, right?" He smiled as he muttered.
He glanced at the clock on the nightstand.
The room was silent, filled only with the hum of the air conditioner and the soft breathing of the three women in the massive bed behind him.
He felt a sudden, twitchy need to be busy.
Usually, every morning he was always busy by this time, Chopping vegetables, planning meals, but here, thwre was nothing to do.
Since sleep was a lost cause, he sat up on the couch and shook off the grogginess. He needed to be more Productive.
He closed his eyes and started the Starlight Meditation Technique.
A week ago, his mana affinity had been so low that trying to use it was like trying to drink water through a solid straw. He mostly did it back then just to keep calm his mind.
But things were different now. His affinity had jumped all the way to A-Rank, and the difference was like night and day.
The moment he triggered the technique, the mana in the room seemed to rush toward him. His body drank it up, his core filling like a dry basin under a waterfall.
So fast.
He kept his eyes shut, trying to keep his composure, but he was genuinely shocked. If he kept this up, he’d be able to stabilize his Tier 7 strength in no time.
After a few minutes of feeling that energy hum through his system, his mind drifted to the other thing he’d been putting off: the Demon Tempering Body Technique.
He’d gotten it as a reward, but he hadn’t had a second of privacy to actually try it out.
He stood up, gave his neck a quick crack, and cleared some space by pushing the coffee table aside.
The instructions were simple enough: 108 forms, extreme stress, and specific mana paths.
How hard could it be?
He kicked his legs up into a headstand, trying to twist his body into the required shape.
The first form was an absolute nightmare.
It was like someone had taken the worst parts of yoga and combined them with a medieval torture device.
"Aarhus is really difficult." Dexter grunted as he tired practicing the technique.
His hips screamed in protest, his spine felt like it was being twisted like a wet towel, and he had to keep his mana moving through twelve specific points at the exact same time.
He lasted ten seconds. Then fifteen. By twenty, his arms were shaking so hard he thought he might shatter his own floor.
He collapsed.
"Damn..." he wheezed, flat on his back, his shirt already soaked through with sweat.
[Ding!]
[Extreme Slaughtering Demon Body — Form 1: Complete]
[Strength Increased: +1%]
He stared at the ceiling, feeling like a fool, until the notification popped up. He sat up, blinking at the blue text hanging in the air.
"...Seriously?"
Twenty seconds of feeling like his bones were being rearranged, and he’d gained a full percent of raw strength. That was insane. If he kept this up, he’d be a monster in a few weeks.
Then he looked at his mana bar.
Half of it was gone. Just like that.
The technique didn’t just train his muscles; it was literally burning his mana to build them. That was a hell of a price to pay.
"This thing is terrifying," he muttered.
He wasn’t going to get any more training in without passing out, so he grabbed a fresh shirt and decided to head outside. The walls were starting to close in on him. He needed a run.

The hotel grounds were massive with green tall, grasses, leading the path and sculptures at the entrance. Dexter jogged along the perimeter, letting the cold morning air hit his face, burning off the restless energy that had been coiling in his gut for days.
He rounded a corner near the back garden, intending to finish another lap, when he saw something.
Five floors up, an old man was standing on a premium suite balcony.
He looked like any other retired guy in a tank top, white hair pulled into a messy knot, moving through some kind of slow-motion workout.
He was graceful, smooth, fluid, like he was moving through water as he practiced.

chapters.title: Chapter 23 | The Old Man!!
paragraphs: Dexter was about to keep jogging when his system pinged.
[Ding!]
[Slaughter Extraction System — Target Detected]
[Analyzing 7th Tier Grade Technique in progress...]
[Would you like to continue analysis? Remain within observation range.]
Dexter froze.
7th tier?
He’d never even heard of a 7-th grade anything. Those were the kinds of things that could cause an entire war, and here was some guy, doing it on a balcony at 4:00 AM like it was a morning stretch.
Without thinking, Dexter backwd up to a tree, keeping his eyes locked on the balcony.
The old man didn’t seem to notice. He just kept moving, shifting his weight, breathing in sync with movements that looked simple but clearly weren’t.
Dexter’s system started pulling data, mapping out the weird way the old man’s mana was circulating through his meridians.
Ten minutes. Then twenty. The old man finished with a long, slow exhale, wiped his face, and ducked back inside.
[Analysis Progress: 5%]
Only five percent?
He let out a frustrated huff.
At this rate, he’d have to live in these bushes for a week to get the whole thing.
He looked up at the empty balcony.
Every day, he thought.Every chance I get. I’m taking this.
The rest of the morning was a dull slog. Dexter went back upstairs, took care of the girls, and played his part in the quiet, awkward routine they’d fallen into.
But his head wasn’t in the room. He kept finding excuses to slip out, checking the balcony from the garden, from the lobby, from the window of the suite.
Finally, in the late afternoon, he saw movement.
He bolted for the back garden, hid behind a hedge, and watched. The old man practiced for another thirty minutes, his movements shifting, becoming more complex.
[Analysis Progress: 11%]
Still not enough. It was driving him crazy. He couldn’t exactly knock on the door and ask for a private lesson this guy was clearly a powerhouse.
He was stuck playing the long game.
Night hit. Back in the suite, Dexter was doing the usual thing—helping Mira from her wheelchair to the bathroom when he saw she was stained red.
She was in her period!
He went bright red. He couldn’t help it.
Mira just stared at him, then let out a dry laugh.
"Why are you so red? I’m the one who should be red aren’t I."
Dexter’s jaw set. He didn’t say a word. So he went inside picked a pad and fixed it to a panties and helped her in it.
Then took her where she needed to go and walked out to the living room.

He was still angry. He was still bitter. And the way she’d teased him didn’t make it better; it just made things feel weird. He could feel Selene and Lyra watching him from the bedroom, but he didn’t care either.
He’d had enough. He grabbed the room key and walked out the door, needing to get away from the suffocating quiet.
At 7:00 PM, he was back at his post.
The old man was there again, moving through the same strange, fluid forms. Dexter watched, focused, as the system worked its magic.
[Analysis Progress: 17%]
When the old man went inside, Dexter sighed and turned to leave. He didn’t see the old man pause at the glass door, watching him with a sharp, amused glint in his eyes.
Inside the suite, a young woman’s voice drifted out.
"Grandfather... are you intentionally teaching that boy?"
The old man stroked his beard, looking down at the empty garden.
"No."
The girl arched an eyebrow.
He chuckled.

He shrugged.
"Then he’s not worth the worry."

The suite was quiet, but as he sat there, he heard it, tiny, jagged spikes of mana.
He focused.
It was as if someone was cultivating.
’Are the girls cultivating in the bedroom?’
If they truly are cultivating with shattered meridians, it would be incredibly painful!
Just like trying to force water through a rusted pipe. It hurt, it was dangerous, and their progress was probably almost zero.
They should have been resting. But they were sitting there, pushing through the agony, trying to put themselves back together.
’Have they changed?’Dexter shook his head and smiled, he felt it as ridiculous. They wouldn’t give up on killing themsolves just like that.
He went to say something, but he stopped.
Tomorrow, he thought.We’ll deal with tomorrow.
He laid back, closed his eyes, and drifted off to the sound of them fighting for every inch of progress.
The next morning, it was 7:00 AM, and the old man was already out there.
Dexter was back, eyes locked on the balcony.

The old man raised a finger.
Come here.

The old man rolled his eyes, took a breath, and just stepped off the balcony.
Five stories.
Dexter eyes popped open, but the old man didn’t hit the ground like a sack of bricks. He landed like he was stepping off a curb—no sound, no impact, just a light tap of his sandals.
He walked over to the hedge, looking at Dexter with with a dangerous smile.

"Interesting," he said, his voice sounding like gravel. He looked Dexter up and down, and for a second, Dexter felt like he was being X-rayed. "A mere C-Rank affinity... and yet, you’re trying to steal my technique."
The old man’s smile went cold. The air suddenly felt like it was pressing down on Dexter’s shoulders.
"Tell me, boy," the old man whispered. "Are you not afraid of dying?"

chapters.title: Chapter 24 | We’re Sorry!
paragraphs: "Tell me, boy..."
"Are you not afraid of dying?"

Dexter eyes blinked as he felt a weight landed on his shoulder. Even with his strength, he felt his knee almost buckling and an illusion of an angry god with blue burning flames appeared behind the man.
Dexter throat perched and he opened his mouth,
But before a single word could leave his lips —
His expression changed instantly.
A sudden sharp sensation shot through his mind. It was like an ice pick driving deep into his skull. His Frost Sense, the ability that connected him to Selene’s unique energy.
Selene.
She was having another episode.
Dexter’s pupils contracted. His entire body went rigid for half a second. The old man noticed the change immediately but said nothing, only watching with curious eyes.
Without even bothering to answer the old man’s question, Dexter abruptly turned around.
"Please stay here. I’ll be right back."
And then like the pressure the old man was putting on him was nothing more than paper weight—
He vanished.
BOOM!
His body exploded forward with terrifying speed. The floor tiles beneath his previous position cracked from the sudden release of force.
Using Flame Burst, Dexter shot through the hotel pathways like a meteor. The mana around his legs combusted and propelled him forward in violent bursts.

The polished hotel corridors became a blur around him. Golden wall lamps streaked past like lines of fire. Several customers walking nearby only felt a gust of scorching wind sweep past them. One woman’s dress fluttered wildly. A man’s hat flew off his head and tumbled down the hallway.
They froze in shock, their eyes wide and mouths hanging open.
"What was that?!" one of them shouted.

But Dexter was already gone. He ignored everything. The surprised gasps, the confused shouts, all of it faded into background noise. He pushed more mana into Flame Burst. The technique roared to life with even greater intensity. His body accelerated even faster. The air around him rippled with heat.
His Brain rapidly process things and he realized the elevator would be too slow.
He immediately changed direction and sprinted straight for the stairway. His right shoulder slammed into the stairwell door, bursting it open without slowing down.
His footsteps struck the stairs like explosions.
Bang. Bang. Bang. Bang.
In seconds—
He reached the hotel room.
BANG!
And the moment Dexter stepped inside, cold air slammed into his face like a wall. The temperature had dropped so low that his skin prickled with frost.
The room had turned into an ice chamber.

Frost covered the walls in thick white layers. The windows were frozen solid, completely with ice crystals spreading in spiral patterns. The carpet crunched under his boots. The entire bed was buried under layers of ice crystals that glittered in the dim light.
And on top of the bed—
Selene was convulsing violently.

Her entire body trembled uncontrollably as freezing energy leaked from her skin in visible waves. Her face was pale as death. Her lips were blue. Her fingers clawed at the frozen sheets. Frost spread outward from her body with every convulsion, creeping across the bed and up the walls.
At the side of the bed sat Mira in her wheelchair.
Beside her was Lyra, her smart glasses resting over her eyes. The AI writing the sounds it could hear to the best of its abilities.
Both girls stared at Selene with furrowed brows, worry evident on their faces.
Dexter acted instantly.
His right hand erupted into crimson flames. The fire roared to life, casting dancing shadows across the frozen walls.

The Berserk Flame Demon Bloodline activated fully, flooding his veins with lava. The flames rapidly melted the thick ice covering parts of the room. Steam immediately rose into the air, filling the space with a thick fog.
Without hesitation, Dexter reached into his pocket and pulled out the Suppressant Serum, took her arm and injected the serum and injected the liquid into her bloodstream.
Slowly, the violent shaking stopped. Selene’s convulsing body gradually relaxed. Her breathing, turned soft as the frost spreading throughout the room began receding, pulling back toward her body.
She fell asleep. Her face, which had been twisted in pain, softened into peace.
Dexter exhaled deeply
"That was too close..."
He activated his bloodline further and heatwaves spread through the room in turning the remaining frost into water mad then into steam.
Within moments, the bed had completely dried and the temperature turned normal.
Dexter carefully covered Selene with several thick blankets. He tucked the edges around her shoulders.
He paused as he at her stunning face, her silver hair spread out across the bed.
She looked both angelic and also fragile buried under all that fabric.
Suddenly, her eyes fluttered open. And she looked directly at Dexter.
For a moment, his breath caught in his throat.
But he then relaxed when he remembered she was blind. But she definitely knew he was still there.
He inhaled and left the bed to turn to Mira and Lyra.
Both girls were staring at him silently with an unreadable expression.
The room fell silent for several seconds
Finally, Dexter spoke. His voice was calm but flat.
"If you two are hungry... I can call room service. I can order food for you."
Mira quietly shook her head. "I’m not hungry."
Lyra’s glasses flickered. The words automatically displayed across the lenses. Strangely the foodie Lyra also shook her head.
Dexter raised an eyebrow in surprise. She had almost finished the entire hotel’s food this morning and afternoon, what’s wrong now?
He didn’t bother to ask, he turned around, preparing to leave. The old man was still waiting downstairs.
But suddenly—
A very soft voice sounded behind him. So soft he almost thought he imagined it.
"...We’re sorry."
Dexter froze. His hand stopped just before reaching the door handle. For a long moment, he did not move. He did not even breathe. The words echoed in his mind, repeating over and over.
He slowly turned around. His expression was unreadable. His voice was quiet, careful.
"What did you say?"
Then—
Lyra spoke again. This time louder. Her voice was still soft, but there was strength behind it now. A strength that had not been there before.
"We’re sorry."
Dexter stood still. He looked at Lyra. Then at Mira. Both girls were looking at him directly. Not avoiding his gaze.
’Did I hear wrong? ’
For a moment, he genuinely thought he had misheard.
He had been cold towards them throughout their stay here since they didn’t care for him nor themselves, he would only take care of them, earn rewards from the system and grow stronger.
After all, they had also remained silent toward him. They had not tried to bridge the gap. So what changed?
Then Mira lowered her head. Her dark hair fell forward as she spoke quietly.
"We are sorry... for everything. And... thank you."
The words made Dexter emotional than he had he’d preferred to be.
Inside him, countless emotions surged at once, like a dam breaking. All the feelings he had suppressed came flooding back.
He wanted to complain. He wanted to yell. He wanted to ask them why they gave up so easily.
He wanted to remind them how lucky they were. They had lived normal lives for years before losing everything. They had seen the sky. They had walked on their own feet. They had experienced the world.

Meanwhile, some people were born blind. Some were born crippled. Some were born deaf. Some never once had the chance to experience life properly, not even for a single day. He wanted to say all of that. He wanted to make them understand how precious their lives were.
But somehow—
Those simple words erased all his anger.

chapters.title: Chapter 25 | The Bet With The Strange Old Man
paragraphs: "You’re welcome."
The tension in the room finally disappeared.
Dexter rubbed the back of his head awkwardly making the corner of Mira’s mouth twitch upward.
"There’s something I need to do," Dexter said. "I’ll be back soon."
Mira suddenly smirked.
"Oh? Do you have another wife hiding somewhere?"
For the first time in two days, Dexter laughed at her banter.
He crossed his arms and raised an eyebrow. "Are you jealous?"
Mira snorted coldly but her eyes were brighter now. "Please."
At the side, a faint smile tugged at Lyra’s usually cold lips.
Seeing their expressions, Dexter felt unexpectedly relieved.
"I will be back in a bit. Don’t open the door for anyone other then me."
The girls nodded their heads.
Without wasting another second, he left the room. The door clicked shut behind him.
Outside, the old man was still standing exactly where Dexter had left him. Not a single inch moved. His posture was straight. His hands were clasped behind his back.
Dexter jogged over and wiped sweat from his forehead. His breathing was slightly heavy from the sprint.
The old man stared at him sharply.
Then said flatly, "You actually left me standing here."
Dexter scratched his head awkwardly.
’I had to save one of my wives.’ but he didn’t say that.
"It was... a matter of life and death."
The old man stared for several seconds. His expression was difficult to read. Then he nodded slowly. "I see."
Suddenly, the old man tilted his head.
"Let us make a deal."
Dexter blinked. A deal? "What kind of deal?"
The old man smiled faintly. "If you manage to learn my technique for the duration of your stay here, I shall give you a gift."
Dexter’s expression shifted. A slight furrow on his brow. Bur internally he was laughing like a mad man.
’This old man doesn’t know what he’s walking into! Hahahaha!’
Externally, he sighed and puffed out his chest.
"As long as you repeatedly demonstrate the technique," Dexter said, "I can learn it in one day."
The old man froze and his eyes widened slightly. He had expected the boy to say a month. Maybe longer, wanting to play with his new toy...But a day?
"One day?" The old man’s voice was sharp with disbelief.
Dexter nodded firmly. "One day."

Sddenly the old man laughed loudly. "Hahaha. Arrogant, simple arrogant! The most talented take years to learn and you want to learn it in one day? Interesting. Very interesting." He stroked his long gray beard.
"Fine. I’ll raise the stakes."
Dexter leaned forward slightly, curious.

"If you can truly learn my technique in one day, I won’t simply give you an ordinary gift." His eyes gleamed with excitement. "I will give you a treasure and not only that, I shall let you marry my granddaughter."
Dexter’s eyes widened slightly. A treasure from a powerhouse would definitely be powerful.
But the old man wasn’t done. He raised a single finger.
But then the granddaughter part made Dexter shake his head.
’I already have three women and they are giving me headache. One more would kill me!’
Dexter immediately shook his head. His response was instant, almost reflexive. "No."
The old man blinked. His raised finger stayed frozen in the air. He looked genuinely caught off guard for the first time.
Dexter sighed. He ran a hand through his hair. "I already have enough wives as it is."
For the first time, the old man looked genuinely surprised.
The he looked up at the stars
"It is late. Come tomorrow morning. From sunrise until sundown. If you fail to learn the technique before sunset, the deal ends."
Dexter smiled. The challenge was set. "Deal."
He bid farewell with a respectful nod and returned to his room.
Later that night, Dexter resumed taking care of the girls.
He helped Mira to the bathroom, removed her clothes without looking and getting tempted.
Only the face and of a single woman clouded his mind.
He helped her use the toilet, took her to the shower and washed her up with sponge and shampoo.
Her breasts weren’t massive but they stood firm and could be cupped on one hand.
They were milky white and the areola was actually very pink like a rose bud.
His hands went down her belly then between her legs, slowly caressing the center with care.
Mira let out a soft a gasp but Dexter pretended not to care. He went down her thighs one by one. They were strong dje to her previous exercise before she got crippled.
With this temptation, any man would be rock hard and tempted. However Dexter’s mind was else where or with someone else.
"Are you gay? "
’What the hell?’
Dexter was caught of guard and he almost stumbled on the bathroom floor.
He glared at her.
"If I was gay, would I marry you? Why would you even ask that? "
"Well. You had no choice but to marry us. And I asked because you’re not hard."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"Can’t I be tired? Why did you associate me with being gay?"
Mira looked down at his crotch then shook her head. "I’ve never seen you hard."
Dexter suddenly smirked any wagged his eyebrows playfully.
"Why? Do you want to see me aroused? If I was, do you want to do something about it? "
"Yes."
Dexter wagging eyebrows froze.
He couldn’t tell if she was serious or not. He shook his heard.
"You’re insane."
The silence was awkward.
He got a new pad, fixed it and wore her panties for her. Then he carried her back gently on the bed.
Everything proceeded normally. Eventually, all three girls appeared to fall asleep.
Dexter walked toward the sofa in the main room. He prepared to rest, sinking into the cushions and closing his eyes.
But then—
He suddenly stopped. His enhanced hearing, picked up something unusual. From the bedroom, he heard synchronized breathing patterns. It wasn’t like normal breathing but like cultivating.
And occasionally, faint grunts of pain that were quickly suppressed.
Dexter narrowed his eyes.

They were cultivating again. Despite their damaged meridians. Despite the pain that must be shooting through their bodies every time they tried to channel mana and the miniscule amount of mana they would gain from that, they were still forcing themselves to continue.
Dexter stared toward the bedroom door silently. His expression was complicated.
’Looks like... it’s time I give them their present.’

His breathing was slightly heavy from the sprint.
The old man stared at him sharply.
Then said flatly, "You actually left me standing here."
Dexter scratched his head awkwardly.
’I had to save one of my wives.’ but he didn’t say that.
"It was... a matter of life and death."
The old man stared for several seconds.
His expression was difficult to read.
Then he nodded slowly.
"I see."
Suddenly, the old man tilted his head.
"Let us make a deal."
Dexter blinked.
A deal?
"What kind of deal?"
The old man smiled faintly.
"If you manage to learn my technique for the duration of your stay here, I shall give you a gift."
Dexter’s expression shifted.
A slight furrow on his brow.
Bur internally he was laughing like a mad man.
’This old man doesn’t know what he’s walking into!
Hahahaha!’
Externally, he sighed and puffed out his chest.
"As long as you repeatedly demonstrate the technique," Dexter said, "I can learn it in one day."
The old man froze and his eyes widened slightly.
He had expected the boy to say a month.
Maybe longer, wanting to play with his new toy...But a day?
"One day?" The old man’s voice was sharp with disbelief.
Dexter nodded firmly.
"One day."
Sddenly the old man laughed loudly.
"Hahaha.
Arrogant, simple arrogant!
The most talented take years to learn and you want to learn it in one day?
Interesting.
Very interesting." He stroked his long gray beard.
"Fine.
I’ll raise the stakes."
Dexter leaned forward slightly, curious.
"If you can truly learn my technique in one day, I won’t simply give you an ordinary gift." His eyes gleamed with excitement.
"I will give you a treasure and not only that, I shall let you marry my granddaughter."
Dexter’s eyes widened slightly.
A treasure from a powerhouse would definitely be powerful.
But the old man wasn’t done.
He raised a single finger.
But then the granddaughter part made Dexter shake his head.
’I already have three women and they are giving me headache.
One more would kill me!’
Dexter immediately shook his head.
His response was instant, almost reflexive.
"No."
The old man blinked.
His raised finger stayed frozen in the air.
He looked genuinely caught off guard for the first time.
Dexter sighed.
He ran a hand through his hair.
"I already have enough wives as it is."
For the first time, the old man looked genuinely surprised.
The he looked up at the stars
"It is late.
Come tomorrow morning.
From sunrise until sundown.
If you fail to learn the technique before sunset, the deal ends."
Dexter smiled.
The challenge was set.
"Deal."
He bid farewell with a respectful nod and returned to his room.
Later that night, Dexter resumed taking care of the girls.
He helped Mira to the bathroom, removed her clothes without looking and getting tempted.
Only the face and of a single woman clouded his mind.
He helped her use the toilet, took her to the shower and washed her up with sponge and shampoo.
Her breasts weren’t massive but they stood firm and could be cupped on one hand.
They were milky white and the areola was actually very pink like a rose bud.
His hands went down her belly then between her legs, slowly caressing the center with care.
Mira let out a soft a gasp but Dexter pretended not to care.
He went down her thighs one by one.
They were strong dje to her previous exercise before she got crippled.
With this temptation, any man would be rock hard and tempted.
However Dexter’s mind was else where or with someone else.
"Are you gay?
’What the hell?’
Dexter was caught of guard and he almost stumbled on the bathroom floor.
He glared at her.
"If I was gay, would I marry you?
Why would you even ask that?
"Well.
You had no choice but to marry us.
And I asked because you’re not hard."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"Can’t I be tired?
Why did you associate me with being gay?"
Mira looked down at his crotch then shook her head.
"I’ve never seen you hard."
Dexter suddenly smirked any wagged his eyebrows playfully.
"Why?
Do you want to see me aroused?
If I was, do you want to do something about it?
"Yes."
Dexter wagging eyebrows froze.
He couldn’t tell if she was serious or not.
He shook his heard.
"You’re insane."
The silence was awkward.
He got a new pad, fixed it and wore her panties for her.
Then he carried her back gently on the bed.
Everything proceeded normally.
Eventually, all three girls appeared to fall asleep.
Dexter walked toward the sofa in the main room.
He prepared to rest, sinking into the cushions and closing his eyes.
But then—
He suddenly stopped.
His enhanced hearing, picked up something unusual.
From the bedroom, he heard synchronized breathing patterns.
It wasn’t like normal breathing but like cultivating.
And occasionally, faint grunts of pain that were quickly suppressed.
Dexter narrowed his eyes.
They were cultivating again.
Despite their damaged meridians.

Despite the pain that must be shooting through their bodies every time they tried to channel mana and the miniscule amount of mana they would gain from that, they were still forcing themselves to continue.
Dexter stared toward the bedroom door silently.
His expression was complicated.
’Looks like... it’s time I give them their present.’

chapters.title: Chapter 26 | Gifting The Girls Talents!
paragraphs: The girls are cultivating even with their shattered meridians and the pain it would cause them.
And yet they persisted.
A faint smile tugged at the corners of Dexter’s lips. There was pride in that smile, yes, but also guilt. He wishes he could help them better.
[Ding!]
The familiar notification materialized before him.
[10,000 Times Investment System Activated.]
[Multiplier: 100x.]
Dexter blinked with surprise. The 100x multiplier was the first time since three days he got it.
[You sincerely took care of your wife: Mira.]
[Reconciled with your wives, gave them hope for pone more trial at life]
[Evaluating rewards...]
[Rewards Granted.]
One by one, the notifications began cascading before him.
[Reward 1: Type-1 Relic Obtained.]
[Rainbow Feather Clothing.]

A defensive armor relic capable of adapting to the wearer’s body while offering excellent protection. The fabric shifts and morphs to accommodate any body type, becoming nearly weightless while maintaining defensive capabilities equivalent to military-grade body armor.
Dexter’s eyes widened ur was actually a relic for such a simple task?
[Reward 2: Grade-2 Herb Obtained.]
[Star-Shaped Leaf.]

A soothing medicinal herb capable of being brewed into tea. Calms the nervous system, restores mental fatigue, and when processed correctly, can accelerate the natural healing processes of the body. The leaves emit a gentle, starlight-like shimmer when exposed to moonlight.
[Reward 4: Grade-2 Herb Obtained.]
[Icy Lotus Leaf.]
A rare medicinal herb with cooling properties capable of stabilizing unstable mana fluctuations. Particularly effective for cultivators experiencing disruption in their energy circulation.

These herbs... they were exactly what the girls needed. Grade-2 medicinal herbs were extraordinarily difficult to obtain, and these particular varieties addressed precisely the issues the girls were facing with their damaged meridians.
[Reward 5: Skill Acquired.]
[Tier-2 36 Styles Massage Technique.]

A specialized body massage technique capable of relieving physical pain to the maximum degree, softening muscles, accelerating blood circulation, and increasing healing speed by 200% when used on others.
Dexter stared at the final notification, and he smiled because it was perfect for the girls.
During the past two days, although he had still been caring for the girls... he had been angry. His actions had not been sincere. That was why the system had not activated.
But now, after reconciling with them, he had genuinely cared for Mira.
And the system had responded.
His gaze shifted toward the bedroom door. Through it, he could still hear the girls’ strained breathing, through the walls.
And suddenly, he made a decision.
’I should help them’
He waited for about an hour when they finally fell asleep.
Dexter stood up and entered the bedroom.
The lights remained dim, just a small lamp on the bedside table casting a warm, amber glow across the room. All three girls were lying on the bed, their bodies arranged in a row beneath the covers.
Asleep.
Dexter stood there for a moment.
"Awake?"’
No one answered.

Then slowly, Dexter approached Mira first. She was sleeping closest to the edge of the bed, her amber hair spread across the pillow like fire captured in silk. Even in sleep, there was a certain fierceness to her features.
Carefully, he reached out and gently stroked her hair. The strands were softer than he had expected. At the same time, he spoke inwardly.
’System. Integrate Mana Arm into host.’
Immediately— a notification appeared in his vision, its text floating in the air like a holographic display only he could see.
[Do you wish to integrate ability: Mana Arm into designated host?]
Dexter answered instantly, without hesitation.
’Yes.’
A soft, faint eneegy passed through his palm and transmitted onto Mira.
Her sleeping expression didn’t change. It was as if nothing had happened.
Dexter exhaled softly, then quietly, he moved toward the middle of the bed.
Selene.
She was sleeping peacefully beneath the blankets, her dark hair a stark contrast to the white pillow.
Dexter gently touched her forehead, his fingers barely making contact with her skin.
System. Integrate D-Rank Talent Card: Echolocation.
[Do you wish to integrate D-Rank Talent Card: Echolocation into designated host?]
Yes.
The same faint energy emerged, flowing from his palm into her body like a stream finding its way to the sea. Selene’s eyelashes trembled slightly—but she remained asleep.
Dexter nodded to himself, in satisfaction.
Her glasses had been placed on the bedside table, leaving her face unobstructed.
Dexter gently brushed aside a strand of hair that had fallen across her face, tucking it behind her ear. Then activated the final gift.
System. Integrate D-Rank Talent Card: Telepathy.
[Do you wish to integrate D-Rank Talent Card: Telepathy into designated host?]
Yes.
The energy transferred silently into her body.

Dexter stared at the three girls quietly, his heart swelling with an emotion he couldn’t quite name. It wasn’t love, their relationship was too complicated, but it was something. Maybe responsibility?
None of them seemed to notice anything unusual.
Or so he thought.
Because in reality— two of them weren’t asleep.
Lyra had been pretending, her mind racing with questions about what Dexter was doing. And Mira— Mira had also been pretending.
Mira kept her eyes shut tightly, her body rigid with the effort of remaining still. But internally, she was confused.
"Why is this pervert touching our heads in the middle of the night?"
’I heard some people are into feet, is he not hair?’
A slight frown formed on her face. Then inwardly she muttered— Perverted gay guy...
Dexter, completely unaware of her thoughts wmiled as he completed his mission.
Satisfied with his secret gifts, he turned and made his way out of the bedroom without making another sound, closing the door behind him with a soft click.

Returning to the living room, he lay down on the sofa, staring up at the ceiling. Tomorrow would be an important day. The challenge with the old man. Learning the legendary technique. If everything went well, he would obtain not only a Legendary Technique but possibly another priceless reward.
Slowly— he closed his eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 27 | Hero Association Representative
paragraphs: The morning came faster than expected, pale light seeping through the windows and painting the room in shades of gray and gold. Dexter woke with a start, momentarily disoriented before remembering where he was and what lay ahead. After washing up, he quickly changed clothes and prepared to leave, his movements efficient despite the early hour.
Just as he reached for the door—
Knock. Knock.
The sound was unexpected, making Dexter paused, his hand hovering inches from the doorknob. His brows furrowed slightly. He hadn’t ordered room service. Who could possibly be here this early?
Curious, and with a slight sense, he walked toward the door and opened it.
The moment the door swung open— both of them froze.
Dexter’s eyes widened, stunned and the woman standing in the hallway had equally widened eyes, her hand still raised in the position of having just knocked.
"...Rachel?"
Dexter couldn’t believe she was herw right now.
It had been a day they saw each other last.
The woman blinked, her long black lashes fluttered, she was just as shocked as his. "Dexter?"
Then Rachel tilted her head, a habitual gesture he remembered well from the bar.
"What are you doing here?"

Dexter scratched his cheek awkwardly, feeling suddenly self-conscious about his appearance. "Well..." he began, searching for the right words. "This is where I’ve been staying ever since the monster outbreak destroyed our street."
Rachel frowned slightly, the expression pulling at features that were, if anything, even more beautiful than he remembered. "Oh. So you were affected too?"
Dexter nodded, "Yeah."
Then he looked at her curiously, taking in her professional attire, it suggested she wasn’t here by accident. "What about you? What are you doing here?"

Rachel smiled. "I’m the representative from the Hero Association assigned to handle matters regarding your damaged home..." She paused, as if choosing her next words carefully. "And... your situation."
Understanding flashed across Dexter’s face. The Hero told them they would send a representative in three days. So she’s the one they sent.
"Ah." He stepped aside, gesturing into the suit. "Come in."

Rachel nodded and stepped inside, and as she passed by him, Dexter found himself momentarily staring. She was still incredibly pretty. And the moment she passed by, a pleasant fragrance reached his nose. Vanilla. Mixed with jasmine.
Shaking away the thought with, Dexter closed the door behind him. "You want something to drink?"
Rachel nodded, already scanning the room. "A soft drink is fine.
Dexter walked toward the fridge and handed her a cold bottle, the condensation wetting his fingers. But the moment Rachel stepped fully into the living room, she froze.
Three women were present.
Mira sat in her wheelchair near the television, her amber hair cascading over her shoulders.
Lyra stood quietly nearby, glasses resting over her eyes, her expression carefully neutral as she assessed the newcomer.
Selene sat silently on the couch, staring blankly ahead.
Rachel blinked several times as though hadn’t comprehended what she was seeing.
She turned toward Dexter, her expression had become very strange.
"I thought..." She hesitated, as if unsure whether to voice what was on her mind. Then asked carefully— "...you were joking."
Dexter frowned, not following her train of thought. "About what?"
Rachel stared at the girls, then back at him. "You actually have three wives?"
Dexter shrugged, feeling suddenly uncomfortable under the combined attention of four women. "Well... I tried telling you."
At that exact moment, Mira slowly turned her head.
Ber suspicious gaze moved between both of them, then she narrowed her eyes, as her face darkened.
"...Do you two know each other?"
Rachel immediately straightened her posture, her professional demeanor snapping back into place.
"No." She caught herself, realizing how defensive that sounded.
She cleared her throat, then quickly corrected herself. "I mean... we met briefly before."
She extended a hand politely toward Mira, the gesture formal and businesslike. "Rachel. Representative from the Hero Association. I’m here to discuss matters regarding your current situation."
Mira stared at her for several seconds, her gaze unblinking.
Then slowly, a smirk spread across her face.
"No.
Rachel blinked, clearly not expecting that response. "No...?"
Mira rolled her eyes.
"It feels like something else."
Her eyes moved between Rachel and Dexter with the precision of a predator tracking prey.
Then she casually asked— "Did you two hook up?"
Dexter nearly choked out on his own spit.
Rachel’s face stiffened, a faint flush creeping up her neck that she quickly suppressed it.
Dexter immediately coughed awkwardly, trying to regain his composure. "What kind of question is that?"
Mira smirked wider, clearly enjoying his discomfort. "Well?"
Dexter rolled his eyes, feeling a headache beginning to form behind his temples. "We’re married. Why would I sleep with someone else?"
Mira simply gave him a mocking smile, she clearly didn’t believe him but didn’t press the matter either.
She turned away without another word, ignoring then both.
The atmosphere immediately became awkward.
At the side Selene and Lyra had also shifted their attention. Unlike before, they weren’t ignoring the conversation. Instead— they were staring directly at Rachel.
Dexter noticed immediately. And to his surprise, it almost looked like they were trying to intimidate her.
Like they were marking their territory.
For some reason— that made him smile slightly, a warm feeling spreading through his chest despite the awkwardness of the situation.
Rachel quickly returned to business, clearly eager to move past the uncomfortable exchange.

She crossed one leg over the other and spoke professionally, her voice regaining its measured cadence. "The repairs on your house are nearly complete. By tomorrow, everything should be fully restored. You and your family can move back in."
Dexter nodded. "That’s good."

Rachel continued, her eyes focused on her tablet as she scrolled through information. "There’s also the matter regarding the sixteen beasts you killed during the outbreak. Their carcasses have been processed. The Nexus Points and compensation have already been calculated."

Dexter listened carefully, his interest piqued. Nexus Points were the currency of the hero world, used to purchase everything from weapons to techniques to rare materials and could be used for cultivation.

chapters.title: Chapter 28 | Meeting Rachael!
paragraphs: Rachel looked up from her tablet. "The processed value of the beast carcasses amounts to approximately... sixty thousand dollars. That is the maximum compensation we were able to extract from the remains."
Dexter thought for a moment, doing quick mental calculations. It was a significant sum and with his system he could double it.
But he wanted more.
Then he shook his head. "I’ll take half the money."
Rachel frowned, clearly not expecting that response. "And the other half?"
Dexter smiled, a plan already forming in his mind. "I want the half of the monster nexus core given to me."
Rachel immediately shook her head, her expression apologetic but firm. "That won’t be possible."
Dexter blinked, not understanding the refusal. "Why?"

Rachel explained calmly, her tone suggesting this was a common misconception she had to address regularly. "Nexus cores can only be issued to registered heroes. You’re currently unlicensed. If you want access to resources... you’ll need to officially register with the Hero Association first."
Dexter slowly nodded, processing this information.
"I see." Then he smiled,
"Well... looks like I’ll have to become a licensed hero then."
Rachel smiled back, the expression transforming her face from attractive to genuinely beautiful. "I figured you’d say that."

Then her expression shifted, becoming more personal. "From what I’ve heard... you killed beasts two levels above your rank during the outbreak." She leaned slightly closer, her vanilla-jasmine scent washing over him again. "With feats like that... passing the Hero Association exam shouldn’t be difficult for you."
Dexter smiled awkwardly, feeling uncomfortable with the praise. "Thanks."
For a brief second— neither spoke.
"Well then, I will be leaving."
Then suddenly, Rachel stood up and before Dexter could react— she stepped forward. And hugged him.
Dexter froze, his body going rigid with surprise before instinct took over and he used one hand to hug her back.
Rachel slowly pulled away, and when she did, a strange smile had formed on her lips.
She lightly licked her lower lip.
Then she said softly. "I’ll be seeing you very soon."
With that, she turned around and left.
Dexter stared at the closed door for several seconds, then shook his head and chuckled.
Then he turned around.
The moment he did— Mira had opened her eyes. And was glaring directly at him.
"So..." She said slowly, each word measured and precise. "That’s who you’ve been going out to see these past two days."
Dexter stared at her blankly. Then sighed. "She’s not. And I already have the three of you to deal with. Why would I want another woman added into the mix?"
Mira narrowed her eyes, her glare intensifying. "Oh? So now we’re burdens?"
Dexter immediately groaned, running a hand through his hair in frustration. "There you go twisting my words again. You know that’s not what I meant."
Mira simply snorted.
Dexter shook his head helplessly, then looked at all three girls, taking in their varied expressions. "Do any of you need anything? Food? Room service?"
Lyra immediately nodded. Mira remained silent, still pouting.
Selene said nothing, but judging by her expression— she was clearly still annoyed, though whether at him or at Rachel or at the situation in general was impossible to tell.
Dexter sighed, the sound carrying an acceptance of his role in this strange domestic dynamic they had developed. "Fine. I’ll order food."
While waiting for room service, he suddenly remembered the herbs he had obtained from the system.
The Star-Shaped Leaf and Icy Lotus Leaf. A thought crossed his mind.
Quietly, so as not to attract attention, accepted the rears and they appeared in his hands as if materializing from thin air, their presence somehow feeling both natural and otherworldly.
The Star-Shaped Leaf lived up to its name, its five points arranged in a perfect star pattern, each point tipped with a faint luminescence that seemed to pulse gently.
The Icy Lotus Leaf was its opposite in appearance, a deep blue-green color that seemed to radiate cold even without direct contact.
Walking toward the kitchen area— he carefully prepared tea using both ingredients, following instincts of a Master Chef.
A soothing aroma slowly began spreading through the room, It was unlike any tea Dexter had ever encountered, carrying with it a sense of calm that seemed to seep directly into the bones.
Minutes later— Dexter returned carrying three cups, each one steam rising in delicate spirals. Placing them on trays, he handed one to each girl.
Mira frowned suspiciously, eyeing the cup as if it might contain poison. "What kind of tea is this?"
Dexter simply crossed his arms, not rising to her suspicion. "Just drink it."

Mira clicked her tongue, the sound sharp with irritation. She still felt annoyed after seeing Rachel earlier, the woman’s obvious familiarity with Dexter stirring feelings she didn’t want to examine too closely. So naturally— she wanted to refuse, out of pure spite.
But then— the aroma reached her nose.
A strange sensation immediately spread through her body. Warm. Refreshing. Like sunlight breaking through clouds on a winter day, or the first breath of spring air after months of cold.
Even before drinking it, she felt her entire body becoming lighter, the constant background ache that had become so familiar she had almost stopped noticing it beginning to fade.
Her eyes widened slightly,
’What... is this?’
Mira opened her mouth and Dexter poured the entire tea in her mouth.
As it hit her throat, her expression changed instantly.
A strange sensation immediately spread through her body.
Warm. Refreshing.
Even before drinking it, she felt her entire body becoming lighter.
Her eyes widened slightly.
’What... is this?’
The moment Dexter brought the tea to her lips and she took the first sip—
Her lips quivered.
She could feel mana moving brought her body.
Not just moving—
It was flowing through her body far more smoothly than usual.
Even more shocking, it wasn’t painful and she could feel her damaged meridians being nourished.
Tiny strands of energy were gently repairing the broken channels inside her body.
Her breathing immediately grew heavier.
She looked at Dexter then and the teacup he was holding, clearly stunned beyond words.

chapters.title: Chapter 29 | Learning The Technique (100 PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: "Tell me. Where did you get it?"
Dexter simply smiled but said nothing.
Mira stared at him for several seconds, then quietly looked away.
She didn’t push further.
Instead, she drank the entire cup in one go.
Then immediately closed her eyes.
Mana began circulating through her body as she focused entirely on guiding the medicinal energy toward her damaged meridians.
At the side—
Lyra and Selene had heard the entire conversation.
At first, both were skeptical.
But after seeing Mira’s reaction—
They immediately drank theirs too.
The effect was instantaneous.
Their breathing immediately grew heavier.
Mana fluctuations surrounded both of them.
Without wasting another second—
They closed their eyes and began circulating the medicinal energy through their own damaged channels.
Dexter smiled faintly as he watched them.
Thankfully—
The herbs he received from the system were plentiful.
Nearly a pound each.
Enough for them to continue drinking for at least a week.
Unfortunately...
There was one drawback.
Rewards obtained from the system...
Could not be reused to trigger new rewards.
Otherwise—
This would have been ridiculously overpowered.
He needed fresh methods of gaining rewards.
Just then— Knock. Knock.
The room service had arrived. A staff member rolled a tray of food into the room, the smells of fresh bread, cooked eggs, and steaming meat filling the space.
After taking the tray, Dexter closed the door behind him. "The food is here,"
But none of the girls responded. All three remained seated silently, eyes shut, completely focused on circulating the medicinal energy through their damaged meridians.
Dexter chuckled softly. Then suddenly— a thought crossed his mind, sobering his mood.
The Divine Pill.
The reward he had obtained earlier, before his reconciliation with the girls. It had the power to completely repair one damaged body.
But he only had one.
One pill.
If he gave it to Mira— then Selene and Lyra would be left out. If he gave it to Selene, the other two might feel abandoned, If he gave it to Lyra— same problem.

No matter what— someone would feel left behind. And in a relationship as fragile and complicated as theirs, that could create unnecessary tension, could reopen wounds that had only just begun to heal.
After thinking for a moment, weighing the options in his mind— Dexter shook his head. Not yet. I’ll wait.
Quietly, he moved toward the door, casting one last look at the three women who had become such an unexpected and important part of his life. "I’ll be back soon."
None of them answered. All three were still fully immersed in cultivation, their bodies still, their breathing synchronized with the flow of energy through their systems.
Outside— the old man was already waiting. But unlike before— this time he wasn’t standing on the balcony.
Instead, he stood calmly in the open hotel courtyard below, hands clasped behind his back, his posture somehow both relaxed and focused.
As though he had been waiting for a long time.
Dexter approached quietly and greeted. "Good morning."
The old man nodded. Then asked calmly. "Are you ready?"
Dexter smiled, feeling a strange mixture of anticipation and nervousness. "Yes."
The old man said nothing further.

Instead, he slowly inhaled, his chest expanding with a deep breath that seemed to pull in more air than his frame should have been able to contain. Then exhaled, the release lasting far longer than any normal breath should.
And instantly. his aura changed.
Without warning, he began moving. His body entered the first form, then the second. Then the third. His breathing shifted with every movement, each inhale and exhale.
At that exact moment, a system notification appeared before Dexter, its text flickering rapidly as it processed what it was observing.
[Analyzing Legendary Technique...]
[Progress: 25%]
The percentage began climbing steadily,
Twenty minutes later— the old man completed one full cycle, He stopped and looked at Dexter, his eyes sharp and assessing.
"Did you get it?"
Dexter smiled faintly and replied. "Getting there."
The old man narrowed his eyes, clearly dissatisfied with that answer but not surprised by it either. Then immediately began again.
And again.
And again.
Over and over.
Repeated endlessly.
The hours passed. Morning slowly turned into afternoon, the sun climbing higher in the sky until it was directly on top of them.
Heat covered the courtyard, the air shimmering with thermal distortion,
Yet, the old man continued moving. Again. Again. Again. Like a machine.
Four full hours passed.
And through it all, there wasn’t a single bead of sweat on the old man’s body.
Dexter watched in stunned silence, his respect for the old man growing with each passing hour.
Even standing nearby, Dexter could feel an invisible pressure radiating from the old man, and he knew the man was probably a hidden powerhouse.
[Ding!]
[Extraction of Legendary-Tier Technique Successful.]
[You have learned...]

chapters.title: Chapter 30 | Grand Cosmos Scripture
paragraphs: The moment the notification appeared before Dexter— his eyes immediately locked onto the description, drinking in every word as if his life depended on it.
[Grand Cosmos Scripture]
(Seventh-Tier )
Description:
A legendary cultivation technique that abandons the traditional path of meridians and transforms the human body into a miniature universe.
Upon activation, dormant Star Nodes hidden throughout the body awaken one by one. Each Star Node functions as an independent celestial core capable of storing vast quantities of mana.

Unlike ordinary cultivators, practitioners of the Grand Cosmos Scripture do not circulate mana through meridians. Instead, every awakened Star Node generates a powerful gravitational force, automatically drawing surrounding mana into itself while the user meditates.
Once a Star Node reaches full capacity, it permanently strengthens the body and serves as an inexhaustible source of mana. The cultivator may then awaken the next Star Node.
Current Star Nodes: 0/360
First Firmament : 1-100 Star Nodes
Second Firmament : 101-200 Star Nodes
Third Firmament : 201-300 Star Nodes
Grand Firmament : 301-360 Star Nodes
Effects:
• Eliminates the need for meridian-based cultivation.
• Awakened Star Nodes automatically absorb surrounding mana during meditation.
• Every Star Node acts as an independent mana reservoir.
• Massively increases total mana capacity.
• Permanently enhances physique with each awakened Star Node.
• Cultivation speed increases as additional Star Nodes are awakened.
• Damage to one Star Node does not affect the others.
Ultimate Effect:
When all 360 Star Nodes are completely filled with mana, they resonate as one, forming a complete Inner Cosmos.
The practitioner will automatically break through the Peak Ultra Warrior Realm and become Legendary.
No bottlenecks.
No breakthrough pills.
No external assistance.
Dexter stood there frozen in shock.
This technique... it was perfect. Absolutely, impossibly perfect.

His thoughts immediately drifted toward Mira, Lyra, and Selene. All three of them had suffered catastrophic damage to their meridians. The pathways they once used to cultivate had been shattered almost beyond repair, leaving them crippled in ways that went beyond physical injury. Without a divine-tier treasure— recovery was nearly impossible.

And even then... he only had one Divine Pill. One. If he gave it to one girl— the other two would inevitably feel left out, would wonder why they hadn’t been chosen, would feel their worth measured and found wanting. It would create resentment, would drive wedges between people who were only just beginning to come together.
But this technique... this changed everything.
The Grand Cosmos Scripture completely abandoned meridian-based cultivation. It didn’t need meridians at all. Meaning, the girls could cultivate again.
Dexter’s eyes widened further as he smiled at the girls.
The technique... was priceless. Beyond priceless. It was the kind of treasure that families would go to war over, that nations would sacrifice generations to obtain.
And he had just learned it by watching an old man practice for a few hours.
At that exact moment— the old man noticed Dexter’s strange expression. His brows slowly furrowed.
’Don’t tell me... this brat is distracted while I’m teaching him?’
The old man narrowed his eyes, a spark of irritation flaring to life.
’Well... he doesn’t know what happens if he loses the bet. I suppose I should keep teaching him seriously for now, make sure he has every opportunity to succeed before I collect my winnings.’
A dangerous glint flashed through his eyes, then he resumed practicing, preparing to demonstrate the technique again.
But suddenly, and he was in quite disbelief by what he saw.
Because something impossible was happening.

Dexter had suddenly begun breathing strangely, the pattern matching exactly what the old man had been demonstrating. The breathing pattern perfectly synchronized with the technique, each inhale and exhale hitting the precise timing required.
The old man’s eyes widened slightly. Them more. Then more again.
Because Dexter had begun copying him. No. Not copying. Learning.

The Grand Cosmos Scripture had two components. The first— the Meditation Aspect. A breathing technique designed to gather mana and guide it into hidden Star Nodes. The second— the Physical Aspect. A sequence of body movements designed to stimulate the body, open every pore, and dramatically increase mana absorption.
Using both together created perfect synergy, each aspect amplifying the effects of the other. While it was possible to cultivate using meditation alone— combining both aspects, increased efficiency.
And right now— Dexter was performing both. Perfectly.
The old man stood completely frozen, his own practice abandoned as he watched in disbelief. His jaw slowly dropped, also low it almost hit devil’s head.
He couldn’t believe what he was seeing.
’Impossible!’
It hasn’t even been a day.
’How...?’ ’How the hell did he learn it already?’
The old man stared at Dexter as if looking at a monster, his previous confidence crumbling to shock. What kind of freak is this? No... What kind of demon is this?
Meanwhile— Dexter remained completely focused, unaware of the old man’s reaction, his entire being consumed by the effort of performing the technique for the first time.
His body moved through the cultivation forms.
Unlike the old man— he wasn’t proficient yet. His movements were rough, slightly stiff, unrefined.
Because of that— it took him almost forty minutes to complete one full cycle. Twice as long as the old man.
By the time he finished— sweat covered his entire body, soaking through his clothes and dripping from his chin onto the courtyard stones.
His chest rose heavily, as his lungs burned.
He could feel mana entering his body, could sense the energy being drawn in by the technique’s innate properties. But, nothing happened.
No Star Node had awakened. Which meant— he still hadn’t located the first dormant node inside his body.
Dexter wiped sweat from his forehead, his arm feeling heavy with exhaustion.
Then looked toward the old man, expecting to see satisfaction or approval or at least acknowledgment of his effort.
Only to freeze.
The old man was staring at him with his mouth wide open, an expression of pure, shock and something else was in the old man’s face.
It was so completely out of character with the composed, superior demeanor he had displayed until now, that Dexter found himself momentarily confused.
Suddenly, without saying a single word, the old man turned around and walked straight into the hotel.
Dexter blinked, his confusion deepening. "...Huh?" He scratched the back of his head, a habitual gesture when he was puzzled. "What did I do?"
