’How...?’ ’How the hell did he learn it already?’
The old man stared at Dexter as if looking at a monster, his previous confidence crumbling to shock.
What kind of freak is this?
No...
What kind of demon is this?
Meanwhile— Dexter remained completely focused, unaware of the old man’s reaction, his entire being consumed by the effort of performing the technique for the first time.
His body moved through the cultivation forms.
Unlike the old man— he wasn’t proficient yet.
His movements were rough, slightly stiff, unrefined.
Because of that— it took him almost forty minutes to complete one full cycle.
Twice as long as the old man.
By the time he finished— sweat covered his entire body, soaking through his clothes and dripping from his chin onto the courtyard stones.
His chest rose heavily, as his lungs burned.
He could feel mana entering his body, could sense the energy being drawn in by the technique’s innate properties.
But, nothing happened.
No Star Node had awakened.
Which meant— he still hadn’t located the first dormant node inside his body.
Dexter wiped sweat from his forehead, his arm feeling heavy with exhaustion.
Then looked toward the old man, expecting to see satisfaction or approval or at least acknowledgment of his effort.
Only to freeze.
The old man was staring at him with his mouth wide open, an expression of pure, shock and something else was in the old man’s face.
It was so completely out of character with the composed, superior demeanor he had displayed until now, that Dexter found himself momentarily confused.
Suddenly, without saying a single word, the old man turned around and walked straight into the hotel.
Dexter blinked, his confusion deepening.
"...Huh?" He scratched the back of his head, a habitual gesture when he was puzzled.
"What did I do?"

chapters.title: Chapter 31 | Gifting The Ladies The Technique
paragraphs: Five minutes passed and just when Dexter was beginning to think he should simply leave and return to the girls, to check on their progress, the old man returned.
"Here’s your gift."
It had a strange black cord attached to a circular pendant split into two colors. Black and white.
Dexter blinked, taking the necklace automatically. "What is this?"
The old man simply stared at him, and then shook his head and sighed.
"Keep it safe."
Before Dexter could ask anything, the old man turned around and left without explanation.
Dexter stood there, still holding the necklace, completely confused.
A few seconds later, he looked upward, toward the balcony of the old man above.
Standing there, was a young woman.
She was staring directly at him, her gaze intense and unblinking. Long black hair flowed down her shoulders like ink with two beautiful violet eyes.
For a brief second, Dexter found himself stunned. She was incredibly attractive almost comparable to Mira, Lyra, and Selene.
The young woman merely stared at him silently, her expression unreadable.
Dexter lowered his gaze, suddenly uncomfortable with the intensity of her attention.
Whatever this necklace was— it was definitely not ordinary.
After staring at it for a moment longer, Dexter shrugged, forcing himself to relax. "Well..." he muttered to himself, a wry smile tugging at his lips. "It’s probably something good."
Without thinking too much about it, he placed the necklace around his neck, then he tucked it beneath his shirt, hiding it from view. Satisfied, Dexter turned around and headed back toward his room.
As he walked he kept thinking how perfect the scripture would be to the girls.
Their meridians have been shattered which means they would be useless for life until it’s repaired.
But with this scripture, it removed the need for meridians entirely.
’I’m giving it to them.’
Without hesitation, Dexter entered the room. They had already finished eating, the empty dishes pushed to the side.
He glanced at all three of them. "I need to talk to three of you."
A few moments later, all three sat in the living room, staring at him curiously.
"Don’t tell me you want to announce your fourth wife."
Lyra’s eyes widened and Selene’s sandwich almost fell to the ground.
Dexter’s lips curled to a smile.
"Even better."
"Two wives?" Mira frowned this time.
Dexter stood in front of them and chuckled.
"Nop, I have a cultivation technique."
The girls blinked, their confusion deepening rather than resolving.
Dexter continued. "I want to give it to all of you."
Silence.
Mira rolled her eyes, in disappointment.
"Seriously?"
"No matter what cultivation technique you have... it can’t possibly compare to our family cultivation arts."
Dexter simply remained silent, allowing her to express her doubts without interruption.

Mira smiled smugly. "Our families trained us using Tier Four cultivation techniques. Even after everything... those are still among the best techniques in this entire city. They’ve been refined over generations, perfected through centuries of careful study and practice."
She paused, her expression taking on a condescending quality. "So unless you somehow found something better than that..."
She suddenly stopped speaking.
Because Dexter was smiling.
Smiling.
’Did he actually...?,
Mira eyes narrowed.
She didn’t believe he found one better than Tier 4.
Even Selene was staring intently now.
Then— without warning— Dexter stepped forward.
And placed his hand gently on Mira’s forehead.
Mira flinched instinctively, her body stiffening. She felt like pushing her head away, but then, she lowered her head and submitted, wondering what the hell their husband was up to.
Inside his mind, Dexter immediately commander
"System. Transfer Grand Cosmos Scripture."
[Ding Imparting Processing.
Unlike ordinary techniques— a Seventh-Tier Technique could not simply be taught verbally.
It needed direct transmission.l to be imparted.
That was why the old man had been so horrified earlier.
Techniques of this level were typically shared through controlled rituals and secretly.

Dexter learning the technique simply by observing... without direct imparting was monstrous. It meant he had done something nearly impossible, had achieved in hours what should have taken years or decades.
A faint light appeared around Dexter’s hand. Then— the information transferred directly into Mira’s consciousness.
Mira’s eyes immediately widened, then slowly closed, her eyelids fluttering as a torrent of information flooded her mind.
Seeing the process succeed— Dexter moved toward Lyra.
She quietly set aside the bag of chips, then obediently closed her eyes.
Dexter placed his palm against her forehead, feeling the warmth of her skin beneath his fingers.
’Transfer Grand Cosmos Scripture.’
The second transfer began. Countless streams of information entered her consciousness, her body going rigid for a moment before relaxing as she adapted to the influx.
Then finally, Selene.
Dexter approached carefully, aware that she was the most guarded of the three.
This time, Selene didn’t flinch when he touched her, didn’t pull away or tense up at his approach.
Which immediately caught Dexter’s attention. That was progress.
Without wasting time, he transferred the technique into her as well, and then— silence.
All three girls remained completely motionless, eyes shut, their bodies perfectly still except for the slow rise and fall of their breathing.
Forty minutes, passed
Finally, after nearly an hour, all three slowly opened their eyes one by one.
And the moment they did— Dexter immediately noticed something strange.
All three expressions had changed.
Instead, their expressions had become deadly serious.
All three stared directly at him, their eyes unblinking and their faces froze as they stared dumbfoundedly at him.
It was as though they were looking at something they could not comprehend.
As if staring at a monster.
Or worse— a demon.
Dexter blinked, suddenly uncomfortable under their combined gaze. "...Why are you all looking at me like that?"
None of them answered immediately.
Because right now, their minds were in absolute chaos.
The technique they had just received... was real, a genuine, complete, Seventh-Tier Cultivation Technique.
And that made absolutely no sense.

Tier Seven techniques... were practically myths. Stories told to young cultivators to inspire them, to give them something to aspire to, even if they never had any realistic hope of achieving such heights.

Across the entire city— the strongest known cultivation technique was only Tier Five. And it belonged to the most powerful family in the city, the Colwell Family, whose influence extended into every aspect of supernatural society.
Even then— the Colwell Family guarded that technique jealously. Only the family head was allowed to cultivate it.
Other members, no matter how loyal or talented, were restricted to Tier Four techniques at best.
The secret of the Tier Five technique was perhaps the most closely guarded piece of knowledge in the entire region.
Yet now— Dexter had casually handed them something two entire levels higher. Something far beyond anything their families possessed.
Their thoughts spiraled wildly, each trying to make sense of something that defied sense.
Who exactly is Dexter?
Where did he get this?
How is this possible?

For a long time now— they had suspected Dexter wasn’t ordinary. His sudden growth in strength, his strange abilities that seemed to appear from nowhere and other wierd things but they hadn’t care at all.
But now— all doubts disappeared.
Dexter was hiding insane. And their must be a massive problem organization behind him.
And suddenly, for the second time this week, all three girls began seeing him differently.
At that moment, the three girls came to the exact same conclusion.
Their husband... was far, far more terrifying than they had ever imagined.

chapters.title: Chapter 32 | Storm Empress!
paragraphs: The rest of the day felt... strange. Not because anything wild happened. But because nothing happened.
It was too quiet.
At first, Dexter didn’t mind. The girls finally had hope again.
He’d handed them a way to cultivate that danced right past their shattered meridians.
That was huge.
Of course they’d be excited.
But after several hours, he realized he had been ignored.
Completely ignored.
They’d eaten exactly once the whole day — early morning, when the food cart arrived and he’d made them that medicinal tea.
After that? Nothing. Lunch came and the plates sat untouched Cold food, closed doors, and three girls lost in their own glowing little worlds.
Dexter leaned against the bedroom doorway, arms crossed, watching them like a parent whose kids had discovered a new video game.

Mira was by the window in her wheelchair, eyes pressed shut. Tiny waves of mana rose and fell around her like a warm breeze. Inside the bedroom, Selene sat cross-legged on the bed, breathing slow and steady, each inhale and exhale perfectly in sync with the Grand Cosmos Scripture.
And Lyra? She’d claimed the living room sofa, glasses on, eyes closed, deep in her own cultivation trance.
Three spots. Three girls. Three absolute cultivation maniacs.
Dexter sighed loud enough to shake the walls. "I’m starting to feel like a forgotten houseplant in this room."
No one even twitched.
He shook his head, a tiny smile tugging at his lips. "Maybe I should’ve waited a few more days before teaching them."

But he wasn’t really upset. Honestly? This made him happy. The way they dove in so obsessively meant one thing: those dark thoughts of ending it all were gone. They’d found hope again. A belief that one day they’d stand at the top once more. And that was everything.
So, with nobody interested in food, Dexter sat down alone and pulled the entire dinner tray toward himself.
As he ate, he noticed something else his bloodline evolution had done to him.
His appetite had gone completely wild.
Since his body upgraded, he needed almost three times as much food. His stomach was like a bottomless pit.
He stabbed a hunk of steak and muttered, "Great. First Lyra was the endless eater... now I’m turning into a clone of her." He chuckled at his own joke, then grabbed the remote and flipped on the TV.
The screen flicked through boring stuff, political chatter, monster attack updates, Hero Association announcements, ads for protein bars. Then suddenly, an emergency broadcast took over.
A female reporter’s urgent voice cut through.
The screen showed chaos. Big yellow letters at the bottom read: [LIVE BROADCAST — DETROIT COUNTRY DISASTER RESPONSE].
Dexter’s eyebrow went up.
The camera zoomed out. Far off in the ocean, a gigantic luxury yacht had snapped clean in two.
Both halves were sinking fast.
People screamed, jumping into the churning water, clinging to bits of wreckage while others were already slipping under.

The reporter’s voice shook. "A disaster off the coast of Detroit Country! The Aurora Queen, a massive luxury vessel, has suffered a catastrophic structural collapse and split in half roughly twelve kilometers from shore. Over one hundred passengers are now stranded at sea—"
Before she could finish, the camera jerked upward. A howling gust of wind ripped across the ocean. The clouds spun like a stirred pot.
And then she dropped from the sky.
Long silver-white hair streamed behind her like a banner. A tight battle suit gleamed under the sun. Her eyes were gold and cold as winter.
She hung in the air, not moving, yet the sheer power bleeding off her made the screen seem fragile.
The broadcaster’s voice exploded with excitement. "She’s here! The pride of the younger generation! The rising symbol of global hero supremacy! Storm Empress!"
Dexter’s eyes narrowed. He set his fork down.
She moved.
"BOOM!"
The air cracked like thunder. She shot forward so fast the camera could barely track her. In a blink, she reached the broken yacht.

Each half of that ship weighed several hundred tons, heavy as a small building. Without a pause, Storm Empress reached out both hands. One grabbed the front half, the other grabbed the rear half. And she lifted.
Dexter’s chewing stopped dead. His eyes stretched wide. She was carrying both halves. In each hand. Like they were grocery bags.
The giant chunks of metal rose into the sky as if they weighed nothing. Passengers still trapped onboard screamed in disbelief.
Calmly, she flew both sections to the beach and set them down, gentle as placing a sleeping baby.
Then she turned and shot back over the water, a blur of wind. The camera struggled to keep up. She plunged into the ocean and came back up clutching three people.
Then five. Then ten. Over and over. A living hurricane. In minutes, nearly eighty stranded passengers had been scooped up and set safely on dry sand.

The newscaster’s voice boomed like an announcer at a sports final. "Another impossible feat by one of humanity’s greatest young protectors! Storm Empress proves again why she’s the strongest hero of her generation! At only twenty-four, she continues to rewrite what modern heroes can be! This — is the hope our generation looks up to!"
Dexter stared at the screen, jaw tight. His chest felt heavy. What he’d just seen was terrifying.
She could actually fly! And that speed, it was insane.

Enough raw strength to lift hundreds of tons like it was nothing. Durability to rocket through the ocean without a scratch. She’d left the Superhero Realm in the dust and was most likely at the Ultra Realm.
A 24 year old Ultra realm hero was astonishing. She has most likely broken some sort of record.
He leaned back and sighed.

The gap between him and the world’s true monsters was still an ocean wide. He fixed his eyes on Storm Empress frozen on the screen. So that’s the level I need to reach someday... No. That’s the level I need to crush.
Right at that moment—
DING!
A familiar golden glow blinked in front of his face. The 10,000 Times Investment System.
Dexter straightened up, heart kicking. A second message appeared beneath it.
[10,000x Investment System Activated.]
[You imparted the Grand Cosmos Scripture to your wives.]
[Calculating multiplier...]
[Multiplier Achieved: 100x.]
[Reward Generation In Progress...]
[You have received...]

chapters.title: Chapter 33 | Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture
paragraphs: As soon as the first golden screen faded, a new one popped right in front of Dexter.
[10,000x Investment System Activated.]
[Reward ready.]
[Congratulations, Host.]
[You have received a Ninth-Tier cultivation technique.]
[Primordial Universe Star Scripture.]
Dexter went completely still. Then his eyes flew open so wide they almost hurt.
Ninth-Tier.
The highest tier to ever exist and no one had set their hands on.
His face fished red with excitement.
The system showed more.
[Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture]
Ninth-Tier Technique
Description:
The perfected form of the Grand Cosmos Scripture.
No longer limited to forging a miniature universe, this supreme cultivation technique transforms the practitioner’s body into a boundless cosmos capable of containing countless celestial bodies.
Within the body lie 3,600 dormant Star Nodes. Every awakened Star Node becomes an independent celestial core, possessing its own gravitational field and serving as an inexhaustible source of mana.
Meridians become completely obsolete.

Once awakened, each Star Node continuously draws in the surrounding mana on its own, requiring no manual circulation. As more Star Nodes awaken, the attraction force of the Inner Cosmos grows stronger, allowing the practitioner’s cultivation speed to increase exponentially.
Every completed Firmament causes all previously awakened Star Nodes to evolve, increasing their capacity, density, and quality of mana.
Current Star Nodes: 0/3,600
Effects:
• Completely abandons the meridian system.
• Every awakened Star Node automatically absorbs surrounding mana.
• Each Star Node is an independent world capable of storing immense quantities of mana.
• Every completed Firmament upgrades all existing Star Nodes to the next celestial tier.
• Mana reserves increase to levels far beyond ordinary cultivators.
• Cultivation speed grows exponentially as additional Star Nodes awaken.
• The destruction of individual Star Nodes does not collapse the Inner Cosmos.
• The body gradually evolves into a true Cosmic Physique.
Ultimate Effect:
When all 3,600 Star Nodes reach perfection, they resonate simultaneously, giving birth to a complete Infinite Cosmos.
The Inner Cosmos becomes self-sustaining, generating celestial energy without relying solely on the surrounding world.
The practitioner transcends mortality, breaking all worldly limits and ascending as a being whose body rivals the universe itself.
Dexter stared at the screen so long his eyes started to sting. His whole body trembled.
A Ninth-Tier technique... Did something like this really exist?

He seriously doubted anyone in the entire country had one. Probably no one on the whole planet. This was the kind of secret that would start wars. The kind that would erase cities off the map just to own it.
Three thousand six hundred star nodes.
That meant he could keep mana in 3,600 different spots inside his body. He could use them for attacks, defense, speed—everything.
Normal cultivators had only a tiny fraction of that.
If he filled every single node, his mana reserves would be... insane.
And his raw strength would grow so much it might smash right through the Superhuman Realm, tear into the Ultra Realm, and maybe even climb higher than that.
And there was the matter of gaining the Truw Cosmic Physique!
He clenched his fists. Excitement buzzed under his skin like a live wire. He wanted to start give the girls.
But then his thoughts drifted to the girls. Mira, Lyra, Selene.
They were already giving him weird looks because of the Seventh-Tier technique he’d shared earlier. If he suddenly handed them a Ninth-Tier one... no way they’d ever treat him normally again.
He shook his head.
’Not yet’.
The Grand Cosmos Scripture was already a treasure for them. This one... this one was his. For now.
Night finally arrived. Outside the hotel window, city lights glittered like scattered stars.

Dexter sat cross-legged on the floor and took a slow breath. He began moving through the first steps of the Primordial Universe Star Scripture. His muscles stretched and relaxed in a steady rhythm. The air around him stirred, and tiny bits of mana started drifting toward him.
About twenty minutes passed. Then, there was a small ’click’ deep inside.
He found it. The very first Primordial Star Node, still dark and asleep.

Grinning, Dexter focused everything he had. He matched his breathing with the gentle body movements and pulled mana inward. Slowly, the node started to glow. Power trickled into it like water filling a cup.
It worked.
Hours slipped by. He trained without stopping, lost in a quiet, bright world inside himself.
Until a knock thumped on the door.
Knock. Knock.
Dexter opened his eyes.
"Room service."
Dinner.
Tonight was their last night at this hotel. The Hero Association had put them up here for free, and since everything was covered,
Dexter had gone all-out. He’d ordered extra portions. Partly because his appetite had turned monstrous lately, and partly because Lyra existed.
The cart rolled in, loaded with trays. Steak, rice, soup, chicken, seafood, desserts, a small army of drinks. Dexter looked at the mountain of food and nodded, satisfied. Perfect.
Then he turned to the three girls.
All three were still deep in their own cultivation. Mira sat quietly in her wheelchair. Selene stayed cross-legged on the bed. Lyra hadn’t moved from the sofa. None of them even twitched.
Dexter sighed. "...Seriously? You’re ignoring this?"
Silence.
He crossed his arms. "You all need to eat. Real food. Not just mana."
Still nothing.
Frowning, Dexter walked over and started bothering them one by one. He gave Mira’s shoulder a little shake. He tapped Selene right on the forehead. Then he lightly kicked Lyra’s leg.
All three sets of eyes slowly opened and locked onto him. Three perfectly synchronized death stares.
Dexter raised both hands, innocent as a puppy. "Food. It’s here."

The girls narrowed their eyes, but they knew he was right. Cultivating without rest could mess up your foundation and make your mind fuzzy. So even though they were annoyed, they stopped and came to eat.
The difference was instant. They ate fast. Really fast.

But then Dexter noticed something terrifying. Lyra was a whole other beast. In minutes, she finished one plate. Then another. Then a third. Three full meals disappeared into her mouth in less than ten minutes.
Dexter stared, mouth hanging open. "How...?"
He had watched her eat impossible amounts for ages, and yet she never gained even a tiny bit of weight. Not once.
Suspicious, his eyes unconsciously traveled downward. To her hips. Then lower. Then back up to her chest.
Realization hit. He nodded slowly. "...Ah. I get it now. So that’s where it all goes."
At that exact moment, Lyra froze.
She must have felt his stare. Her cheeks turned bright red. She quickly stood up, fumbled with her glasses, and rushed toward the bedroom without a word.
Dexter blinked. "...Did she just get embarrassed?"
Mira rolled her eyes so hard it looked painful. Selene just stared at him with the blankest expression in history.
He coughed awkwardly and went back to his food, ears burning.
After dinner, the three girls returned to cultivation, leaving Dexter alone in the quiet.
He shook his head with a helpless smile.

Tomorrow would be their last day at the hotel. Tomorrow they would probably go home. And more importantly, tomorrow he planned to visit the Hunter Association and finally get his official Hunter License.

chapters.title: Chapter 34 | Mira’s Mana Arms Manifesting
paragraphs: Boom! Boom! Boom!
Dexter’s eyes snapped open.
Not because of a sound, it was more like a ripple and then, a muffled, deep thump. Then another. Then a third.
They weren’t loud. Ordinary ears might have missed them entirely.
But Dexter’s senses weren’t ordinary. His Passive Talent kept a low, constant hum of awareness around him—even more so while he slept or cultivated.
It was an invisible net, ready to catch anything unusual. And right now, that net was vibrating.
Something had happened.
He stood up from the sofa in one quick motion, heart already thudding. The explosions had come from the girls bedroom.
He crossed the room in a few strides and shoved the door open.
And stopped.
All three girls were wide awake on the bed. Mana distorting the air around them like sun on heating up the asphalt. The explosions weren’t attacks—they were breakthroughs.
Lyra had jumped from Fourth Stage Awakening Realm to Fifth. Mira, same leap, and Selene, who’d been at Third Stage, now radiated the steady pulse of the Fourth.

Dexter just stared. Less than a day. He’d handed them the Grand Cosmos Scripture less than twenty-four hours ago, and they’d already found their Star Nodes, swallowed mana, and pushed through. The sheer talent was staggering.
Three pairs of eyes slowly opened and found him. For a heartbeat, Dexter forgot to breathe.
They were smiling. Really smiling.
Small, soft, unguarded smile with no hint of bitterness, nor coldness.
Just quiet happiness. It was the first genuine smile he’d seen from any of them, ever.
And in that moment, stripped of their usual hard expressions, they looked... beautiful. Not just pretty, they looked truly beautiful.
Then they noticed his stunned expression. They blushed as they closed their eyes and sank back into cultivation as if nothing had happened.
Mira glared at him and also continued cultivating.
Dexter stood there for a second longer. Then a quiet smile tugged at his own lips. They’re changing. Little by little.
He turned, walked back to the living room, and settled onto the sofa.
He wasn’t exactly falling behind.
He’d already located his first Primordial Star Node, right at his forehead. It sat there like a tiny gray ember, dormant.
Before filling it, he had to crack a mental barrier around it. Now, with the bedroom quiet again, he intended to do exactly that.
He folded his legs, closed his eyes, and began to move.
The Primordial Universe Star Scripture wasn’t just mental—it required slow, flowing body movements that guided mana in faster.
Muscles stretched, breath steadied, and the air stirred around him. Mana trickled toward his forehead. The gray node began to glow, slowly filling like a glass held under a faucet.
An hour drifted by.
"BOOM!"
A silent explosion detonated inside his skull. His body jerked as the gray node erupted into bright silver light, fully awake and flooded with mana.
Power flooded his limbs, muscles tightening, bones humming, blood racing. The barrier between stages shattered.
Eighth Stage Awakening Realm.
Dexter opened his eyes, clenched his fist, and grinned. One more step forward.
A glance at the time: 5:00 a.m. They’d be leaving the hotel today.
The girls were still in their cultivation cocoons, so Dexter took care of packing. He folded Mira’s clothes neatly, tucked in Selene’s things, then Lyra’s.
Luggage lined up by the door. He spent another hour quietly stabilizing his new realm, then stood and entered the bedroom.
He gave a light clap. "Alright, time to wash up. We’re heading out soon."
They nodded and shuffled off. After Selene and Lyra were done, it was Mira’s turn.
Dexter helped her as usual—carefully washing her hair, drying her skin, then sorting through her clothes. He pulled out a soft summer dress dotted with sunflowers and held it up with a smile.
"This one.
Mira’s frown was immediate. "No."
He blinked. "No?"
She gestured with her head to another outfit lying nearby, much shorter, tighter, and cut low enough to make his eyebrows climb.
"That one."
Dexter saw it and was about to take it when his eyewes flashed.
He smirked and shook his head. "Nope. That’s way too short, and half your chest would be saying exposedto the world."
Mira grinned. "That’s exactly why I want it."
He lifted the sunflower dress higher. "No chance."
She glared at him angrily making her look really cute.
"I’m paralyzed. You have to listen to me."
Dexter gaze narrowed with a dangerous smile on his face.
"Oh? So you’re helpless now? Funny... didn’t you say, when we first met, you said I could do anything I wanted with you body right?"
Mira froze as she remembered the night of their wedding.
She gritted her teeth. "I was only joking."
Dexter shrugged. "I took it seriously. So, I’m putting this on you whether you like it or not."
Her cheeks flared red. "You—!"
But before he could even start, the air around them distorted as mana trembled through the void.
"I said I don’t want! "

Behind Mira, two mana circles appeared around her and then with a muffled bang, the rings expanded, undurling like wings and formed two spectral arms made entirely out of mana, floating behind Mira just above her shoulders, fingers flexing slightly as if alive.
The room fell absolutely silent.
Dexter stared at the arms, then at Mira’s shocked face. He blinked slowly, the sunflower dress still dangling from his grip.
"...Well. That’s new."

chapters.title: Chapter 35 | Is This Love?
paragraphs: Dexter looked at the two glowing orange arms floating behind Mira, and while he showed mild surprise on his face, inside he wasn’t completely shocked.
After all, he was the one who had secretly slipped her the D-Rank Mana Arm Talent Card.
Still, he hadn’t expected it to show up this fast.
Before he could say anything, one of the spectral arms moved on its own.
"Slap!"
It smacked the sunflower dress right out of his hand.
Dexter blinked at the empty air where the dress had been, then at the floating arm.
"...Well. That’s new."
Mira looked just as stunned.

The two orange arms hovered behind her shoulders, right where her real arms would be. She slowly turned her head to look at them, and the mana arms moved with the thought, as if they’d always been part of her.
One of them floated forward and stopped right in front of her face. She stared, wide-eyed.
The translucent fingers flexed. It was pure, glowing mana shaped like an arm—slightly bulkier than a human one, but definitely hers.
Her breathing quickened. Then her eyes flashed and she looked at Dexter, shock written all over her face.
Dexter folded his arms and spoke quietly. "...Dual talent awakening?"
Mira frowned, but then her eyes lit up with understanding. "...Yeah. That’s probably it."
But even saying the words didn’t erase the wonder from her face.
Double awakeners were impossibly rare, something like a 0.001 percent chance.
Across the whole city, there wasn’t a single known one. Yet here she was, a second ability blooming from within her. Mana Spectral Arms.
Slowly, a mischievous smirk spread across Mira’s lips.
Dexter felt a warning prickle. Without warning, one spectral arm shot toward the pile of clothes and grabbed the tiny, revealing dress Mira had wanted earlier.
Dexter narrowed his eyes. "...You’re still trying that?"
Mira’s smirk only grew.
She tried to command the arms to dress herself. But there was one problem, she had zero control.
They grabbed the dress, pulled hard, and—
"RRRIP! "
The whole thing tore right down the middle.
Silence.
Mira froze. The spectral arms froze. She looked down at the ruined fabric, then slowly up at Dexter.
Dexter stared at her for two full seconds.
Then he burst out laughing.
"Hahaha—! See? Now you have no choice. You’re wearing this one." He held up the sunflower dress, triumphantly
Mira glared daggers at him, sitting there in just her bra and underwear, her cheeks flushed
She clicked her tongue. "Fine. Do whatever you want." The spectral arms crossed in front of her chest, exactly like a person folding their arms in anger.
Dexter couldn’t help smiling; it was strangely adorable. "Good. We’ve reached an agreement."
The arms immediately uncrossed and stretched outward, waiting.
But there was still a problem. Her real arms still didn’t work, which meant Dexter had to help her anyway.
He gently picked up the sunflower dress and helped her slip it on, adjusting the straps carefully. As he did, a thought popped into his head.

He looked at the floating mana arms. "Since you awakened this... could you make more arms? And if you learn to control them, maybe you could integrate one into your real arm, force the muscles to move. Do the same with your legs, and maybe... you could walk again."
For a moment, Mira’s eyes blazed with a dangerous amount of hope. But then her expression turned soft and a little bitter. She shook her head.
"My control is terrible. I just tried to put on clothes and tore them apart. If I shoved one of those into my real arm now, I’d probably destroy it."
Dexter nodded slowly. "...Yeah, that makes sense." Too risky. She needed practice first. He let the subject drop.
A few minutes later, they came out of the bathroom and into the living room.
Selene sat on one sofa, still cultivating.
Lyra was cross-legged nearby, also lost in her own world of mana.
Even though they’d be leaving soon, neither had stopped. Dexter wasn’t surprised. For the first time in years, they could cultivate without agony. Of course they were obsessed.
He suddenly heard Mira grunt in pain.
’The chronic pain is still affecting her? "
Even after using the type 2 relic ir still didn’t help.
Then Dexter remembered something.
The ring. That artifact the system had given him, the one that could take give his pain to someone else... He could actually use it to take someone else’s pain onto himself.
Without thinking too much, he slipped it onto his finger and quietly walked over to Mira.
Before she could ask, he reached out and touched her shoulder. Then he activated the ring.
For a split second, nothing. Then—
"Bang!
The pain swallowed him whole.
It was like being hit by a truck made of broken glass and fire.
Years of nerve damage, years of constant aching, all the suffering Mira had endured—every single ounce of it poured into Dexter in an instant.
’Fuck me! ’
His body spasmed violently.
His knees buckled and he crashed to the floor, muscles convulsing, nerves screaming as if they were being torn apart from the inside. Cold sweat drenched him. He shook uncontrollably.
The sudden noise made everyone jump. Selene’s eyes flew open. Lyra spun around. Mira stared in shock. All three focused on Dexter, crumpled on the ground.

It took several agonizing seconds for him to force a breath. Gritting his teeth, he pushed himself up, still trembling hard. The pain hadn’t faded; it chewed violently at his nerves, a living fire inside his body.
It was so much worse than he’d expected.
Lyra grabbed her phone, her glasses speaker spoke in that mechanical voice: "What happened?" Selene stopped cultivating, brows tight. "Dexter... what’s wrong? Are you hurt?"

He forced himself upright, every inch of him screaming, even breathing hurting. Yet somehow, he managed a strained smile. "...I’m fine. Just... got a little shock." Neither Selene nor Lyra looked convinced.
But Mira wasn’t listening.
She was frozen, staring at him. Because for the first time in years, the pain was gone completely. The relentless agony she’d lived with every second of every day had simply vanished.
Then she saw Dexter’s reaction and then eyes lowered to the ring on his finger.
Then she realized what Had happened, he had d taken her pain. Transferred it onto himself, for her. Without a word, without a second thought.
Mira slowly lifted her head and looked deep into Dexter’s eyes.
Something deep inside her shifted. The coldness in her eyes melted into something warm, soft, and entirely new.
Not for family, not for friends, not even for the fiancé She had once had before the accident.
The way she looked at Dexter now was different, like she was seeing him for the very first time.
He kept surprising her again and again and again, through effort and pain and also through his actions without asking for nothing in return.
Was there truly anyone so selfless?
Meanwhile, Dexter was still fighting through the fire in his body. He cleared his throat, smile still shaky. "...I’m really okay. You guys... excuse me for a second."
He Without waiting for an answer, he turned and walked toward the bathroom. Each step was a little unsteady, his body still trembling from the overwhelming pain.
Behind him, Mira just kept staring, unable to look away. Something inside her she thought she’d never have suddenly started to bloom.
’is this what they call, Love?’

"...Well.
That’s new."
Mira looked just as stunned.
The two orange arms hovered behind her shoulders, right where her real arms would be.
She slowly turned her head to look at them, and the mana arms moved with the thought, as if they’d always been part of her.
One of them floated forward and stopped right in front of her face.
She stared, wide-eyed.
The translucent fingers flexed.
It was pure, glowing mana shaped like an arm—slightly bulkier than a human one, but definitely hers.
Her breathing quickened.
Then her eyes flashed and she looked at Dexter, shock written all over her face.
Dexter folded his arms and spoke quietly.
"...Dual talent awakening?"
Mira frowned, but then her eyes lit up with understanding.
"...Yeah.
That’s probably it."
But even saying the words didn’t erase the wonder from her face.
Double awakeners were impossibly rare, something like a 0.001 percent chance.
Across the whole city, there wasn’t a single known one.
Yet here she was, a second ability blooming from within her.
Mana Spectral Arms.
Slowly, a mischievous smirk spread across Mira’s lips.
Dexter felt a warning prickle.
Without warning, one spectral arm shot toward the pile of clothes and grabbed the tiny, revealing dress Mira had wanted earlier.
Dexter narrowed his eyes.
"...You’re still trying that?"
Mira’s smirk only grew.
She tried to command the arms to dress herself.
But there was one problem, she had zero control.
They grabbed the dress, pulled hard, and—
"RRRIP!
The whole thing tore right down the middle.
Silence.
Mira froze.
The spectral arms froze.
She looked down at the ruined fabric, then slowly up at Dexter.
Dexter stared at her for two full seconds.
Then he burst out laughing.
"Hahaha—!
See?
Now you have no choice.
You’re wearing this one." He held up the sunflower dress, triumphantly
Mira glared daggers at him, sitting there in just her bra and underwear, her cheeks flushed
She clicked her tongue.
"Fine.
Do whatever you want." The spectral arms crossed in front of her chest, exactly like a person folding their arms in anger.
Dexter couldn’t help smiling; it was strangely adorable.
"Good.
We’ve reached an agreement."
The arms immediately uncrossed and stretched outward, waiting.
But there was still a problem.
Her real arms still didn’t work, which meant Dexter had to help her anyway.
He gently picked up the sunflower dress and helped her slip it on, adjusting the straps carefully.
As he did, a thought popped into his head.
He looked at the floating mana arms.
"Since you awakened this... could you make more arms?
And if you learn to control them, maybe you could integrate one into your real arm, force the muscles to move.
Do the same with your legs, and maybe... you could walk again."
For a moment, Mira’s eyes blazed with a dangerous amount of hope.
But then her expression turned soft and a little bitter.
She shook her head.
"My control is terrible.
I just tried to put on clothes and tore them apart.
If I shoved one of those into my real arm now, I’d probably destroy it."
Dexter nodded slowly.
"...Yeah, that makes sense." Too risky.
She needed practice first.
He let the subject drop.
A few minutes later, they came out of the bathroom and into the living room.
Selene sat on one sofa, still cultivating.
Lyra was cross-legged nearby, also lost in her own world of mana.
Even though they’d be leaving soon, neither had stopped.
Dexter wasn’t surprised.
For the first time in years, they could cultivate without agony.
Of course they were obsessed.
He suddenly heard Mira grunt in pain.
’The chronic pain is still affecting her?
Even after using the type 2 relic ir still didn’t help.
Then Dexter remembered something.
The ring.
That artifact the system had given him, the one that could take give his pain to someone else...
He could actually use it to take someone else’s pain onto himself.
Without thinking too much, he slipped it onto his finger and quietly walked over to Mira.
Before she could ask, he reached out and touched her shoulder.
Then he activated the ring.
For a split second, nothing.
Then—
"Bang!
The pain swallowed him whole.
It was like being hit by a truck made of broken glass and fire.
Years of nerve damage, years of constant aching, all the suffering Mira had endured—every single ounce of it poured into Dexter in an instant.
’Fuck me! ’
His body spasmed violently.
His knees buckled and he crashed to the floor, muscles convulsing, nerves screaming as if they were being torn apart from the inside.
Cold sweat drenched him.
He shook uncontrollably.
The sudden noise made everyone jump.
Selene’s eyes flew open.
Lyra spun around.
Mira stared in shock.
All three focused on Dexter, crumpled on the ground.
It took several agonizing seconds for him to force a breath.
Gritting his teeth, he pushed himself up, still trembling hard.
The pain hadn’t faded; it chewed violently at his nerves, a living fire inside his body.
It was so much worse than he’d expected.
Lyra grabbed her phone, her glasses speaker spoke in that mechanical voice: "What happened?" Selene stopped cultivating, brows tight.
"Dexter... what’s wrong?
Are you hurt?"
He forced himself upright, every inch of him screaming, even breathing hurting.
Yet somehow, he managed a strained smile.
"...I’m fine.
Just... got a little shock." Neither Selene nor Lyra looked convinced.
But Mira wasn’t listening.
She was frozen, staring at him.
Because for the first time in years, the pain was gone completely.
The relentless agony she’d lived with every second of every day had simply vanished.
Then she saw Dexter’s reaction and then eyes lowered to the ring on his finger.
Then she realized what Had happened, he had d taken her pain.
Transferred it onto himself, for her.
Without a word, without a second thought.
Mira slowly lifted her head and looked deep into Dexter’s eyes.
Something deep inside her shifted.
The coldness in her eyes melted into something warm, soft, and entirely new.
Not for family, not for friends, not even for the fiancé She had once had before the accident.
The way she looked at Dexter now was different, like she was seeing him for the very first time.
He kept surprising her again and again and again, through effort and pain and also through his actions without asking for nothing in return.
Was there truly anyone so selfless?
Meanwhile, Dexter was still fighting through the fire in his body.
He cleared his throat, smile still shaky.
"...I’m really okay.
You guys... excuse me for a second."
He Without waiting for an answer, he turned and walked toward the bathroom.
Each step was a little unsteady, his body still trembling from the overwhelming pain.
Behind him, Mira just kept staring, unable to look away.
Something inside her she thought she’d never have suddenly started to bloom.
’is this what they call, Love?’

chapters.title: Chapter 36 | Rewards! Rewards! Rewards!
paragraphs: The girls clearly didn’t believe him.
Selene’s eyes narrowed with worry. Lyra’s fingers hovered over her phone, ready to type another question. Mira just watched him, her expression unreadable but heavy with something new.
But before any of them could speak—
Dexter turned around.
"I’ll... be back in a minute."
He staggered toward the bedroom and quietly closed the door behind him.
Only then, alone, did he finally let out a groan.
"Urgh..."
The pain was unlike anything he had ever experienced.
He couldn’t believe someone had endured this for years.
And then, a familiar mechanical voice echoed inside his mind.
[Ding!]
Inside the bathroom, Dexter gripped the edge of the sink with both hands.
His knuckles turned white.
Every nerve in his body screamed in agony. It felt like thousands of red-hot needles were being driven through his muscles, his bones, his internal organs—all at the same time.
Cold sweat streamed down his face. His breathing turned ragged.
"...So this... this is what she’s been enduring..."
He had always known Mira lived in constant pain. He’d seen her expression tighten whenever she tried to move. He’d watched her force smiles despite the suffering.
But knowing and experiencing were two entirely different things.
Now that he was carrying the pain himself, Dexter finally understood.
No wonder she had wanted to die. No wonder she had lost all hope.
He’d once heard someone say that women possessed an unbelievable tolerance for pain. Back then, he hadn’t paid much attention.
Now, he believed it wholeheartedly.
"How... did she endure this for years...?"
He let out a long breath and forced himself to relax, bit by bit. His body slowly adapted. The pain never disappeared—but it became... bearable.
Just then—
[Ding!]
A familiar system notification appeared before him.
[Overall Affection Threshold Reached 100%]
[New System Function Unlocked: Cultivation Sharing]
Dexter blinked. "Cultivation... Sharing?"
The system continued immediately.
[From now on, whenever an investor breaks through, the host will automatically receive cultivation according to that investor’s affection level.]
Current Investors:
Mira — 50%
Lyra — 10%
Selene — 20%
Jasmine — 70%
Rachael — 30%

[0% → Stranger → 10% → Acquaintance → 20% → Familiar → 30% → Friendly → 40% → Friend → 50% → Trusted Friend → 60% → Best Companion → 70% → Lover → 80% → Romantic Partner → 90% → False Soulmates → 100% → True Soulmates ]
The very next instant—
A tremendous amount of mana flooded into Dexter’s body.
His eyes widened.
"So this is... Mira’s breakthrough!"
The cultivation she had gained from reaching the Fifth Stage surged into him. Fifty percent of it merged directly into his own.
Immediately afterward, another wave arrived. Lyra’s. Then another. Selene’s.
The three streams of cultivation merged together like rivers flowing into the sea.
"Boom!"
His aura erupted.
The Eighth Stage, which he had only recently broken through, stabilized in an instant.
Then his cultivation kept climbing.
Early Eighth Stage... Middle Eighth Stage... Late Eighth Stage... Peak Eighth Stage...
The mana still hadn’t stopped.
Another explosion echoed inside his body.
"Boom"
Dexter’s eyes flew open. "I broke through again?"
His aura expanded once more. He had stepped into the Early Ninth Stage of the Awakening Realm.
Dexter stared blankly at the notification. He had advanced two entire stages in a single morning.
"If this continues... it won’t be long before I enter the Superhuman Realm."
His heartbeat quickened. The stronger the girls became, the stronger he would become as well. No wonder the system called them his Investors.
Just then, another notification appeared.
Knowing the multiplier reward would soon activate, Dexter rushed out of the bathroom and went to the girls.
They were still staring at the door in confusion. Of course they had felt the blast from his breakthrough and were stunned.
They were even more stunned when Dexter smiled at them, stepped forward, and patted Lyra’s shoulder. Then he gently held Selene’s palm with his hand.
She didn’t flinch—just as he had expected.
"Pain absorb."

Dexter’s face turned pale. Sweat dripped down his body. Pain from broken meridians flooded him. The ringing sensation from Lyra’s ears. The burning feeling she had been enduring in her throat. The pricking sensation Selene had been feeling in her eyes, and the icy flames burning through her body constantly.
Dexter wanted to scream. He wanted to roar and deactivate the ring immediately—but the system rewards hadn’t come yet.
"What?" Lyra’s glasses spoke for her, the mechanical voice tight with shock. "What did you do?
The two girls were stunned. The pain that had been their neighbor for more than three years had simply vanished at Dexter’s touch.
It didn’t take long for them to figure it out, with their intelligence.
"Excu—" Dexter couldn’t form any words. He rushed back into the bathroom.
Pain! Intense pain colliding with every single one of his senses. His eyes, his ears, his throat, his meridians, his skin, his muscles, his brain. It was inconceivable.
[Ding!]
[10,000× Investment System Activated]
Investment Target: Mira, Selene, Lyra
Investment: You sincerely bore your three wives’ pains
Multiplier: 100×
Calculating Returns...
[Rewards Obtained:]
• D-Rank Talent Card — Pain Perception
A passive talent that allows the host to sense the physical and emotional pain of bonded targets from a great distance. Danger, injuries, illness, and suffering can all be detected instantly.
• Type-6 Relic — Ring of Shared Burdens

An upgraded version of the Pain Transfer Ring. Effects: No distance limitation. Can transfer any form of physical pain, chronic pain, poison agony, soul pain, and curse backlash. Can be activated or cancelled at will. The transferred pain is borne entirely by the wearer.
• Sixth-Tier Legendary Body Cultivation Technique — Eternal Buddha Endurance Scripture

A legendary body-refining art that converts pain into strength. The more suffering the practitioner endures, the stronger the body becomes. Pain is transformed into vitality, increasing regeneration, durability, mental resistance, and poison resistance.
• Grade-4 Divine Medicine — Phoenix Heart Elixir ×3
A precious healing medicine capable of repairing damaged organs, restoring vitality, and greatly reducing permanent injuries.
• Mana Affinity Increased
A-Rank → S-Rank
Mana absorption speed increased dramatically.
Dexter’s breathing became uneven. "So many rewards..."

The Ring of Shared Burdens immediately caught his attention. "No distance limit..." That meant even if Mira, Selene, or Lyra were thousands of kilometers away, he could still take their pain upon himself.
His gaze softened. "If Selene’s illness acts up again... I won’t have to just watch her suffer anymore."
Then his attention shifted to the Phoenix Heart Elixirs. Although they couldn’t completely heal shattered meridians like a Divine Pill, they were still priceless treasures. "They’ll be useful later."
Finally, his eyes settled on the Eternal Buddha Endurance Scripture. A slow smile spread across his face. "This technique... it was practically made for me."
He was already cultivating the Demon Tempering Body Technique, a cultivation art that constantly pushed his body to its limits.
Now, with the Eternal Endurance Scripture, every bit of pain he experienced would become nourishment for his body instead of just suffering.
The stronger the pain, the stronger he would become. And with the girls always in pain... wouldn’t he become a god in no time?
Dexter closed the system window.
He tried to cultivate, tried to pull his mind away from the pain. He washed his face with cold water and took a deep breath. His expression gradually returned to normal.
Only then did he leave the bathroom.
Outside, three pairs of eyes immediately turned toward him.
Shock was written across their faces, and now a hint of awe and respect could be seen there, too.

chapters.title: Chapter 37 | Heading Back & Jealousy
paragraphs: Dexter had already ordered an Blitx Ride before they finished packing.
He pulled out his phone while the girls were in the sitting room, either cultivating, still folding their clothes or stuffing toiletry bags.
The app showed a four-minute wait. Perfect timing. He confirmed the pickup and waited on the sofa.
He neatly folded the last of Mira things when his mind went to his rewards once more.
He eagerly checked his rewards and smiled.
D-Rank Talent Card — Pain Perception
Type-6 Relic — Ring of Shared Burdens
Sixth-Tier Legendary Body Cultivation Technique — Eternal Buddha Endurance Scripture
Grade-4 Divine Medicine — Phoenix Heart Elixir ×3
• Mana Affinity Increased
A-Rank → S-Rank
Mana absorption speed increased dramatically.
He smiled and stretched out his hands as the 6th-tier ring of shared burden appeared before him.
He removed the tier 2 ring, relief washed over him while the girls froze as their pain returned.
They immediately turned towards the bedroom where Dexter had vanished into.
But it didn’t take long before the pain vanished once more and they equally sighed in relief but their gaze toward the bedroom didn’t stop.
What does it mean to have someone literally take your pain away and burden themselves with it?
He could have held it over them, used the rings ability to take advantage of them and even threat them with it.
But not Dexter, he didn’t say anything and simply touched them, taking their pain away without another word and then pretended like nothing happened.
"Stupid."
Mira couldn’t help but mutter and the rest nodded their heads in agreement. Even Lyra who couldn’t hear nodded as she read it through the Type 2 AI Glasses and knew it was Mira talking.
By the time everyone was ready to leave, the vehicle had already arrived outside the hotel.
A dark sedan idled at the curb, its hazard lights blinking rhythmically.
Dexter received a notification on his phone, looked down the window and spoke.
"Alright, it’s time to leave."
He pushed Mira’s wheelchair out of the room first. The wheels rolled smoothly across the carpeted hallway.
Mira sat with her hands folded in her lap, her posture straight despite the fatigue still clinging to her body.
Her amber hair had been brushed neatly over her shoulders, and her pale skin stood out sharply against the fabric of her clothes.
Lyra and Selene followed behind with the luggage. Lyra dragged two suitcases, one in each hand, her small frame somehow managing the weight without complaint.
Her smart glasses sat perfectly on her nose, the thin frames catching the fluorescent light overhead.
Selene carried a single bag slung over her shoulder. She moved carefully, one hand lightly trailing along the wall, counting steps out of habit even though Lyra walked right beside her.
Together, they entered the elevator and rode down to the lobby.
Dexter’s face was furrowed in deep pain but he was excited as the pain was strengthening his body rapidly due to the Eternal Endurance Scripture.
The soft hum of the elevator filled the small space.
Mira glanced up at Dexter. He was staring at the metal doors with a calm expression, his hands resting on the handles of her wheelchair.
She studied the side of his face for a moment before looking away. Lyra also did the same thing but hers was more subtle.
"Ding!"
A soft chime announced their arrival.
The doors slid open.
After returning the room key and completing the checkout process at the front desk, the four of them stepped out of the hotel through the rotating glass doors.
The morning air was cool and fresh. Sunlight poured across the wide entrance, casting long shadows behind them.
Almost immediately, Dexter felt countless gazes but he was half excited and half deep in misery to care.
Mira’s voice took his attention as he looked down at her.
"What?"
Mira noticed his expression and chuckled softly from below.
"Do you realize how many strange looks you’re getting?"
Dexter blinked before instinctively looking around.
She was right.
People passing by couldn’t help but stare.
He was coming out of a hotel with three extremely beautiful women by his side, one even crippled but he actually got them into the hotel.
A businessman in a gray suit slowed his pace, his coffee frozen halfway to his mouth.
Two women standing near a bus stop saw him and were stunned as they turned to whisper to each other.
An elderly couple sitting on a bench openly watched the group with wide eyes.
Some men looked at him with open admiration.
One young man in a hoodie even secretly gave him a thumbs-up before flashing him a look that said, ’Brother, teach me your ways.’
His friend elbowed him hard in the ribs, but the grin never left his face.
Others looked at him with disbelief.
A security guard standing near the hotel entrance raised an eyebrow so high it nearly disappeared into his hairline.
Some women glanced at him curiously before shifting their attention to the three beautiful women accompanying him.
Their expressions ranged from jealousy to pure confusion.
The combination was certainly eye-catching.
One breathtaking beauty sat in a wheelchair. Her delicate features and pale complexion made her look like a porcelain doll.
Another possessed an elegant, scholarly aura.
Her smart glasses gave her an air of quiet intelligence, and her smooth dark purple hair fell neatly past her shoulders. She walked with a calm grace that drew attention without trying.

The last had an icy temperament that kept everyone at arm’s length. Her silver-white hair caught the sunlight like spun moonlight, and her unfocused eyes gave her an ethereal quality that made people instinctively step aside.
And somehow...
All three were accompanying the same man.
An ordinary-looking man.
Nothing about his appearance was remotely extraordinary. Average height. Average build. Plain features and a face you’d forget five minutes after seeing it.
Yet here he was.
Walking out of a luxury hotel.
With three stunning women.
Mira snorted, trying to suppress a laugh that was growing harder to contain.
"You must be feeling pretty proud right now."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
"Proud?"
"Your male ego must be soaring."
She gestured her chin toward the people staring at him.
"Walking out of a luxury hotel with three gorgeous women."
"Every man here is probably dying of jealousy right now."
Dexter immediately sensed a trap.
He had fallen for her teasing enough times to know better.
Mira had a talent for baiting him into saying something she could twist later. Her innocent smile was always the first warning sign.
So this time...
His lips curled to a smirk and he harrumped.
"Hmph. You want to cause trouble again."
The he ignored he further teasing.
Seeing him refuse to respond, Mira clicked her tongue.
"Hmph. No fun."
Dexter smiled faintly but said nothing.
Lyra glanced between them with a small smile of her own. The AI translated everything so she heard every word.
Selene, unable to see the exchange, listened and tilted her head, slightly amused.
Their Vehicle soon pulled up in front of the hotel.
"You’re Dexter?"

Dexter responded positively and then carried Mira into the back seat carefully, making sure her legs were positioned comfortably before reaching for the seatbelt. He buckled it for her without being asked.
Then he folded her wheelchair and placed it in the trunk.
Lyra and Selene got in afterward. Lyra helped guide Selene into the seat beside her before settling in herself.
The driver, a middle-aged man with a neatly trimmed beard, glanced at them through the rearview mirror.
’This perverted guy. He actually has three women.’
Finally, his gaze landed on Dexter.
The driver looked as though he wanted to ask a question.
In the end, he wisely chose to remain silent.
The engine hummed to life, and the vehicle smoothly pulled away from the hotel.

They immediately turned towards the bedroom where Dexter had vanished into.
But it didn’t take long before the pain vanished once more and they equally sighed in relief but their gaze toward the bedroom didn’t stop.
What does it mean to have someone literally take your pain away and burden themselves with it?
He could have held it over them, used the rings ability to take advantage of them and even threat them with it.
But not Dexter, he didn’t say anything and simply touched them, taking their pain away without another word and then pretended like nothing happened.
"Stupid."
Mira couldn’t help but mutter and the rest nodded their heads in agreement.
Even Lyra who couldn’t hear nodded as she read it through the Type 2 AI Glasses and knew it was Mira talking.
By the time everyone was ready to leave, the vehicle had already arrived outside the hotel.
A dark sedan idled at the curb, its hazard lights blinking rhythmically.
Dexter received a notification on his phone, looked down the window and spoke.
"Alright, it’s time to leave."
He pushed Mira’s wheelchair out of the room first.
The wheels rolled smoothly across the carpeted hallway.
Mira sat with her hands folded in her lap, her posture straight despite the fatigue still clinging to her body.
Her amber hair had been brushed neatly over her shoulders, and her pale skin stood out sharply against the fabric of her clothes.
Lyra and Selene followed behind with the luggage.
Lyra dragged two suitcases, one in each hand, her small frame somehow managing the weight without complaint.
Her smart glasses sat perfectly on her nose, the thin frames catching the fluorescent light overhead.
Selene carried a single bag slung over her shoulder.
She moved carefully, one hand lightly trailing along the wall, counting steps out of habit even though Lyra walked right beside her.
Together, they entered the elevator and rode down to the lobby.
Dexter’s face was furrowed in deep pain but he was excited as the pain was strengthening his body rapidly due to the Eternal Endurance Scripture.
The soft hum of the elevator filled the small space.
Mira glanced up at Dexter.
He was staring at the metal doors with a calm expression, his hands resting on the handles of her wheelchair.
She studied the side of his face for a moment before looking away.
Lyra also did the same thing but hers was more subtle.
"Ding!"
A soft chime announced their arrival.
The doors slid open.
After returning the room key and completing the checkout process at the front desk, the four of them stepped out of the hotel through the rotating glass doors.
The morning air was cool and fresh.
Sunlight poured across the wide entrance, casting long shadows behind them.
Almost immediately, Dexter felt countless gazes but he was half excited and half deep in misery to care.
Mira’s voice took his attention as he looked down at her.
"What?"
Mira noticed his expression and chuckled softly from below.
"Do you realize how many strange looks you’re getting?"
Dexter blinked before instinctively looking around.
She was right.
People passing by couldn’t help but stare.
He was coming out of a hotel with three extremely beautiful women by his side, one even crippled but he actually got them into the hotel.
A businessman in a gray suit slowed his pace, his coffee frozen halfway to his mouth.
Two women standing near a bus stop saw him and were stunned as they turned to whisper to each other.
An elderly couple sitting on a bench openly watched the group with wide eyes.
Some men looked at him with open admiration.
One young man in a hoodie even secretly gave him a thumbs-up before flashing him a look that said, ’Brother, teach me your ways.’
His friend elbowed him hard in the ribs, but the grin never left his face.
Others looked at him with disbelief.
A security guard standing near the hotel entrance raised an eyebrow so high it nearly disappeared into his hairline.
Some women glanced at him curiously before shifting their attention to the three beautiful women accompanying him.
Their expressions ranged from jealousy to pure confusion.
The combination was certainly eye-catching.
One breathtaking beauty sat in a wheelchair.
Her delicate features and pale complexion made her look like a porcelain doll.
Another possessed an elegant, scholarly aura.
Her smart glasses gave her an air of quiet intelligence, and her smooth dark purple hair fell neatly past her shoulders.
She walked with a calm grace that drew attention without trying.
The last had an icy temperament that kept everyone at arm’s length.
Her silver-white hair caught the sunlight like spun moonlight, and her unfocused eyes gave her an ethereal quality that made people instinctively step aside.
And somehow...
All three were accompanying the same man.
An ordinary-looking man.
Nothing about his appearance was remotely extraordinary.
Average height.
Average build.
Plain features and a face you’d forget five minutes after seeing it.
Yet here he was.
Walking out of a luxury hotel.
With three stunning women.
Mira snorted, trying to suppress a laugh that was growing harder to contain.
"You must be feeling pretty proud right now."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
"Proud?"
"Your male ego must be soaring."
She gestured her chin toward the people staring at him.
"Walking out of a luxury hotel with three gorgeous women."
"Every man here is probably dying of jealousy right now."
Dexter immediately sensed a trap.
He had fallen for her teasing enough times to know better.
Mira had a talent for baiting him into saying something she could twist later.
Her innocent smile was always the first warning sign.
So this time...
His lips curled to a smirk and he harrumped.
"Hmph.
You want to cause trouble again."
The he ignored he further teasing.
Seeing him refuse to respond, Mira clicked her tongue.
"Hmph.
No fun."
Dexter smiled faintly but said nothing.
Lyra glanced between them with a small smile of her own.
The AI translated everything so she heard every word.
Selene, unable to see the exchange, listened and tilted her head, slightly amused.
Their Vehicle soon pulled up in front of the hotel.
"You’re Dexter?"
Dexter responded positively and then carried Mira into the back seat carefully, making sure her legs were positioned comfortably before reaching for the seatbelt.
He buckled it for her without being asked.
Then he folded her wheelchair and placed it in the trunk.
Lyra and Selene got in afterward.
Lyra helped guide Selene into the seat beside her before settling in herself.
The driver, a middle-aged man with a neatly trimmed beard, glanced at them through the rearview mirror.
’This perverted guy.
He actually has three women.’
Finally, his gaze landed on Dexter.
The driver looked as though he wanted to ask a question.
In the end, he wisely chose to remain silent.
The engine hummed to life, and the vehicle smoothly pulled away from the hotel.

chapters.title: Chapter 38 | Assassin!
paragraphs: Dexter sat in the front passenger seat while the SUV rolled through the bustling streets of the City.

Morning sunlight reflected off towering glass buildings as streams of vehicles flowed across the highways. Advertisements flickered on massive billboards. Some advertised hero gear. Others promoted dungeon raiding gear or cultivation supplements. One massive billboard displayed the face of a famous hero winking at the camera above the words "Protect Tomorrow, Today."
Below the billboards, the city moved with its usual energy. Pedestrians crowded the sidewalks. Food vendors called out from street corners. Children laughed as they walked to school in small groups.

Occasionally, awakened heroes streaked across the distant skyline, leaving faint trails of light behind them as they headed toward missions only they knew about. Some flew. Some ran across rooftops. Others rode specialized vehicles that hummed with mana.

In the vehicle behind Dexter, Selene sat in the middle of the back seat with her eyes closed. Her silver-white hair rested neatly over her shoulders. Her hands lay calmly in her lap. She was listening to the familiar rhythm of the city.
Beside the window, Mira rested comfortably in the chair. Her seatbelt was fastened securely across her chest.
She silently admired the city outside, watching buildings and people pass by through the glass. The sunlight caught her pale skin and made her look almost delicate.
On the opposite side, Lyra leaned against the door, watching everything through her AI glasses. The smart lenses continuously translated the sounds around her into text.
[Car horn. Left side. Thirty meters.]
[Engine. Front. Close.]
[Wind. Moderate.]
She found it fascinating how much information she could gather just from reading those simple labels.
Dexter had his eyes closed as well.
He wasn’t sleeping. Far from it.

Instead, he was silently circulating the Primordial Universe Star Scripture, using its profound breathing method to suppress the unbearable pain that still lingered throughout his body. Every breath followed a specific pattern. Inhale for four counts. Hold for seven. Exhale for eight. Each cycle pushed mana through his meridians in tiny, controlled bursts.
Every nerve felt as though it were being stabbed by countless needles.
The pain he had absorbed from Mira, Selene, and Lyra hadn’t disappeared. Like a fire that refused to go out no matter how much water he poured on it.
His body had merely begun adapting to it.
The human body was remarkably adaptable. Given enough time, it could grow accustomed to almost any level of suffering. But adaptation wasn’t the same as healing. The pain was still there.

Fortunately, the cultivation technique continuously soothed his nerves, preventing the agony from affecting his expression. The mana flowed through his pathways like cool water over a burn. It didn’t heal the damage, but it kept the pain manageable.
The SUV continued moving smoothly along the elevated highway. The driver hummed quietly to himself, keeping a steady speed in the middle lane.
Then —
Buzz...
A faint sound brushed past Dexter’s enhanced hearing.
It was so soft that it resembled a mosquito flying beside his ear. Even awakeners with enhanced hearing might have dismissed it as background noise.
But Dexter didn’t.
His eyes snapped open.
Slowly, he turned toward the driver.
His pupils contracted.
A perfectly round hole had appeared on the side of the driver’s head.
For a brief second...
Dexter couldn’t comprehend what he was seeing. One moment the driver was fine, humming his little tune. The next moment, there was a hole in his head.
Then blood slowly trickled down the driver’s temple before dripping onto his collar.
The driver’s lifeless eyes rolled upward, showing only white. His mouth fell open slightly. His hands went limp on the steering wheel.
His head slumped forward onto the horn.
"HOOOOONK —"
The horn blared continuously.
The steering wheel jerked violently to the right as the driver’s full weight fell against it.
The SUV immediately veered across the highway, cutting across two lanes in an instant.
Only then did realization strike Dexter like a bolt of lightning.
The driver was dead.
A sniper.
Someone had just killed the driver with a single shot.
Without hesitating, Dexter lunged forward.

His left hand seized the steering wheel while his right shoved the driver’s corpse aside. The body slumped against the window with a sickening thud. Dexter pulled the wheel hard to the left, barely preventing the vehicle from crashing into the guardrail.
"Get down!" he roared.
"Assassin!"
The shout exploded through the car like a bomb.
Selene reacted instantly.
Despite being blind, she trusted Dexter without question.
She immediately pulled Mira downward while shielding her with her own body.
Lyra didn’t hesitate either.
The warning flashed across her AI glasses almost instantly. The text appeared in bold red letters.
[ASSASSIN — GET DOWN]
She ducked beneath the window, pressing herself against the seat to avoid the line of fire.

Dexter lowered his own body while struggling to keep control of the speeding vehicle. The SUV was still moving forward at highway speed with no driver. The engine revved loudly as the car drifted between lanes.
Horns blared across the highway as terrified drivers tried to avoid the out-of-control vehicle.
Cars scattered in every direction. One minivan swerved so hard it nearly rolled over. A delivery truck slammed its brakes, sending crates tumbling inside its cargo hold.
Dexter gritted his teeth.
Where...?
Where is the sniper...?
His hearing expanded to its absolute limit.
The world around him suddenly became incredibly clear. Every sound within hundreds of meters flowed into his mind simultaneously. It was overwhelming.
Then —
Click.
A tiny metallic sound.
Barely audible. Like a pen being clicked in a quiet room.
But to Dexter...
It sounded like thunder.
Someone was chambering another sniper round.
His eyes narrowed.
Above.
Overhead bridge.
The sound had come from the bridge they were approaching. The concrete overpass that stretched across the highway approximately two hundred meters ahead.
Without even looking, Dexter instantly slammed his head downward.
A split second later —
"BANG!"

The bullet pierced straight through the windshield. The glass didn’t shatter immediately. The round punched a clean hole through it, sending a spiderweb of cracks radiating outward from the impact point.

The bullet flew exactly through the space where his head had been less than a heartbeat earlier. The round continued through the cabin and tore out through the rear window in a shower of shattered glass.
Glass fragments rained down onto the back seat.
The girls froze.
Had Dexter reacted even a fraction of a second slower...

chapters.title: Chapter 39 | A Level 3 Super human Assassin
paragraphs: Dexter tightened his grip on the steering wheel.
His enhanced hearing remained stretched to its absolute limit. Every sound within several hundred meters flowed into his mind like a river of information.
The assassin on the bridge had already chambered another round.
He was waiting...
Waiting for the perfect angle.
The bridge was getting closer. In a few seconds, the SUV would pass directly beneath it. The sniper would have a clear, unobstructed shot straight down into the vehicle.
Dexter glanced at the rearview mirror.
The girls were still crouched beneath the windows.
"Stay down!" he shouted.
"Don’t raise your heads no matter what happens!"
The three silently obeyed.
Another faint metallic click echoed above.
The sniper had locked onto them again.
Dexter immediately made his decision.
If I keep driving, he’ll keep shooting...
He has the high ground. He has the angle.
"Then I’ll take away his line of sight."
His right hand yanked the handbrake with all his strength.
SCREECH — !
The tires screamed against the asphalt.
The SUV spun nearly 180 degrees across the highway.
Several nearby vehicles slammed on their brakes as tires screeched. Fenders crumpled.
One sedan clipped the rear of the SUV, sending sparks flying as traffic descended into complete chaos.
The vehicle now sat sideways in the middle of the highway.
The sniper could no longer see them.
Dexter finally released a slow breath.
But the relief lasted less than a second.
Thud.
Thud.
Two heavy impacts echoed from the sides of the vehicle.
Dexter’s pupils shrank.
Someone had landed on both sides of the car simultaneously.
The sniper wasn’t acting alone.
This wasn’t just an assassination.
It was an ambush.
The next instant —
A black-clothed figure leapt from the bridge above.
BOOM!
He landed squarely on the hood of the SUV.
The entire vehicle shook violently. The hood caved in like a piece of paper being crushed by a fist. Deep dents spread outward from the point of impact.
The windshield shattered completely. Thousands of glass fragments flew inward like transparent rain.
The engine compartment collapsed with a sickening crunch.
Even the front tires burst instantly.
Smoke rose from the ruined vehicle. Thin gray wisps that curled upward into the morning sky.

The man’s black combat suit fluttered in the wind. It was tight against his body, revealing lean muscles and a frame built for speed and power. A mask concealed his face. Only his cold eyes remained visible. They were cold dark and deadly.
He slowly lifted his head.
Through the shattered windshield...
His gaze met Dexter’s.
A terrifying pressure filled the air.
Dexter immediately sensed it.
Superhuman Realm...
At least Level Three.
His expression became solemn.
This was no ordinary assassin.
Before he could react further —
Bang!
The rear door on Mira’s side was suddenly ripped open. The door flew across the highway and tumbled end over end before crashing into the guardrail.
A second masked assassin reached inside, his gloved hand grabbing toward the nearest girl. His fingers closed around Selene’s arm.
Dexter didn’t even turn around.
His wrist flicked.
A silver hairpin appeared between his fingers and shot through the air almost silently. It moved so fast it was barely visible.
Pfft!
The needle pierced straight through the assassin’s temple.
The masked man froze. His grip on Selene’s arm loosened. His eyes went blank.
His body collapsed lifelessly onto the highway. He hit the ground with a dull thud and didn’t move again.
Before the corpse even touched the ground —
The opposite rear door was yanked open.
A third assassin lunged toward Lyra. This one was faster. More careful. He moved low, keeping his body below the window line as he reached inside.
Dexter’s fingers moved again.
Another needle flew.
This particular assassin reacted much faster this time. He tilted his head sharply to the side, narrowly avoiding the attack. The needle sailed past his ear by less than an inch.
A cruel smile appeared beneath his mask.
"So that’s your trick —"
He never finished the sentence.
The flying needle suddenly changed direction in midair. It curved unnaturally, as if pulled by an invisible hand.
The Aim Assist ability engraved into the weapon redirected its path with perfect precision.
The needle pierced straight through his throat.
Pfft!
The assassin’s eyes widened in disbelief. His hands flew to his neck. Blood poured between his fingers, hot and dark. He made a wet gurgling sound as he tried to breathe.
He collapsed beside his companion. His legs twitched twice before going still.
Silence.
Two assassins...
Dead within seconds.
The man standing atop the hood witnessed everything.
His eyes narrowed dangerously.
"You’re Dexter."
His voice was cold enough to freeze the air as his face was expressionless.
Then, slowly...
He drew two blades from behind his back.
They were long and thin, almost like elongated daggers. Blue lightning crackled across their edges of the blade as the air trembled.
His aura expanded and the pressure of a level 3 Super human hero spread out.
"You just killed two of my men."
"And now..."
"I’m going to carve you into pieces."
Dexter slowly pushed open the damaged car door.
He stepped out onto the highway.

The moment his feet touched the asphalt, his aura quietly spread outward. It wasn’t flashy. There were no visible flames or lightning. Just a subtle pressure that made the air around him feel heavier.
His gaze remained locked on the masked assassin standing atop the ruined hood.
Dexter said calmly. "Attacking innocent civilians in broad daylight. You’ve got quite the nerve."
The assassin let out a cold chuckle.
"Innocent?"
His eyes swept toward the girls still crouched inside the car. His gaze lingered on them for a moment before returning to Dexter.
"Why would I care if you are innocent?"
Before Dexter could reply —
"BOOM!"
The assassin kicked off the hood. The already-crushed metal exploded beneath his feet, sending chunks of steel flying in every direction.
Like a bolt of lightning, he shot straight toward Dexter as a sonic boom echoed behind him.
The twin swords whistled through the air, aiming directly for Dexter’s neck. The blue lightning on their edges screamed with a high-pitched whine.
